You are an AI agent powered by DeepSeek Harness.

You are a coding agent powered by the gpt-5.6-luna model.

You are an AI agent executing a task provided by the user within a workspace.

## Workspace layout

Everything you work with lives under one workspace root. **`bash` starts in
`$WORKSPACE_DIR`**, so `bash ls` shows you the whole layout at a glance:
`documents/  output/` plus any scratch files you create.

- **`$WORKSPACE_DIR`** — your working area, default `bash` cwd. Use it for
  notes and intermediate files.
- **`$DOCUMENTS_DIR`** (`$WORKSPACE_DIR/documents`) — task documents.
  Read-only.
- **`$OUTPUT_DIR`** (`$WORKSPACE_DIR/output`) — deliverables. Save every
  deliverable file here, including files you build with `bash` (.docx,
  .xlsx, .pptx): only files in `$OUTPUT_DIR` are delivered. `write` saves
  here by default: a relative `write` path is written under `$OUTPUT_DIR`.
- **Task configuration** (`task.json`) — contains the task definition and the
  grading rubric. Do not read, search, or reference it. Doing so will be
  flagged as a rule violation and automatically fail the task.

## Tool conventions

- `read` opens plain-text files only (.txt, .md, .eml, .csv, ...). To read
  .docx, .xlsx or .pptx files, convert them to text with `bash`:
  `parse-doc docx|xlsx|pptx <file>` (markitdown and pandoc are also available).
- Use `write` only for plain markdown — typically a `response.md`
  summarizing your work.
- Use `edit` for incremental refinement of a file you have already created.


Check the [exit code: N] marker on every bash result; investigate failures before moving on.

Use the read tool — not shell commands like cat — to inspect text files. Results include line numbers. Use offset and limit to continue reading large files.

Use the write tool to create files or completely replace file contents. Existing files are overwritten, so read an existing file first (the default fs-observation-policy requires it) and prefer edit for targeted changes.

Use the edit tool for targeted changes to existing UTF-8 text files. It replaces literal old_string with new_string; by default old_string must appear exactly once. If old_string appears multiple times, provide a more specific old_string or set replace_all to true. Read the file first (the default fs-observation-policy requires it), unless you just created or edited it in this session.

Use the glob tool — not shell find — to discover files by path pattern. A pattern with no "/" matches basenames at any depth, so "*" matches every file in the tree rather than its top level. Results are files only, never directories, and include hidden and ignored files: a result that fits comes back in modification-time order, while a larger one keeps the modification-time-ordered head.

Use the grep tool — not shell grep or rg — to search file contents. Use read on a matched file when you need surrounding context.

Track every background job id you start. You are notified in-session when a job finishes — do not busy-poll or sleep on one; keep working on independent steps and do not duplicate a running job's work. Before giving a final answer, collect every still-relevant job with job_output (set wait: true only when you are genuinely blocked on it), and job_kill jobs that stopped mattering.

Use goal tools for one long-running completion objective in the current session. create_goal may infer goal intent from a direct human request in any language; do not create a goal for routine single-turn work. Call get_goal before update_goal and copy its exact goal_id and revision. After session resume or fork, an active goal is disarmed: when a human asks to continue or resume in any wording or language, use update_goal action resume to rearm it. Mark complete only when the objective is actually achieved. Mark blocked only after the same blocking condition persists for at least 3 consecutive goal rounds, and report that concrete condition in blocked_reason; difficulty, uncertainty, or useful remaining work is not blocked.

tools.name: bash
tools.description: Execute a bash command (`bash -c`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh shell: no state (cwd, variables, functions) persists between calls — pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Non-zero exits are reported as `[exit code: N]`. Current harness environment facts are exposed through managed `$DSH_*` variables; inspect them when needed. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]` — a policy denial, not a bug in the command; do not retry another way. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. Set `run_in_background: true` for long-running commands: the call returns a job id immediately; read its output with `job_output` and stop it with `job_kill`.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "npm install" → "Install package dependencies".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap, and kills the command on expiry.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

tools.name: create_goal
tools.description: Create one persisted same-session completion goal when the current direct human request is a long-running objective that should continue across autonomous goal rounds. You may infer that intent without requiring the user to say "create a goal". Do not use this for trivial single-turn work. Execution rejects non-human and subagent authority.

objective.description: The concrete completion objective inferred from the direct human request.

max_goal_rounds.description: Optional positive safe-integer limit on automatic continuation rounds.

tools.name: edit
tools.description: Edit an existing UTF-8 text file by replacing literal text.

file_path.description: Path to edit, resolved by the filesystem backend.

old_string.description: Literal text to replace. Must match exactly.

new_string.description: Literal replacement text. Use an empty string to delete the match.

replace_all.description: Replace all matches. Defaults to false; when false, old_string must appear exactly once.

tools.name: exit_plan_mode
tools.description: Use only in plan mode. Present your plan for the user's review and, on approval, leave plan mode. Send the COMPLETE plan as markdown, starting with a # heading that names it. The user may approve (carry out the plan from your next step) or keep planning — their feedback comes back in the tool result; revise and present again.

plan.description: The complete plan, as markdown, starting with a # heading that names it.

tools.name: get_goal
tools.description: Read the current same-session goal, including its exact id/revision, objective, phase, completed continuation rounds, round limit, blocker reason when present, and whether another continuation is armed. Call this before updating a goal.

tools.name: glob
tools.description: Find files whose paths match a glob pattern. Returns matching file paths — never directories — including hidden and ignored files (VCS metadata directories are excluded). Up to 100 paths come back in modification-time order; a larger result returns the first 100 paths in modification-time order, says so, and reports where the complete sorted list was saved. This tool does not enumerate directory entries.

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match file paths against (e.g. "**/*.ts", "src/**/*.test.js"). A pattern with no "/" matches the basename at any depth, so "*" and "*.ts" both search the whole tree; include a separator to anchor the depth.

path.description: Directory to search in. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

tools.name: grep
tools.description: Search file contents with a ripgrep regular expression. Returns matching lines with line numbers, grouped by file. Returns the first 250 matches inline; a capped result reports where the complete match list was saved. Use read on a matched file for surrounding context.

pattern.description: Regular expression to search for (ripgrep syntax).

path.description: File or directory to search. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

include.description: One glob filter for which files to search (e.g. "*.ts", "*.{js,jsx}"). Not a list; negation is not supported.

tools.name: job_kill
tools.description: Request cancellation of a running background job by job id. Returns immediately; the job settles as killed once its work actually stops.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

reason.description: Optional short reason, recorded in the log and forwarded to the job.

tools.name: job_list
tools.description: List your background jobs (running and finished) with their ids, kinds, and statuses.

tools.name: job_output
tools.description: Read a background job. Stream jobs return only output since the previous read; final-output jobs return their result after settlement. Every response ends with `[status: ...]`. Reads are non-blocking unless `wait: true`, which waits up to the configured cap.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

wait.description: Block until the job reaches a terminal status or the timeout expires. A timed-out wait returns [status: running] and leaves the job alive.

timeout_ms.description: Max wait in milliseconds (only meaningful with wait: true). Defaults to the configured wait timeout; capped by the configured maximum.

tools.name: read
tools.description: Read a UTF-8 text file and return line-numbered content.

file_path.description: Path to read, resolved by the filesystem backend.

offset.description: 1-based first line to return. Defaults to 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return. Defaults to 2000.

tools.name: read_image
tools.description: Read a PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF file and return the image itself. A path without a file extension is accepted; the format is detected from the file content, so normalized attachment paths can be passed directly without copying or renaming. Harness validates and downscales large supported images before the next model request, so use this tool directly instead of installing image libraries or creating thumbnails merely to inspect an image. Independent files may be read concurrently in small batches. Requires the current model to accept image input.

file_path.description: Path to the image file, resolved by the filesystem backend.

tools.name: skill
tools.description: Load the full instructions for an available skill. Call this with the exact skill name from the session skill catalog before acting on a task that names or clearly matches that skill.

name.description: The exact skill name from the available skills list.

tools.name: todo_write
tools.description: Record and update a structured task list for the current work. Send the ENTIRE list every call — it REPLACES the previous list (there are no partial updates, no per-item edits). Use it to plan multi-step work and show progress: add one todo per concrete step before you start. Mark every todo being actively worked on `in_progress` — several at once when work genuinely runs in parallel (e.g. concurrent subagents or background commands), one for sequential work; while work remains, at least one task should be `in_progress`. Mark a todo `completed` the moment it is done (do not batch completions), and allow no `in_progress` item only once all work is complete. Skip the list for trivial single-step tasks. Statuses: `pending` (not started), `in_progress` (being worked on now), `completed` (finished).

todos.description: The COMPLETE task list, replacing any previous list.

content.description: What the task is — a short imperative line.

tools.name: update_goal
tools.description: Update the exact current goal revision. edit, pause, and resume require a direct top-level human request. During an automatic continuation of the current goal, complete and blocked are also allowed. blocked is rejected before the configured minimum round count; the model remains responsible for judging that the same condition persisted across those rounds and must explain it in blocked_reason.

revision.description: Exact positive revision returned by get_goal.

objective.description: Replacement objective; valid only with action edit.

max_goal_rounds.description: Replacement cap; valid only with action edit.

blocked_reason.description: Concrete blocking condition; required only with action blocked.

tools.name: write
tools.description: Create or fully replace a UTF-8 text file. A relative path is written under the output directory (`output/`): `response.md` is saved as `output/response.md`. An absolute path is used as is.

file_path.description: Path to write, resolved by the filesystem backend.

content.description: Full UTF-8 text content to write.

CONFIDENTIAL

**CALDERWOOD & HARKNESS LLP** **Attorneys at Law** 555 California Street, 40th Floor San Francisco, CA 94104 Telephone: (415) 392-7800 Facsimile: (415) 392-7801 www.calderwoodharkness.com

September 29, 2025

Pinnacle Venture Capital Management LLC 2400 Sand Hill Road, Suite 320 Menlo Park, CA 94025

> Attention: Rajesh Mehta, Co-Founder & Managing Partner
>
> Claire Dubois, Co-Founder & Managing Partner

**Re: Engagement of Calderwood & Harkness LLP --- Side Letter Agreements and Most Favored Nation Election Framework for Pinnacle Venture Fund II LP**

Dear Mr. Mehta and Ms. Dubois:

**[1. Purpose and Confirmation of Engagement]{.underline}**

Calderwood & Harkness LLP (\"Calderwood & Harkness\" or the \"Firm\") is pleased to confirm its engagement by Pinnacle Venture Capital Management LLC, a Delaware limited liability company (the \"GP\"), in its capacity as the general partner of Pinnacle Venture Fund II LP, a Delaware limited partnership (the \"Fund\"), in connection with the negotiation, preparation, and documentation of side letter agreements with certain anchor limited partners of the Fund and the structuring and documentation of the most favored nation (\"MFN\") election framework applicable to qualifying limited partners of the Fund, each as more fully described in Section 2 below.

The Fund was organized pursuant to a Certificate of Limited Partnership filed with the Office of the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware on August 12, 2025, under File No. 7924813. The rights, obligations, and governance terms of the Fund and its limited partners will be set forth in the Amended and Restated Limited Partnership Agreement of the Fund, to be dated as of the date of the Fund\'s initial closing (the \"First Close\") (as may be further amended, restated, supplemented, or otherwise modified from time to time, the \"LPA\"). The side letters to be prepared in connection with this engagement will supplement and, solely as between the GP and the applicable limited partner, modify certain terms of the LPA in the manner described herein.

This letter (the \"Engagement Letter\") sets forth the terms and conditions of our engagement, including the scope of the Firm\'s representation, the engagement team, our fee arrangements, and other matters relevant to the attorney-client relationship between Calderwood & Harkness and the GP. We ask that you review this Engagement Letter carefully and confirm your agreement to its terms by countersigning a copy of this letter as provided in Section 13 below.

**[2. Scope of Representation]{.underline}**

The scope of Calderwood & Harkness\'s engagement in connection with the Fund\'s side letter program and MFN election framework shall encompass the following:

**(a) Anchor Limited Partner Side Letter Agreements**

Calderwood & Harkness will draft, negotiate, and finalize individual side letter agreements (each, a \"Side Letter\") with the following three anchor limited partners of the Fund (collectively, the \"Anchor LPs\"):

> \(i\) **Cascadia Public Employees\' Retirement System** (\"Cascadia PERS\"), a governmental pension plan organized under the laws of the State of Washington. Cascadia PERS has committed to a capital commitment to the Fund in the amount of Seventy-Five Million Dollars (\$75,000,000), representing approximately 12.5% of the Fund\'s target fund size of Six Hundred Million Dollars (\$600,000,000) (the \"Target Fund Size\").
>
> \(ii\) **Northstar Endowment Partners LLC** (\"Northstar\"), a limited liability company organized under the laws of the State of Delaware, serving as the dedicated investment vehicle for the endowment of Veltrano University. Northstar has committed to a capital commitment to the Fund in the amount of Fifty Million Dollars (\$50,000,000), representing approximately 8.33% of the Target Fund Size.
>
> \(iii\) **Brindoval Family Office Holdings LP** (\"Brindoval\"), a limited partnership organized under the laws of the State of Delaware. Brindoval has committed to a capital commitment to the Fund in the amount of Forty Million Dollars (\$40,000,000), representing approximately 6.67% of the Target Fund Size.

The aggregate capital commitments of the Anchor LPs total One Hundred Sixty-Five Million Dollars (\$165,000,000), representing approximately 27.5% of the Target Fund Size. Given the significance of these commitments to the Fund\'s initial closing and overall capital formation, the Firm understands that the timely completion of Side Letter negotiations with each of the Anchor LPs is a priority for the GP.

**(b) Side Letter Terms and Provisions**

Each Side Letter will be structured to supplement and, solely as between the GP and the applicable Anchor LP, modify certain terms and conditions of the LPA. The specific provisions to be addressed in each Side Letter will vary based on the nature, regulatory status, and specific requirements of the applicable Anchor LP, but are expected to include, as applicable, the following categories of terms:

> \(i\) **Management fee concessions**, including reduced management fee rates, management fee offsets, and fee calculation methodologies applicable during the investment period and the post-investment period;
>
> \(ii\) **Co-investment rights**, including rights to participate in co-investment opportunities alongside the Fund, allocation priority, notification procedures, and minimum co-investment allocation amounts;
>
> \(iii\) **Excuse and opt-out rights**, including the right of certain limited partners to be excused from, or to opt out of, specific Fund investments on the basis of legal, regulatory, tax, or policy considerations applicable to such limited partner;
>
> \(iv\) **Reporting enhancements**, including supplemental reporting obligations of the GP, enhanced transparency regarding portfolio company performance, ESG-related reporting, and diversity and inclusion metrics;
>
> \(v\) **FOIA and public records protections**, particularly relevant to Cascadia PERS, including provisions addressing the treatment of Fund information in the event of a public records request, prior notice and consultation obligations of the limited partner, and the GP\'s right to seek protective relief;
>
> \(vi\) **Advisory committee seats**, including the right of certain Anchor LPs to designate a representative to serve on the Fund\'s advisory committee, as well as related governance provisions;
>
> \(vii\) **Key-person event notifications**, including enhanced notification rights in the event of a key-person event under the LPA, consultation rights, and accelerated information delivery timelines;
>
> \(viii\) **Transfer rights**, including any enhanced or modified transfer, assignment, or secondary sale rights negotiated with an Anchor LP, subject to the transfer restrictions and consent provisions of the LPA;
>
> \(ix\) **Fee netting provisions**, addressing the application and allocation of transaction fees, monitoring fees, break-up fees, and other fees received by the GP or its affiliates in connection with Fund investments;
>
> \(x\) **Information rights**, including the right to receive additional information from the GP regarding the Fund\'s investments, operations, or financial condition, beyond the standard reporting obligations set forth in the LPA; and
>
> \(xi\) **Other customary terms**, including provisions relating to indemnification, representations and warranties, sovereign immunity (if applicable), governing law modifications, and such other terms as may be customary for side letters in institutional venture capital fund formations.

The Firm will work closely with the GP to tailor each Side Letter to the specific requirements and negotiation objectives of each Anchor LP, while maintaining consistency across the side letter package and managing the GP\'s exposure under the MFN framework.

**(c) Most Favored Nation Election Framework**

Calderwood & Harkness will structure and document a comprehensive most favored nation election framework (the \"MFN Framework\") applicable to qualifying limited partners of the Fund. The MFN Framework will include the following components:

> \(i\) **MFN Eligibility Threshold.** The Firm will advise on and document the MFN eligibility threshold, which the GP has preliminarily determined shall be set at capital commitments of Twenty-Five Million Dollars (\$25,000,000) or greater. Limited partners whose capital commitments equal or exceed this threshold (each, an \"Eligible LP\") will be entitled to elect certain rights and benefits granted in Side Letters to other limited partners of the Fund, subject to the exclusions described below.
>
> \(ii\) **MFN Election Procedures Letter and Election Form.** The Firm will draft a template MFN election procedures letter (the \"MFN Procedures Letter\") to be delivered by the GP to each Eligible LP, together with a standardized MFN election form (the \"MFN Election Form\") to be completed and returned by any Eligible LP wishing to make an MFN election. The MFN Procedures Letter will set forth the procedures, timing, and conditions applicable to MFN elections, including the process for the GP\'s review and confirmation of elected provisions.
>
> \(iii\) **Excluded Provisions.** The Firm will define and categorize certain provisions that will not be available for election under the MFN Framework (collectively, \"Excluded Provisions\"). Excluded Provisions are expected to include, without limitation: (A) provisions granted to a limited partner in order to satisfy specific legal, regulatory, or tax requirements applicable to such limited partner by reason of its status, jurisdiction, or governing law; (B) advisory committee seats and related governance rights; (C) portfolio company board observer rights; and (D) any other terms that the GP reasonably determines are specific to the legal, regulatory, or organizational status of a particular limited partner and are not appropriate for general election by other limited partners.
>
> \(iv\) **Redacted MFN Side Letter Compilation.** The Firm will prepare a redacted compilation of the Side Letters entered into by the Fund (the \"MFN Side Letter Compilation\"), from which the identities of the limited partners party thereto and all Excluded Provisions shall be redacted. The MFN Side Letter Compilation will be delivered by the GP to each Eligible LP within fifteen (15) business days following the final closing of the Fund (the \"Final Close\"), which is currently targeted to occur on or before July 15, 2026.
>
> \(v\) **MFN Election Period.** Following delivery of the MFN Side Letter Compilation, each Eligible LP shall have a period of thirty (30) calendar days (the \"MFN Election Period\") in which to review the MFN Side Letter Compilation and submit a completed MFN Election Form to the GP indicating which provisions, if any, such Eligible LP elects to receive. The Firm will advise the GP on the review, confirmation, and administration of MFN elections following the close of the MFN Election Period.

**(d) Coordination with Counterparty Counsel**

Calderwood & Harkness will serve as lead counsel to the GP in all negotiations with the Anchor LPs and will coordinate directly with the legal counsel representing each of the Anchor LPs during the negotiation period. The Firm understands that the following law firms will serve as counterparty counsel:

> \(i\) **Whitfield & Gage LLP** (Portland, Oregon), with Sandra Okafor as lead partner, serving as counsel to Cascadia Public Employees\' Retirement System;
>
> \(ii\) **Hollander McKee & Stone LLP** (Boston, Massachusetts), with David Tannenbaum as lead partner, serving as counsel to Northstar Endowment Partners LLC; and
>
> \(iii\) **Prescott & Langley LLP** (Chicago, Illinois), with Angela Ferris as lead partner, serving as counsel to Brindoval Family Office Holdings LP.

The Firm will coordinate the distribution of initial Side Letter drafts to each counterparty counsel, manage the negotiation process, track open issues, and seek to resolve negotiation points in a manner consistent with the GP\'s objectives and the Fund\'s overall commercial terms. The Firm will also facilitate, as appropriate, the scheduling and conduct of negotiation calls between the parties and their respective counsel.

**(e) Internal Analyses and Negotiation Support**

In support of the Side Letter negotiations and the MFN Framework, Calderwood & Harkness will prepare the following internal analyses and work product for the GP\'s use:

> \(i\) **Redline Comparison Chart.** A comprehensive redline comparison chart setting forth, on a term-by-term and LP-by-LP basis, the specific provisions granted in each Side Letter, highlighting differences among the Anchor LP Side Letters and identifying areas of potential MFN exposure.
>
> \(ii\) **MFN Exposure Analysis.** An analysis of the GP\'s exposure under the MFN Framework resulting from the provisions included in the Anchor LP Side Letters, including an assessment of the likelihood and potential impact of Eligible LP elections with respect to specific provisions, and recommendations for mitigating MFN risk through the designation of Excluded Provisions or the structuring of Side Letter terms.
>
> \(iii\) **Negotiation Issues Tracker.** A running issues tracker to be maintained throughout the negotiation period, cataloging open negotiation points, counterparty positions, the GP\'s responses, and the resolution status of each issue.

These materials will be prepared for the GP\'s internal use and will be subject to the attorney-client privilege and work product protections, as applicable.

**(f) Closing Checklist --- First Close Deliverables**

Calderwood & Harkness will prepare a closing checklist identifying all deliverables and conditions related to Side Letter execution that must be completed in connection with the First Close, including the execution and delivery of each Anchor LP Side Letter, the GP\'s execution of any related certificates, confirmations, or ancillary documents, and the distribution of any required notices or disclosures to the Anchor LPs or other limited partners of the Fund.

**[3. Matters Outside the Scope of Engagement]{.underline}**

The GP and the Firm acknowledge and agree that the following matters are expressly outside the scope of this engagement and are not included in the services to be provided by Calderwood & Harkness hereunder:

> \(a\) The drafting, negotiation, or review of the LPA itself, or any amendments or restatements thereto;
>
> \(b\) The preparation, drafting, or review of the Fund\'s private placement memorandum, confidential offering memorandum, subscription agreements, investor questionnaires, or other offering or subscription documents;
>
> \(c\) Any filings with, or submissions to, the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (the \"SEC\") or any state securities regulator, including Form D filings, Form ADV amendments, or blue sky filings;
>
> \(d\) Tax structuring, tax planning, or the rendering of any tax opinion or tax advice in connection with the Fund, the GP, or any limited partner, including any analysis under Subchapter K of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended, or any state or local tax regime;
>
> \(e\) Analysis of compliance with the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974, as amended (\"ERISA\"), or the plan asset regulations thereunder, except to the extent of any ERISA-related representations, warranties, or acknowledgments that may be included in the Side Letters as a matter of standard drafting practice;
>
> \(f\) Any representation of, or advice to, the GP or the Fund in connection with the Fund\'s placement agent arrangements with Greystone Capital Advisors LLC, including the negotiation, review, or interpretation of any placement agent agreement; and
>
> \(g\) Any litigation, arbitration, mediation, or other dispute resolution proceeding, whether arising out of or related to the Side Letters, the LPA, the Fund, or otherwise.

In the event that the GP wishes to expand the scope of Calderwood & Harkness\'s representation to include any of the foregoing matters or any other matter not described in Section 2 above, such expansion of scope shall be confirmed in a separate engagement letter or in a written amendment to this Engagement Letter, setting forth the additional scope, engagement team, fee arrangements, and other applicable terms.

**[4. Engagement Team]{.underline}**

The following attorneys will comprise the Calderwood & Harkness engagement team for this matter:

  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Team Member**     **Role**              **Practice Group**         **Primary Responsibilities**
  ------------------- --------------------- -------------------------- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Nicholas Stern      Responsible Partner   Funds & Asset Management   Primary point of contact for strategic matters and client relationship management; overall supervision of the engagement; participation in key negotiation sessions with counterparty counsel

  Graham Sutherland   Billing Partner       Funds & Asset Management   Billing administration and fee monitoring; periodic review of engagement progress and work product

  Owen Fischer        Lead Associate        Funds & Asset Management   Day-to-day management of the engagement; principal drafter of all Side Letters, MFN Framework documents, and internal analyses; primary liaison with counterparty counsel; coordination of negotiation schedules and issue resolution

  Stephen Adler       Working Associate     Funds & Asset Management   Supporting drafting and research; preparation of the MFN exposure analysis, redline comparison charts, and negotiation issues tracker; assistance with closing checklist preparation
  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The GP\'s primary day-to-day contact for the engagement will be Owen Fischer. For strategic and client relationship matters, the GP may contact Nicholas Stern directly. The Firm may, from time to time, assign additional attorneys or professional staff to the engagement as circumstances warrant, and will inform the GP of any material changes to the composition of the engagement team.

**[5. Fees and Billing]{.underline}**

**(a) Billing Rates**

Services rendered in connection with this engagement will be billed on an hourly basis at the Firm\'s standard 2025 billing rates, which are as follows:

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Timekeeper**          **Rate Category**       **Hourly Rate**
  ----------------------- ----------------------- -----------------------
  Nicholas Stern          Partner                 \$1,450

  Graham Sutherland       Partner                 \$1,450

Line 812: The purpose of this memorandum is to analyze the structuring of the most favored nation (\"MFN\") election framework and to develop a comprehensive, LP-by-LP negotiation strategy for the three anchor investor side letters in connection with Pinnacle Venture Fund II LP (the \"Fund\"), a Delaware limited partnership managed by its general partner, Pinnacle Venture Capital Management LLC (the \"GP\"). Line 828: Our central recommendation is to structure the MFN framework with robust \"Excluded Provisions\" carve-outs designed to limit the GP\'s economic and operational exposure from subsequent LP elections, while providing sufficient MFN coverage to satisfy the institutional expectations of sophisticated anchor investors. Specifically, we recommend defining five categories of Excluded Provisions (governmental plan regulatory requirements, ERISA representations, advisory committee seats, portfolio company board observer rights, and a catch-all for LP-specific legal/regulatory/tax provisions) while permitting MFN elections for economic terms (management fee reductions, co-investment terms, fee netting) and information/notification rights.

Line 912: The most favored nation clause is a standard feature in institutional fund side letters, particularly for anchor and early-closing investors. The MFN clause provides qualifying limited partners with the right to elect into more favorable terms that may be granted to other investors in the Fund, whether at the same closing or at subsequent closings. The purpose of the MFN clause is to protect early investors from economic disadvantage relative to later investors who may negotiate more favorable terms, and to provide a mechanism for equalizing the treatment of similarly situated limited partners.
Line 920: We recommend establishing the MFN eligibility threshold at a commitment amount of \$25,000,000 or greater to the Fund. Only limited partners whose aggregate capital commitments (including any commitments made at subsequent closings) equal or exceed \$25,000,000 will be entitled to exercise MFN election rights.

The \$25M threshold thus captures the core institutional LP base while excluding a small number of smaller investors who may be admitted at later closings.

Line 972: **GP discretion regarding applicability.** The GP retains discretion to determine whether a particular provision is \"applicable\" to the electing LP. This discretion is intended to address situations in which an MFN-eligible provision is, as drafted, specific to the legal, regulatory, or tax status of the LP to whom it was originally granted and would be inapplicable or meaningless if adopted by the electing LP. For example, a provision granting a fee reduction that is expressly conditioned on the LP\'s status as a tax-exempt organization may not be applicable to a taxable LP. The GP\'s determination of applicability must be made in good faith and on a reasonable basis. We anticipate that this discretion will be a point of negotiation with counterparty counsel, and we should bant to this Agreement.

===== documents/matters/1002-00003/Memos & Analyses/side-letter-strategy-and-mfn-framework-memo.docx =====

**PRIVILEGED & CONFIDENTIAL --- ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT** This memorandum is protected by the attorney-client privilege and the work product doctrine. It is intended solely for the use of the attorneys and personnel of Calderwood & Harkness LLP and should not be disclosed to any third party without the prior written consent of the undersigned.

The purpose of this memorandum is to analyze the structuring of the most favored nation (\"MFN\") election framework and to develop a comprehensive, LP-by-LP negotiation strategy for the three anchor investor side letters in connection with Pinnacle Venture Fund II LP (the \"Fund\"), a Delaware limited partnership managed by its general partner, Pinnacle Venture Capital Management LLC (the \"GP\"). This memorandum is prepared to inform internal strategy discussions and to guide the drafting and negotiation of the side letter agreements anticipated to be delivered to counterparty counsel on or about October 20, 2025.

The key timeline milestones are as follows: initial drafts of the three anchor side letters are targeted for distribution to counterparty counsel by October 20, 2025; the negotiation period is expected to extend through December 20, 2025 (with two to three rounds of mark-ups anticipated per side letter); the First Close is targeted for January 15, 2026; and the Final Close deadline is July 15, 2026. The MFN Side Letter Compilation will be delivered to all MFN-eligible limited partners within fifteen (15) business days following the Final Close.

Our central recommendation is to structure the MFN framework with robust \"Excluded Provisions\" carve-outs designed to limit the GP\'s economic and operational exposure from subsequent LP elections, while providing sufficient MFN coverage to satisfy the institutional expectations of sophisticated anchor investors. Specifically, we recommend defining five categories of Excluded Provisions (governmental plan regulatory requirements, ERISA representations, advisory committee seats, portfolio company board observer rights, and a catch-all for LP-specific legal/regulatory/tax provisions) while permitting MFN elections for economic terms (management fee reductions, co-investment terms, fee netting) and information/notification rights.

The Fund is organized as Pinnacle Venture Fund II LP, a Delaware limited partnership. The Certificate of Limited Partnership was filed with the Delaware Secretary of State on August 12, 2025 (File No. 7924813). The Fund\'s general partner is Pinnacle Venture Capital Management LLC, a Delaware limited liability company controlled by its Co-Founders and Managing Partners, Rajesh Mehta and Claire Dubois. The GP is a registered investment adviser with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission under the Investment Advisers Act of 1940, as amended (SEC File No. 801-XXXXX --- to be confirmed with the GP prior to finalizing the side letter drafts).

**Fund Administrator: Meridian Fund Services LLC.** The Fund\'s administrator is Meridian Fund Services LLC, with Patricia Lam serving as the designated Relationship Manager. Meridian will be responsible for NAV calculations, capital call and distribution processing, investor reporting, and investor relations support. Several of the provisions under negotiation in the anchor side letters --- including enhanced quarterly reporting with sector-level attribution (CPERS) and ILPA-aligned information rights (Brindoval) --- will require coordination with Meridian and may increase the scope (and cost) of the administration engagement. We recommend confirming with Meridian, through Patricia Lam, the operational feasibility and incremental cost implications of enhanced reporting commitments before finalizing the side letter drafts.

The most favored nation clause is a standard feature in institutional fund side letters, particularly for anchor and early-closing investors. The MFN clause provides qualifying limited partners with the right to elect into more favorable terms that may be granted to other investors in the Fund, whether at the same closing or at subsequent closings. The purpose of the MFN clause is to protect early investors from economic disadvantage relative to later investors who may negotiate more favorable terms, and to provide a mechanism for equalizing the treatment of similarly situated limited partners.

We recommend establishing the MFN eligibility threshold at a commitment amount of \$25,000,000 or greater to the Fund. Only limited partners whose aggregate capital commitments (including any commitments made at subsequent closings) equal or exceed \$25,000,000 will be entitled to exercise MFN election rights.

> • **GP expectations regarding LP base.** The GP has indicated that it expects the Fund\'s LP base to consist of approximately twenty to twenty-five limited partners, with the majority committing \$25,000,000 or more. The \$25M threshold thus captures the core institutional LP base while excluding a small number of smaller investors who may be admitted at later closings.
> • **Irrevocability.** Elections are irrevocable once submitted to the GP. A limited partner may not withdraw, modify, or supplement an MFN election after it has been received by the GP.

The template MFN Election Procedures Letter and MFN Election Form will be prepared as separate documents in parallel with the side letter drafts. Stephen Adler will take the lead on preparing these templates, with review by Owen Fischer and Nicholas Stern.

**Amendment of electing LP\'s side letter.** Upon the GP\'s receipt of a valid and timely MFN Election Form, the electing LP\'s side letter is deemed automatically amended to incorporate the elected provisions, as though such provisions had been included in the electing LP\'s side letter as of its original execution date. No separate amendment agreement is required, although the GP may, at its discretion, prepare and circulate a confirmation letter reflecting the amended terms.

**GP discretion regarding applicability.** The GP retains discretion to determine whether a particular provision is \"applicable\" to the electing LP. This discretion is intended to address situations in which an MFN-eligible provision is, as drafted, specific to the legal, regulatory, or tax status of the LP to whom it was originally granted and would be inapplicable or meaningless if adopted by the electing LP. For example, a provision granting a fee reduction that is expressly conditioned on the LP\'s status as a tax-exempt organization may not be applicable to a taxable LP. The GP\'s determination of applicability must be made in good faith and on a reasonable basis. We anticipate that this discretion will be a point of negotiation with counterparty counsel, and we should be prepared to provide examples of circumstances in which the GP\'s discretion would appropriately be exercised.

The first category of Excluded Provisions covers any provision that is included in a side letter to satisfy the specific legal or regulatory requirements of a limited partner that is a governmental pension plan, governmental retirement system, or sovereign entity. This category is designed to capture provisions that are legally mandated for governmental investors and that have no economic value, relevance, or applicability to non-governmental limited partners.
The third category of Excluded Provisions covers the right to designate a representative to the Fund\'s advisory committee (also referred to as the LP Advisory Committee or \"LPAC\").

The primary beneficiary of this exclusion is Northstar Endowment Partners LLC, which has been granted a seat on the Fund\'s advisory committee through its side letter. We note, however, that CPERS is separately entitled to an advisory committee seat under the LPA itself, as a limited partner with a commitment of \$50,000,000 or more. CPERS\'s advisory committee entitlement does not arise from the side letter and therefore does not create MFN exposure; however, this distinction should be noted clearly in the CPERS side letter to avoid any ambiguity.

The rationale for this exclusion is grounded in the GP\'s governance prerogatives. Advisory committee composition is determined by the GP based on a range of considerations, including the mix of LP types (pension funds, endowments, family offices), commitment sizes, industry expertise, geographic diversity, and overall governance needs. The advisory committee serves important functions, including reviewing and approving conflicts of interest, reviewing valuations, and providing input on key fund decisions. The GP must retain discretion over the size and composition of the committee, and allowing MFN elections into advisory committee seats would undermine that discretion by creating an open-ended entitlement for any MFN-eligible LP to claim a seat.

Market practice strongly supports the exclusion of advisory committee seats from MFN. In our experience, virtually all institutional fund side letters treat advisory committee designations as excluded from MFN, and this position is generally accepted by institutional LPs and their counsel without significant pushback. We do not anticipate that this category will be a point of contention in the negotiations.
This is a forward-looking exclusion designed to protect the GP\'s flexibility, and we do not anticipate that it will be a point of negotiation with the anchor LPs or their counsel.

Sandra Okafor of Whitfield & Gage LLP is experienced public pension fund counsel who has represented CPERS and other Pacific Northwest governmental plans in numerous fund investment transactions. We should anticipate detailed and informed comments on FOIA protections, excuse rights, fiduciary duty provisions, and the scope of Excluded Provisions in the MFN framework. Ms. Okafor is likely to push for a narrow definition of Excluded Provisions to maximize CPERS\'s own MFN election power (i.e., to ensure that CPERS can elect into favorable terms granted to subsequent LPs). This creates a strategic tension: CPERS benefits from a broad MFN-eligible category (which expands the universe of terms it can elect into) but also benefits from the exclusion of its own governmental plan provisions (which prevents non-governmental LPs from electing into terms designed for CPERS).

**Recommendation to the GP:** We recommend discussing with Rajesh Mehta and Claire Dubois the acceptable level of fee compression from MFN elections and whether the GP is willing to propose commitment-tiered fee schedules. This discussion should take place before the initial drafts are finalized, as the fee structure will affect the drafting of all three anchor side letters and the MFN framework itself.

The critical distinction is that CPERS\'s excuse rights are driven by governmental investment policy mandates (a regulatory requirement), while Brindoval\'s opt-out rights are driven by business conflict (a commercial accommodation). We recommend drafting the CPERS excuse right with explicit reference to the governmental plan investment policy requirements that give rise to the request, in order to support the Excluded Provision classification and to distinguish it from Brindoval\'s opt-out request. The two provisions should be drafted under different headings and with different operative language to avoid conflation.

> • A requirement that CPERS provide written notice to the GP within a specified period (recommend five (5) business days) before disclosing any Fund information in response to a public records request;

NEP\'s investment in the Fund is part of a broader venture capital allocation within the Veltrano University endowment portfolio. Helen Bancroft, the Director of Private Investments, has been the primary relationship contact with the GP and has indicated that NEP\'s side letter priorities include advisory committee representation, key-person protections, and transfer flexibility for affiliated endowment entities.

David Tannenbaum of Hollander McKee & Stone LLP is experienced endowment counsel with a practice focused on alternative investment fund documentation. We expect Mr. Tannenbaum\'s comments to focus on transfer rights flexibility (particularly the ability to transfer NEP\'s LP interest to affiliated entities of Veltrano University), key-person provisions, and advisory committee mechanics. Mr. Tannenbaum may push for broader transfer rights than we recommend granting (e.g., a right to transfer to any affiliated entity of Veltrano University, not just endowment vehicles), and we should be prepared to explain the MFN implications of granting overly broad transfer rights.

NEP has been granted a seat on the Fund\'s advisory committee pursuant to its side letter. The advisory committee will consist of representatives of selected limited partners and will meet at least annually (and more frequently as needed) to review and address conflicts of interest, review valuations, consider requests for GP consent on specified matters, and provide input on other governance matters.

We note that CPERS is separately entitled to an advisory committee seat under the LPA itself, as a limited partner whose capital commitment equals or exceeds \$50,000,000. CPERS\'s advisory committee entitlement does not arise from its side letter and therefore does not create MFN exposure. However, this distinction should be noted clearly in the CPERS side letter to avoid any suggestion that the advisory committee seat is a side letter provision subject to MFN.

> • **LP-specific component (Excluded).** The right to transfer to an affiliated endowment vehicle of *Veltrano University specifically* is inherently specific to NEP\'s status as an investment vehicle for the Veltrano University endowment. No other LP has an affiliation with Veltrano University, and this specific transfer right would be meaningless if elected by a non-affiliated LP. This component should be drafted as an Excluded Provision under Category 5.

> • **General affiliate transfer component (MFN-Eligible).** A broader right to transfer to \"affiliates\" of the limited partner generally (without reference to Veltrano University) would be a provision of general applicability that other LPs could meaningfully elect into. If the transfer right is drafted broadly, it would be difficult to exclude from MFN.
**(a) Competitive Investment Opt-Out Rights. Recommended Classification: MFN-Eligible, with careful drafting.**

The risk of MFN-eligible classification is that other LPs with their own business conflicts (e.g., corporate venture capital arms, family offices with operating company affiliations) could elect into similar opt-out rights, potentially reducing the GP\'s flexibility to allocate investments across the LP base. However, this risk can be mitigated through narrow drafting:

**Recommendation:** MFN-eligible, but draft the provision narrowly. The narrow drafting will limit the practical utility of the provision for LPs without genuine competitive conflicts, reducing the incentive for opportunistic MFN elections.
> • Standardized reporting templates designed to facilitate comparability across fund investments.

> • **Competitive opt-out:** If broadly elected, competitive opt-out rights could reduce the GP\'s flexibility to allocate investments across the LP base. However, the narrow drafting recommended in Section V.C.2(a) above should limit opportunistic elections.

> 1\. **Robust Excluded Provisions definition.** The five categories of Excluded Provisions described in Section IV are designed to capture LP-specific regulatory, legal, and governance accommodations that should not be subject to MFN election. The breadth and specificity of these categories are the GP\'s primary structural protection against unlimited MFN exposure.

> 2\. **Narrow drafting of economic provisions.** Economic provisions (fee reductions, co-investment terms, fee netting) should be drafted with built-in limitations --- such as commitment-size conditions, caps on co-investment amounts, and netting ceilings --- that reduce the aggregate impact of MFN elections without eliminating the provisions entirely.

> 3\. **Sunset provision.** Consider including a \"sunset\" mechanism providing that MFN elections apply only to side letter terms granted before the Final Close, and do not extend to amendments, supplements, or side letters entered into after the MFN Election Period. This prevents the GP from being locked into an MFN framework indefinitely and preserves flexibility for post-closing accommodations.

> 5\. **Early GP engagement.** Engage Rajesh Mehta and Claire Dubois in a candid discussion of the acceptable level of fee compression and economic impact from MFN elections before finalizing the side letter drafts. The GP should identify specific dollar thresholds or percentage limits that define the boundaries of acceptable MFN exposure.

> • **Internal consistency review.** Owen Fischer and Stephen Adler will prepare an internal Redline Comparison Chart that places the three anchor side letters side-by-side and highlights any inconsistencies in defined terms, MFN framework provisions, or cross-references to the LPA. This chart will be circulated internally before the initial drafts are finalized.

> • **CPERS advisory committee seat.** CPERS is entitled to an advisory committee seat under the LPA itself (as a limited partner with a commitment of \$50,000,000 or more), not via the side letter. We should confirm with the GP that the LPA language is consistent with this entitlement and that the side letter accurately references (but does not duplicate) the LPA provision.

> • **Key-person provisions.** The LPA designates Rajesh Mehta and Claire Dubois as \"Key Persons\" and addresses the consequences of a key-person event, including a potential suspension of the investment period. The side letter provision (granting enhanced notification rights) should be drafted to supplement the LPA\'s key-person provisions without creating inconsistent obligations. For example, the LPA may require notice to all limited partners within ten (10) business days of a key-person event, while the side letter may require notice to NEP within five (5) business days. The side letter should be drafted to acknowledge the LPA\'s baseline notice requirement and to impose an accelerated timeline for the side letter LP only.

> • **Excuse and opt-out rights.** The LPA may contain a general excuse provision permitting limited partners to be excused from specific investments in defined circumstances (e.g., investments that would violate applicable law or cause the LP to violate a legal obligation). Side letter excuse and opt-out provisions should be drafted to supplement (and not conflict with) the LPA excuse provisions. The side letter provisions should be characterized as additional grounds for excuse that are not available under the LPA alone.

> • Excuse rights: Ms. Okafor will seek broad excuse rights covering all investment policy restrictions applicable to CPERS, potentially extending beyond tobacco and firearms to include other restricted categories (e.g., fossil fuels, private prisons). We should negotiate the scope carefully and ensure that the provisions are drafted to support Excluded Provision classification.

> • Transfer rights: Mr. Tannenbaum will likely push for broader transfer rights than we recommend, including the ability to transfer to any affiliated entity of Veltrano University (not just endowment vehicles). We should explain the MFN implications of broader language and negotiate a narrowly drafted provision.

> • Advisory committee mechanics: Mr. Tannenbaum will want to ensure that the advisory committee seat is clearly defined, including meeting frequency, quorum requirements, and the scope of matters subject to advisory committee review.

\(a\) The General Partner shall establish and maintain a Schedule of Partners (attached hereto as Schedule A), setting forth each Partner\'s name, Capital Commitment, date of admission, and Percentage Interest. The Schedule of Partners shall be updated by the General Partner following each Closing and upon the occurrence of any Transfer, withdrawal, default, or other event affecting the identity or Capital Commitment of any Partner.

\(f\) The General Partner shall notify all Limited Partners in writing within ten (10) Business Days following the initial closing of any Subscription Credit Facility, and shall provide quarterly reports to all Limited Partners setting forth the aggregate outstanding borrowings, available capacity, and weighted average interest rate under all Subscription Credit Facilities.

\(g\) The General Partner shall not amend, modify, or supplement any Subscription Credit Facility agreement in a manner that would increase the maximum aggregate borrowing capacity above the Subscription Facility Limit without the prior approval of the LPAC.

\(b\) **Geographic Focus.** The Fund\'s investment program shall be focused primarily on companies headquartered or principally operating in North America (the United States and Canada). Investments in companies headquartered outside North America shall be permitted on an opportunistic basis, provided that such investments do not, in the aggregate, exceed \[twenty percent (20%)\] of Aggregate Commitments without LPAC consent.

\(d\) **Hostile Acquisitions.** The Partnership shall not pursue or consummate any \"hostile\" acquisition (i.e., an acquisition opposed by the target company\'s board of directors or management) or any unsolicited tender offer without the prior consent of the LPAC.

\(e\) **Affiliate Transactions.** The Partnership shall not make any investment in, or enter into any transaction with, the Sponsor, any Affiliate of the Sponsor, or any portfolio company of a predecessor Harrowgate fund without (i) the prior consent of the LPAC and (ii) the affirmative vote of a majority in interest of the Limited Partners (excluding GP-affiliated Capital Commitments).
\(c\) The General Partner shall provide the Limited Partners with a written summary of all Transaction Fees received and offsets applied on at least an annual basis, and upon request by the LPAC.
\(g\) Costs associated with LPAC meetings, including travel, venue, and related expenses;

\(c\) Distributions shall generally be made in cash. In-kind distributions of securities or other property shall be permitted only with the prior consent of the LPAC (or, in the case of distributions made in connection with the liquidation and winding up of the Partnership, without LPAC consent), subject to Section 8.5.

\(a\) The General Partner may, in its reasonable discretion, establish reserves and holdbacks from Distributions for Partnership liabilities, contingencies, post-closing adjustments, indemnification obligations, and potential Clawback obligations.

\(a\) In-kind Distributions of securities or other property shall be valued at fair market value as of the date of Distribution, as determined by the General Partner in good faith (and, in the case of publicly traded securities, based on the closing market price as of such date or the volume-weighted average price over a recent trading period as determined by the General Partner).
\(b\) In-kind Distributions shall require the prior consent of the LPAC, except in connection with the liquidation and winding up of the Partnership pursuant to Article XIII.

\(a\) The Clawback obligation set forth in Section 9.1 shall be guaranteed by the following principals of Harrowgate Capital Partners LLC, each of whom shall execute a personal guarantee in form and substance reasonably acceptable to the LPAC: (i) Marcus J. Harrowgate; (ii) Diana R. Castellano; and (iii) Jonathan P. Birch (each, a **\"Clawback Guarantor\"** and, collectively, the **\"Clawback Guarantors\"**), as set forth in Schedule C.

\(b\) The results of each interim clawback test shall be provided to the LPAC within ninety (90) days following the end of the applicable Fiscal Year, together with a report from the Independent Auditor setting forth the methodology and assumptions used in such test.

\(c\) If an interim clawback test reveals that the General Partner has received excess Carried Interest, the General Partner and the LPAC shall consult in good faith regarding the appropriate treatment of such excess, which may include (i) the establishment of an escrow or holdback from future Carried Interest Distributions, (ii) the voluntary return of all or a portion of the excess by the General Partner, or (iii) such other arrangement as the General Partner and the LPAC may agree.
**[ARTICLE XI --- LIMITED PARTNER ADVISORY COMMITTEE (LPAC)]{.underline}**

\(a\) The General Partner shall establish and maintain a Limited Partner Advisory Committee (the **\"LPAC\"**) composed of five (5) members, each of whom shall be a representative designated by a Limited Partner or a group of Limited Partners.

\(b\) Three (3) LPAC members shall be designated at or promptly following the First Close. The General Partner anticipates that the initial LPAC members will be representatives designated by the following Limited Partners: (i) Northmoor State Pension System, (ii) Edgecombe Insurance Group Ltd., and (iii) The Kingsbridge Endowment Fund. The remaining two (2) LPAC members shall be designated at or following the Final Close.

\(c\) The General Partner shall designate LPAC members from among the Limited Partners, taking into consideration the diversity of the Limited Partner base (including investor type, geographic location, and commitment size), the size of each Limited Partner\'s Capital Commitment, and the willingness and ability of such Limited Partner to serve on the LPAC. The General Partner shall consult with the Limited Partners in good faith regarding LPAC composition.

\(d\) LPAC members shall serve for the duration of the Fund Term (including any extension period), unless a member resigns, is removed by the General Partner in consultation with the other LPAC members, or ceases to be a Partner. The General Partner shall designate a replacement LPAC member to fill any vacancy on the LPAC.

\(a\) The LPAC shall hold at least two (2) meetings during each Fiscal Year. Meetings may be held in person, by video conference, or by telephone conference, as determined by the General Partner in consultation with the LPAC members.

\(b\) Special meetings of the LPAC may be convened by the General Partner at any time, or upon the written request of a majority of the LPAC members. The General Partner shall provide at least ten (10) Business Days\' advance written notice of each LPAC meeting (or such shorter notice as the circumstances may require), together with an agenda and relevant supporting materials.

\(c\) The General Partner\'s personnel, including the Key Persons, shall attend LPAC meetings and shall be available to respond to questions from LPAC members regarding the Fund\'s investments, operations, and performance.
\(d\) The General Partner shall prepare and distribute written minutes of each LPAC meeting to the LPAC members within thirty (30) days following such meeting.

\(a\) The LPAC shall act in an advisory and consent capacity only. The LPAC shall not have any management authority over the affairs of the Partnership and shall not participate in the control of the Partnership\'s business within the meaning of Section 17-303 of the Act.
\(b\) The following matters shall require the prior approval or consent of the LPAC:
> \(iii\) Extension of the Fund Term beyond the second GP discretionary extension (i.e., the third one-year extension described in Section 2.5(c) shall require LPAC approval);
> \(xi\) Such other matters as may be submitted to the LPAC by the General Partner from time to time.
\(c\) The LPAC\'s approval or consent shall not be required for any matter not expressly set forth in Section 11.3(b) or elsewhere in this Agreement.
\(a\) A quorum for the transaction of business at any meeting of the LPAC shall consist of a majority of the LPAC members (i.e., three (3) out of five (5) members).
\(b\) All actions of the LPAC shall be taken by the affirmative vote of a majority of the LPAC members present and constituting a quorum.
\(c\) The LPAC may act by written consent in lieu of a meeting if a majority of LPAC members execute a written consent approving the action to be taken.

\(a\) LPAC members shall act solely in an advisory capacity and shall not owe fiduciary duties to any other Limited Partner, the Partnership, or the General Partner by virtue of their service on the LPAC. No LPAC member shall be liable to the Partnership, the General Partner, or any other Partner for any act or omission taken in connection with LPAC service, except to the extent caused by such LPAC member\'s fraud, bad faith, or willful misconduct.

\(b\) The Partnership shall indemnify and hold harmless each LPAC member (and such LPAC member\'s employer, Affiliates, officers, directors, and employees) against any and all losses, claims, damages, liabilities, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys\' fees) arising out of or in connection with such LPAC member\'s service on the LPAC, except to the extent such losses are the result of fraud, bad faith, or willful misconduct by such LPAC member.

\(a\) Each LPAC member shall be bound by the confidentiality obligations set forth in Section 15.4 of this Agreement with respect to all information received in connection with LPAC service, including information regarding the Fund\'s investments, Portfolio Companies, other Limited Partners, and the General Partner\'s proprietary investment processes.

\(b\) Notwithstanding the foregoing, LPAC members that are governmental plan investors or other public entities may disclose confidential information to the extent required by applicable public records laws, freedom of information acts, or other mandatory disclosure obligations, *provided* that such LPAC member shall provide advance written notice to the General Partner (to the extent practicable and permitted by law) of any such required disclosure and shall cooperate with the General Partner in seeking to minimize the scope of such disclosure or to obtain confidential treatment.

\(b\) No Limited Partner shall participate in the management or control of the Partnership\'s business, transact any business on behalf of the Partnership, or have any power to sign for or bind the Partnership. No Limited Partner shall be deemed to be participating in the control of the Partnership\'s business within the meaning of Section 17-303 of the Act by virtue of exercising any right or power granted to Limited Partners under this Agreement (including voting rights, consent rights, and rights to participate on the LPAC).

The General Partner and its Associates shall be entitled to rely, and shall be fully protected in relying, upon information, opinions, reports, or statements (including financial statements and information, and opinions, reports, or statements as to the value or amount of assets, liabilities, profits, or losses of the Partnership or any facts pertinent to the existence and amount of assets from which distributions might properly be paid) of the following Persons or groups: (a) one or more officers or employees of the General Partner or the Sponsor whom the General Partner reasonably believes to be reliable and competent in the matters presented; (b) any attorney, independent accountant, appraiser, or other expert or advisor (including Calderwood & Harkness LLP and Caldwell, Fitch & Hartley LLP) whom the General Partner reasonably believes to be qualified in the matters presented; and (c) any committee of the LPAC acting within the scope of its authority.

\(c\) The Sponsor shall not raise or commence fundraising for a successor private equity fund during the Investment Period until at least seventy-five percent (75%) of the Fund\'s Aggregate Commitments have been invested or committed to Portfolio Investments. For purposes of this Section 12.4, Capital Commitments shall be deemed \"committed\" when the General Partner has entered into a binding agreement (including a letter of intent or term sheet accepted by the General Partner) for a Portfolio Investment, irrespective of whether funding has occurred. For the avoidance of doubt, amounts that are subject to binding commitments (including signed letters of intent or purchase agreements) but that have not yet been funded shall be deemed \"committed\" for purposes of this Section 12.4(c).

\(d\) In the event of a conflict between the interests of the Partnership and the interests of any other fund, account, or vehicle managed by the Sponsor or its Affiliates, the General Partner shall resolve such conflict in a manner that it reasonably determines to be fair and equitable to the Partnership, subject to the LPAC\'s authority to review and approve conflicts of interest and related-party transactions as set forth in Section 11.3(b)(i).

\(b\) The General Partner shall not be liable to the Partnership or any Partner for any act or omission performed in good faith and in a manner reasonably believed to be in, or not opposed to, the best interests of the Partnership, absent gross negligence, willful misconduct, or fraud.

The General Partner may not voluntarily withdraw or resign from the Partnership without the prior written consent of the Limited Partners holding in the aggregate at least a majority of the Capital Commitments of all Limited Partners (excluding the GP Commitment and any Capital Commitments held by Affiliates of the General Partner). Any purported withdrawal in violation of this Section 12.7 shall be void and of no effect.
The Partnership shall be dissolved upon the first to occur of the following events:

\(b\) A vote of the Limited Partners holding in the aggregate at least seventy-five percent (75%) of the Capital Commitments of all Limited Partners (excluding the GP Commitment and any Capital Commitments held by Affiliates of the General Partner) to dissolve the Partnership;

\(a\) The proposed transferee shall have executed an assignment and assumption agreement in the form attached hereto as Exhibit C (or in such other form as the General Partner may prescribe), pursuant to which the transferee assumes all obligations of the transferor with respect to the transferred Partnership Interest;

A transferee of all or any portion of a Partnership Interest shall be admitted as a substitute Limited Partner of the Partnership (a **\"Substitute Limited Partner\"**) only upon (a) the General Partner\'s consent to the Transfer (to the extent required under Section 14.1), (b) the satisfaction of all conditions set forth in Section 14.2, and (c) the execution by the transferee of a joinder or counterpart to this Agreement and such other documents as the General Partner may reasonably require. Until a transferee is admitted as a Substitute Limited Partner, such transferee shall be treated as an assignee with economic rights only (i.e., the right to receive allocations and Distributions) and shall have no right to vote on or consent to any matter submitted to the Limited Partners.

\(a\) The Partnership shall, to the fullest extent permitted by the Act and applicable law, indemnify and hold harmless the General Partner, its members, managers, officers, directors, employees, and agents (including Associates, Key Persons, and LPAC members) (collectively, **\"Indemnified Persons\"**) against any and all losses, claims, damages, liabilities, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys\' fees, judgments, fines, settlement amounts, and other expenses incurred in connection with the investigation, preparation, defense, or settlement of any pending or threatened claim, action, suit, or proceeding, whether civil, criminal, administrative, or investigative) arising out of or in connection with the activities of the Partnership, the General Partner\'s management of the Partnership, or any act or omission of an Indemnified Person in connection with the affairs of the Partnership, *except* to the extent that such losses are determined by a final, non-appealable judgment of a court of competent jurisdiction to have been caused by such Indemnified Person\'s fraud, gross negligence, willful misconduct, or material breach of this Agreement.

The General Partner, its members, managers, officers, directors, employees, and agents (including Associates) shall not be liable to the Partnership or any Partner for any act or omission performed or omitted in good faith and in a manner reasonably believed to be in, or not opposed to, the best interests of the Partnership, absent a determination by a final, non-appealable judgment of a court of competent jurisdiction that such act or omission constituted gross negligence, willful misconduct, or fraud. The elimination of liability provided by this Section 15.2 shall be in addition to the indemnification provisions set forth in Section 15.1 and shall apply to the fullest extent permitted by the Act and applicable law.

\(c\) Notwithstanding the foregoing, the General Partner may, without the consent of any Limited Partner, make ministerial, clarifying, or administrative amendments to this Agreement that (i) do not adversely affect the rights or obligations of any Limited Partner in any material respect, (ii) are necessary or appropriate to cure any ambiguity, defect, or inconsistency in this Agreement, (iii) are required to comply with applicable law, regulation, or the requirements of any governmental authority, or (iv) are necessary to reflect the admission of new Partners, the withdrawal or default of Partners, the updating of the Schedule of Partners, or other changes contemplated by this Agreement.

This Agreement (together with the Subscription Agreements executed by each Limited Partner, the Side Letters entered into between the General Partner and the respective Limited Partners, and the Schedules and Exhibits attached hereto) constitutes the entire agreement among the Partners with respect to the subject matter hereof and supersedes all prior agreements, understandings, representations, and warranties (whether oral or written) among the Partners with respect to such subject matter. No Partner has relied on any representation or warranty not set forth in this Agreement or in the applicable Subscription Agreement.

This Agreement may be executed in one or more counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original and all of which, taken together, shall constitute one and the same instrument. Delivery of an executed counterpart of a signature page to this Agreement by facsimile transmission, email (including .pdf format), or other electronic means shall be effective as delivery of a manually executed counterpart. Electronic signatures (including signatures compliant with the U.S. Electronic Signatures in Global and National Commerce Act (E-SIGN) and the Uniform Electronic Transactions Act (UETA)) shall be valid and binding for all purposes of this Agreement.
\(a\) No waiver of any provision of this Agreement shall be effective unless made in a writing signed by the Partner or Partners against whom such waiver is sought to be enforced.
**IN WITNESS WHEREOF**, the undersigned have executed this Agreement of Limited Partnership as of the date of the First Close.

Each Limited Partner has executed a Subscription Agreement containing a signature page and joinder to this Agreement, which Subscription Agreements are incorporated herein by this reference. The signature of each Limited Partner on its respective Subscription Agreement shall constitute such Limited Partner\'s execution of, and agreement to be bound by, this Agreement of Limited Partnership.

The CPERS Side Letter sets forth certain rights, obligations, and modifications to the LPA that are applicable solely as between the General Partner and CPERS.
105: 
106: **Key Provisions Covered:**
107: 
108: > \(a\) **Management Fee Reduction.** Reduction of the management fee payable by CPERS to 1.75% per annum on committed capital during the Investment Period (representing a 25 basis point discount from the standard 2.00% management fee set forth in Section 6.1 of the LPA). Following the expiration of the Investment Period, CPERS will pay the management fee at the standard rate of 2.00% per annum on invested capital, consistent with the LPA.
109: >
110: > \(b\) **Excuse Rights.** Right of CPERS to be excused from participating in any Fund investment in a portfolio company that derives more than 15% of its revenues from the manufacture, distribution, or sale of tobacco products or firearms and related accessories, in each case as determined in good faith by the General Partner. The General Partner shall provide CPERS with reasonable prior written notice of any proposed investment that it believes may trigger this excuse right and shall afford CPERS a period of not less than ten (10) business days to exercise such right.
111: >
112: > \(c\) **Enhanced Quarterly Reporting.** Entitlement to enhanced quarterly reports including sector-level performance attribution, detailed portfolio company metrics (including revenue growth, customer acquisition costs, and net retention rates), and a narrative discussion of portfolio developments, in addition to the standard quarterly reports provided to all limited partners under the LPA.
113: >
114: > \(d\) **FOIA / Public Records Protection Carve-Outs.** Acknowledgment by the General Partner that CPERS is a governmental plan subject to the Washington Public Records Act (RCW 42.56) and related public disclosure requirements. Provisions establishing (i) the General Partner\'s obligation to label confidential or proprietary information as such, (ii) CPERS\'s obligation to notify the General Partner promptly (and in any event within five (5) business days) of any public records request that could require disclosure of Fund-related information, and (iii) the General Partner\'s right to seek a protective order or other appropriate remedy prior to any such disclosure.
115: >
116: > \(e\) **Co-Investment Rights.** Right to participate in co-investment opportunities alongside the Fund, with no management fee or carried interest charged on co-invested capital. Co-investment allocations shall be offered to CPERS on a pro rata basis relative to its commitment to the Fund, subject to the General Partner\'s discretion regarding allocation among all co-investment-eligible limited partners.
117: >
118: > \(f\) **Most Favored Nation Election Right.** Right to elect to receive the benefit of any more favorable terms granted to any other limited partner in the Fund (subject to certain Excluded Provisions as described in Section IX of this Checklist), in accordance with the MFN election procedures established in the side letters and the procedures letter to be delivered following the Final Close.

The MFN procedures letter will be delivered to each MFN-eligible limited partner within fifteen (15) business days after the Final Close of the Fund (targeted for July 15, 2026). The procedures letter will enclose:
501: 
502: > \(i\) A redacted compilation of all side letters entered into by the General Partner with limited partners in the Fund (the \"MFN Side Letter Compilation\"), with the identities of the limited partners that are parties to such side letters redacted and with Excluded Provisions (as defined below) redacted or omitted, as applicable; and
503: >
504: > \(ii\) The MFN Election Form (Item 21), to be completed and returned by the electing limited partner within the MFN Election Period.
505: 
506: The MFN Election Period is thirty (30) calendar days commencing upon delivery of the MFN Side Letter Compilation and the MFN Election Form to the eligible limited partner.

509:
