519: 
520: **Note:** The MFN procedures letter and MFN election form are not executed at the First Close. However, both templates must be in final approved form prior to or concurrently with the First Close to ensure compliance with the MFN framework established in each of the three anchor LP side letters and to facilitate prompt delivery following the Final Close.
521: 
522: **Responsible Party:** C&H (prepare and finalize the procedures letter template and the MFN Side Letter Compilation format); GP (review and approve the final forms of the procedures letter and compilation)

The MFN Election Form is the document that an MFN-eligible limited partner will complete and return to the General Partner to elect the benefit of one or more provisions from the MFN Side Letter Compilation.

**[I. INTRODUCTION AND INSTRUCTIONS]{.underline}**

This Closing Checklist (this \"Checklist\") has been prepared by Calderwood & Harkness LLP (\"C&H\") in its capacity as fund counsel to Pinnacle Venture Capital Management LLC (the \"General Partner\" or \"GP\"), the general partner of Pinnacle Venture Fund II LP (the \"Fund\" or \"Fund II\"), a Delaware limited partnership. The purpose of this Checklist is to track all deliverables required for the execution and closing of the side letter package in connection with the First Close of the Fund, which is targeted for January 15, 2026 (the \"First Close\" or the \"First Close Date\").

The side letters described herein supplement and, to the extent of any conflict between the provisions of a side letter and the corresponding provisions of the partnership agreement, modify solely as between the General Partner and the applicable limited partner, the Amended and Restated Limited Partnership Agreement of Pinnacle Venture Fund II LP, dated as of the First Close (the \"LPA\"). In all cases, the side letters are intended to be read in conjunction with the LPA, and any capitalized terms used in the side letters and not otherwise defined therein have the meanings assigned to them in the LPA.
Three anchor limited partners are party to individually negotiated side letters at the First Close:

> 1\. **Cascadia Public Employees\' Retirement System (\"CPERS\")** --- Capital commitment of \$75,000,000, representing approximately 12.5% of the Fund\'s \$600,000,000 target fund size. CPERS is a governmental pension plan organized under the laws of the State of Washington.

> 2\. **Northstar Endowment Partners LLC (\"Northstar\" or \"NEP\")** --- Capital commitment of \$50,000,000, representing approximately 8.33% of the Fund\'s \$600,000,000 target fund size. Northstar is a Delaware limited liability company that serves as the investment vehicle for the Veltrano University endowment\'s allocation to venture capital and growth equity.

> 3\. **Brindoval Family Office Holdings LP (\"Brindoval\")** --- Capital commitment of \$40,000,000, representing approximately 6.67% of the Fund\'s \$600,000,000 target fund size. Brindoval is a Delaware limited partnership that functions as the principal investment vehicle for the Raines family single-family office.

The total aggregate capital commitments from the three anchor limited partners at the First Close amount to \$165,000,000, representing approximately 27.5% of the Fund\'s \$600,000,000 target fund size. These anchor commitments form the foundation of the Fund\'s investor base and are expected to represent the largest individual LP commitments in the Fund at the Final Close.

All side letters and the LPA are governed by the laws of the State of Delaware, without regard to conflict of law principles that would result in the application of the laws of any other jurisdiction.
**Responsible Party abbreviations.** The following abbreviations are used throughout this Checklist to identify the party or parties responsible for each deliverable:
> • **C&H** --- Calderwood & Harkness LLP (fund counsel to the General Partner)
> • **GP** --- Pinnacle Venture Capital Management LLC, as general partner of Pinnacle Venture Fund II LP
> • **LP Counsel** --- The applicable limited partner\'s outside legal counsel, as follows:
> • *Whitfield & Gage LLP* (Sandra Okafor, Partner) --- counsel to Cascadia Public Employees\' Retirement System
> • *Hollander McKee & Stone LLP* (David Tannenbaum, Partner) --- counsel to Northstar Endowment Partners LLC
> • *Prescott & Langley LLP* (Angela Ferris, Partner) --- counsel to Brindoval Family Office Holdings LP

**Instructions for Use.** Each item in this Checklist should be marked with its current status (using the Status Legend set forth on the cover page) and the date on which the status was last updated. As documents move from draft to final to executed status, the responsible party should notify Owen Fischer at C&H so that the master version of this Checklist can be updated. All final, fully executed versions of the documents and deliverables described herein will be compiled into the closing binder (physical and electronic) promptly following the First Close. Stephen Adler at C&H will be responsible for the compilation and indexing of the closing binder.

This Checklist covers only the side letter package deliverables. The main Fund Closing Checklist (maintained separately by C&H) covers all other First Close deliverables, including subscription agreements, LPA execution by all limited partners, partnership tax matters (including tax identification numbers, FATCA/CRS classifications, and IRS Form W-9 or W-8 collection), state and federal regulatory filings, banking and custody arrangements, and related matters.
**[II. EXECUTED SIDE LETTERS]{.underline}**
**Item 1: Side Letter --- Cascadia Public Employees\' Retirement System**

**Description:** Execution copy of the Side Letter (the \"CPERS Side Letter\") between Pinnacle Venture Capital Management LLC, in its capacity as general partner of Pinnacle Venture Fund II LP, and Cascadia Public Employees\' Retirement System, dated as of the First Close (January 15, 2026). The CPERS Side Letter sets forth certain rights, obligations, and modifications to the LPA that are applicable solely as between the General Partner and CPERS.
**Key Provisions Covered:**

> \(a\) **Management Fee Reduction.** Reduction of the management fee payable by CPERS to 1.75% per annum on committed capital during the Investment Period (representing a 25 basis point discount from the standard 2.00% management fee set forth in Section 6.1 of the LPA). Following the expiration of the Investment Period, CPERS will pay the management fee at the standard rate of 2.00% per annum on invested capital, consistent with the LPA.

> \(b\) **Excuse Rights.** Right of CPERS to be excused from participating in any Fund investment in a portfolio company that derives more than 15% of its revenues from the manufacture, distribution, or sale of tobacco products or firearms and related accessories, in each case as determined in good faith by the General Partner. The General Partner shall provide CPERS with reasonable prior written notice of any proposed investment that it believes may trigger this excuse right and shall afford CPERS a period of not less than ten (10) business days to exercise such right.

> \(c\) **Enhanced Quarterly Reporting.** Entitlement to enhanced quarterly reports including sector-level performance attribution, detailed portfolio company metrics (including revenue growth, customer acquisition costs, and net retention rates), and a narrative discussion of portfolio developments, in addition to the standard quarterly reports provided to all limited partners under the LPA.

> \(d\) **FOIA / Public Records Protection Carve-Outs.** Acknowledgment by the General Partner that CPERS is a governmental plan subject to the Washington Public Records Act (RCW 42.56) and related public disclosure requirements. Provisions establishing (i) the General Partner\'s obligation to label confidential or proprietary information as such, (ii) CPERS\'s obligation to notify the General Partner promptly (and in any event within five (5) business days) of any public records request that could require disclosure of Fund-related information, and (iii) the General Partner\'s right to seek a protective order or other appropriate remedy prior to any such disclosure.

> \(e\) **Co-Investment Rights.** Right to participate in co-investment opportunities alongside the Fund, with no management fee or carried interest charged on co-invested capital. Co-investment allocations shall be offered to CPERS on a pro rata basis relative to its commitment to the Fund, subject to the General Partner\'s discretion regarding allocation among all co-investment-eligible limited partners.

> \(f\) **Most Favored Nation Election Right.** Right to elect to receive the benefit of any more favorable terms granted to any other limited partner in the Fund (subject to certain Excluded Provisions as described in Section IX of this Checklist), in accordance with the MFN election procedures established in the side letters and the procedures letter to be delivered following the Final Close.
> \(g\) **Tax-Exempt Status Representations.** Representations by CPERS regarding its status as a tax-exempt entity under Section 115 of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended.
**Commitment Amount:** \$75,000,000
**Responsible Party:** C&H (prepare final execution version); GP (execute on behalf of the Fund); LP Counsel --- Whitfield & Gage LLP (Sandra Okafor) (obtain LP execution)
**Number of Originals Required:** Two (2) --- one original for the General Partner\'s files and one original for CPERS\'s files.
**Status:** \[   \]
**Date Last Updated:** **\_\_\_**
**Item 2: Side Letter --- Northstar Endowment Partners LLC**

**Description:** Execution copy of the Side Letter (the \"Northstar Side Letter\") between Pinnacle Venture Capital Management LLC, in its capacity as general partner of Pinnacle Venture Fund II LP, and Northstar Endowment Partners LLC, dated as of the First Close (January 15, 2026). The Northstar Side Letter sets forth certain rights, obligations, and modifications to the LPA that are applicable solely as between the General Partner and Northstar.
**Key Provisions Covered:**

> \(a\) **Management Fee Reduction.** Reduction of the management fee payable by Northstar to 1.85% per annum on committed capital during the Investment Period (representing a 15 basis point discount from the standard 2.00% management fee set forth in Section 6.1 of the LPA). Following the expiration of the Investment Period, Northstar will pay the management fee at the standard rate of 2.00% per annum on invested capital, consistent with the LPA.

> \(b\) **Advisory Committee Seat.** Right to designate one (1) representative to serve on the Fund\'s Advisory Committee established under Section 9.1 of the LPA. Northstar\'s initial designee is expected to be Helen Bancroft, Director of Private Investments, or such other individual as Northstar may designate from time to time upon written notice to the General Partner.

> \(c\) **Key-Person Event Notification.** Right to receive prompt written notification (and in any event within five (5) business days) in the event that either Rajesh Mehta or Claire Dubois ceases to devote substantially all of his or her business time and attention to the affairs of the Fund (a \"Key Person Event\"), together with a description of the General Partner\'s plan to address the Key Person Event. This notification right is in addition to, and does not limit, the Key Person Event provisions set forth in Section 8.3 of the LPA.

> \(d\) **Co-Investment Rights.** Right to participate in co-investment opportunities alongside the Fund on terms substantially similar to those described in the CPERS Side Letter (Item 1, clause (e) above).

> \(e\) **Transfer Rights.** Right to transfer all or a portion of Northstar\'s limited partnership interest in the Fund to one or more affiliated endowment investment vehicles of Veltrano University, without the prior written consent of the General Partner that would otherwise be required under Section 10.2 of the LPA, provided that (i) such transfer complies with all applicable securities laws, (ii) the transferee executes such documents as the General Partner may reasonably require (including a joinder to the LPA and, if applicable, a counterpart to the Northstar Side Letter), and (iii) such transfer would not cause the Fund to be treated as a \"publicly traded partnership\" for U.S. federal income tax purposes.

> \(f\) **ERISA Representation Waiver.** Representation by Northstar that it is not, and the assets being contributed by it to the Fund do not constitute \"plan assets\" of, an \"employee benefit plan\" as defined in Section 3(3) of the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974, as amended (\"ERISA\"), nor is Northstar subject to the provisions of ERISA. The standard ERISA representations in the subscription agreement shall be modified accordingly.

> \(g\) **Most Favored Nation Election Right.** Right to elect to receive the benefit of any more favorable terms granted to any other limited partner in the Fund (subject to certain Excluded Provisions as described in Section IX of this Checklist), in accordance with the MFN election procedures established in the side letters and the procedures letter to be delivered following the Final Close.
**Commitment Amount:** \$50,000,000
**Responsible Party:** C&H (prepare final execution version); GP (execute on behalf of the Fund); LP Counsel --- Hollander McKee & Stone LLP (David Tannenbaum) (obtain LP execution)
**Number of Originals Required:** Two (2) --- one original for the General Partner\'s files and one original for Northstar\'s files.
**Status:** \[   \]
**Date Last Updated:** **\_\_\_**
**Item 3: Side Letter --- Brindoval Family Office Holdings LP**

**Description:** Execution copy of the Side Letter (the \"Brindoval Side Letter\") between Pinnacle Venture Capital Management LLC, in its capacity as general partner of Pinnacle Venture Fund II LP, and Brindoval Family Office Holdings LP, dated as of the First Close (January 15, 2026). The Brindoval Side Letter sets forth certain rights, obligations, and modifications to the LPA that are applicable solely as between the General Partner and Brindoval.
**Key Provisions Covered:**

> \(a\) **Opt-Out Rights.** Right of Brindoval to elect not to participate in any Fund investment in a portfolio company that the General Partner determines, in good faith and after consultation with Brindoval, to be directly competitive with any software-as-a-service (\"SaaS\") business owned or controlled by the Raines family or any of its affiliated entities. The General Partner shall provide Brindoval with reasonable prior written notice of any proposed investment that it believes may trigger this opt-out right, together with a summary description of the proposed portfolio company\'s business sufficient for Brindoval to make an informed determination, and shall afford Brindoval a period of not less than ten (10) business days to exercise such right. For the avoidance of doubt, Brindoval\'s exercise of this opt-out right shall not reduce its unfunded commitment to the Fund.

> \(b\) **Co-Investment Rights.** Right to participate in co-investment opportunities alongside the Fund on terms consistent with those made available to other co-investment-eligible limited partners, subject to the General Partner\'s discretion regarding allocation.

> \(c\) **Management Fee / Carried Interest Netting.** Right to have management fees paid by Brindoval netted against distributions of carried interest otherwise payable to the General Partner with respect to Brindoval\'s interest in the Fund. This netting mechanism applies at the time of each distribution and effectively reduces the General Partner\'s carried interest allocation attributable to Brindoval\'s interest by the aggregate amount of management fees previously paid by Brindoval.

> \(d\) **Information Rights.** Entitlement to enhanced information rights aligned with the Institutional Limited Partners Association (\"ILPA\") best practices, including (i) annual audited financial statements delivered within 90 days following the end of each fiscal year, (ii) unaudited quarterly financial statements delivered within 45 days following the end of each fiscal quarter, (iii) capital account statements, and (iv) annual meeting or investor update access.

> \(e\) **Most Favored Nation Election Right.** Right to elect to receive the benefit of any more favorable terms granted to any other limited partner in the Fund (subject to certain Excluded Provisions as described in Section IX of this Checklist), in accordance with the MFN election procedures established in the side letters and the procedures letter to be delivered following the Final Close.

> \(f\) **Management Fee Rate.** Standard management fee of 2.00% per annum on committed capital during the Investment Period (no discount from the standard rate set forth in Section 6.1 of the LPA). Post-Investment Period management fee at the standard rate of 2.00% per annum on invested capital.
**Commitment Amount:** \$40,000,000
**Responsible Party:** C&H (prepare final execution version); GP (execute on behalf of the Fund); LP Counsel --- Prescott & Langley LLP (Angela Ferris) (obtain LP execution)
**Number of Originals Required:** Two (2) --- one original for the General Partner\'s files and one original for Brindoval\'s files.
**Status:** \[   \]
**Date Last Updated:** **\_\_\_**

**Item 19: Executed Amended and Restated Limited Partnership Agreement**

**Description:** Fully executed copy of the Amended and Restated Limited Partnership Agreement of Pinnacle Venture Fund II LP, dated as of January 15, 2026 (the \"LPA\"). The LPA sets forth the comprehensive terms and conditions governing the Fund, including the rights and obligations of the General Partner and all limited partners, capital contributions and distributions, management fees and carried interest, investment restrictions, governance, reporting, transfers, dissolution, and other matters. All side letters described in Section II of this Checklist supplement and modify the LPA solely as between the General Partner and the applicable limited partner, and only to the extent expressly set forth in the applicable side letter. In the event of a conflict between the terms of a side letter and the terms of the LPA, the side letter shall control, but only as to the limited partner that is a party to such side letter.
**Key LPA Terms (for Reference):**

> The following is a summary of certain key terms of the LPA, included for reference purposes only in connection with the review and finalization of the side letter package. This summary is not exhaustive and does not purport to be a complete description of the LPA.
> • **Fund Target Size:** \$600,000,000
> • **Fund Hard Cap:** \$750,000,000 (125% of target)
> • **First Close:** January 15, 2026
> • **Final Close Deadline:** July 15, 2026 (six months after First Close)
> • **Management Fee (Investment Period):** 2.00% per annum on committed capital, payable quarterly in advance, during the Investment Period (January 15, 2026 through January 15, 2031)

> • **Management Fee (Post-Investment Period):** 2.00% per annum on invested capital (cost basis of unrealized investments plus committed but uncalled capital for follow-on investments), payable quarterly in advance

> • **Carried Interest:** 20% of net profits, calculated on a whole-fund (aggregated) basis, subject to an 8% preferred return (compounded annually) and a 100% General Partner catch-up until the General Partner has received 20% of cumulative net profits, thereafter splitting 80% to limited partners and 20% to the General Partner
> • **Preferred Return:** 8% per annum, compounded annually
> • **Clawback:** Standard European-style clawback, with interim clawback testing on a rolling basis

> • **Fund Term:** Ten (10) years from the First Close (expiring January 15, 2036), with two (2) successive one-year extension periods at the discretion of the General Partner (latest possible termination date: January 15, 2038)

**[IX. MOST FAVORED NATION ELECTION FRAMEWORK]{.underline}**
**Item 20: MFN Election Procedures Letter Template --- Finalization**

**Description:** Confirmation that the template most favored nation (\"MFN\") election procedures letter to be sent to MFN-eligible limited partners has been finalized and approved by the General Partner. The MFN procedures letter will be delivered to each MFN-eligible limited partner within fifteen (15) business days after the Final Close of the Fund (targeted for July 15, 2026). The procedures letter will enclose:

> \(i\) A redacted compilation of all side letters entered into by the General Partner with limited partners in the Fund (the \"MFN Side Letter Compilation\"), with the identities of the limited partners that are parties to such side letters redacted and with Excluded Provisions (as defined below) redacted or omitted, as applicable; and
> \(ii\) The MFN Election Form (Item 21), to be completed and returned by the electing limited partner within the MFN Election Period.
The MFN Election Period is thirty (30) calendar days commencing upon delivery of the MFN Side Letter Compilation and the MFN Election Form to the eligible limited partner.

**MFN Eligibility Threshold.** Only limited partners with aggregate capital commitments to the Fund equal to or greater than \$25,000,000 are eligible to exercise the MFN election right. As of the First Close, all three anchor limited partners (CPERS, Northstar, and Brindoval) satisfy this threshold.

**Categories of Excluded Provisions.** The following categories of provisions are excluded from the MFN election process and may not be elected by an MFN-eligible limited partner (collectively, \"Excluded Provisions\"):

> \(a\) Provisions that the General Partner has granted to a limited partner solely because such provisions are required to satisfy specific legal, regulatory, or tax requirements applicable to such limited partner and not generally applicable to all limited partners (e.g., FOIA/public records protection carve-outs for governmental pension plans such as CPERS; ERISA representations or waivers for endowment vehicles such as Northstar);
> \(b\) Advisory committee seats and related governance rights;
> \(c\) Portfolio company board observer rights;

> \(d\) Any other terms that the General Partner reasonably determines, in its sole discretion, are specific to the legal, regulatory, tax, or organizational status of the limited partner to which they were originally granted and are not applicable to or appropriate for the limited partner seeking to elect such terms.

**Note:** The MFN procedures letter and MFN election form are not executed at the First Close. However, both templates must be in final approved form prior to or concurrently with the First Close to ensure compliance with the MFN framework established in each of the three anchor LP side letters and to facilitate prompt delivery following the Final Close.

**Responsible Party:** C&H (prepare and finalize the procedures letter template and the MFN Side Letter Compilation format); GP (review and approve the final forms of the procedures letter and compilation)
**Status:** \[   \]
**Date Last Updated:** **\_\_\_**
**Item 21: MFN Election Form Template --- Finalization**

**Description:** Confirmation that the standalone most favored nation election form template (the \"MFN Election Form\") has been finalized and approved by the General Partner. The MFN Election Form is the document that an MFN-eligible limited partner will complete and return to the General Partner to elect the benefit of one or more provisions from the MFN Side Letter Compilation.
**Required Fields and Content.** The MFN Election Form includes the following fields and sections:
> \(a\) Name of the electing limited partner;
> \(b\) Capital commitment amount of the electing limited partner (to verify compliance with the \$25,000,000 MFN eligibility threshold);
> \(c\) Date of the MFN election;
> \(d\) Identification of the specific provisions elected by the limited partner, by reference to the section or item numbers assigned in the MFN Side Letter Compilation;

> \(e\) Representations by the electing limited partner regarding its MFN eligibility, including confirmation that (i) the limited partner\'s capital commitment to the Fund is equal to or greater than \$25,000,000, (ii) the limited partner has reviewed the MFN Side Letter Compilation and the MFN procedures letter, and (iii) the elected provisions are not Excluded Provisions;

1970: \(c\) The interest component of the catch-up contribution shall be distributed to the Partners who funded Capital Calls prior to such Subsequent Close, pro rata in proportion to their respective funded Capital Contributions, and shall not constitute a return of capital for purposes of the distribution waterfall.
1971: 
1972: \(d\) Upon admission at a Subsequent Close, each Limited Partner shall be treated, for purposes of the distribution waterfall, allocations, and all other economic provisions of this Agreement, as if such Limited Partner had been admitted at the First Close.
1973: 
1974: **[Section 3.5 --- Minimum LP Commitment]{.underline}**
1975: 
1976: Each Limited Partner shall be required to make a Capital Commitment of at least Ten Million Dollars (\$10,000,000) (the **\"Minimum LP Commitment\"**); *provided*, that the General Partner may, in its sole discretion, waive or reduce the Minimum LP Commitment for any particular Limited Partner or class of Limited Partners.
1977: 
1978: **[Section 3.6 --- Schedule of Partners]{.underline}**
1979: 
1980: \(a\) The General Partner shall establish and maintain a Schedule of Partners (attached hereto as Schedule A), setting forth each Partner\'s name, Capital Commitment, date of admission, and Percentage Interest. The Schedule of Partners shall be updated by the General Partner following each Closing and upon the occurrence of any Transfer, withdrawal, default, or other event affecting the identity or Capital Commitment of any Partner.
1981: 
1982: \(b\) The Schedule of Partners shall constitute a part of this Agreement, and any updates thereto by the General Partner shall be deemed to be an amendment to this Agreement, without requiring the consent of the Limited Partners.
1983: 
1984: **[ARTICLE IV --- CAPITAL COMMITMENTS AND CAPITAL CONTRIBUTIONS]{.underline}**
1985: 
1986: **[Section 4.1 --- Capital Commitments]{.underline}**
1987: 
1988: \(a\) Each Partner\'s Capital Commitment shall be as set forth in such Partner\'s Subscription Agreement and reflected in the Schedule of Partners. Capital Commitments shall be irrevocable once accepted by the General Partner, except as otherwise expressly provided in this Agreement.
1989: 
1990: \(b\) The aggregate of all Capital Commitments shall not exceed Two Billion Dollars (\$2,000,000,000) (the **\"hard cap\"**), except as may be increased by the General Partner with the consent of a majority in interest of the Limited Partners.
1991: 
1992: \(c\) No Partner shall be required to contribute capital to the Partnership in excess of such Partner\'s Capital Commitment, except as may be required (i) pursuant to Section 4.5 (Subsequent Close Equalization), (ii) to fund the return of distributions required by law or by the terms of this Agreement, or (iii) as otherwise agreed in writing by such Partner.
1993: 
1994: **[Section 4.2 --- Capital Calls / Drawdown Notices]{.underline}**
1995: 
1996: \(a\) During the Investment Period and thereafter (solely for the purposes permitted by Section 5.2), the General Partner may require each Partner to contribute all or any portion of such Partner\'s unfunded Capital Commitment by issuing a Capital Call (also referred to as a \"Drawdown Notice\") to each Partner in writing. Each Capital Call shall specify: (i) the aggregate amount of the capital contribution requested from all Partners; (ii) each Partner\'s pro rata share of such capital contribution (based on each Partner\'s unfunded Capital Commitment as a proportion of the aggregate unfunded Capital Commitments of all Partners, unless otherwise agreed); (iii) the purpose of such capital contribution (including whether for a Portfolio Investment, Management Fees, Organizational Expenses, Fund Expenses, Subscription Credit Facility repayment, or other Partnership purposes); and (iv) the funding date on which such capital contribution is due.
1997: 
1998: \(b\) Each Capital Call shall be issued not less than ten (10) Business Days prior to the applicable funding date, unless a shorter notice period is agreed to by the Partners or is necessitated by the timing requirements of a Portfolio Investment (in which case the General Partner shall provide as much notice as is practicable under the circumstances, and in no event less than five (5) Business Days).
1999: 
2000: \(c\) Capital Calls shall be made pro rata based on each Partner\'s unfunded Capital Commitment relative to the aggregate unfunded Capital Commitments of all Partners, unless the General Partner and the affected Partners otherwise agree (for example, in connection with the exercise of excuse rights under Section 15.19 or the reallocation of a Defaulting Partner\'s share).
2001: 
2002: \(d\) The General Partner may issue Capital Calls for any purpose related to the business of the Partnership, including (i) funding Portfolio Investments; (ii) paying Management Fees; (iii) paying Organizational Expenses and Fund Expenses; (iv) repaying amounts borrowed under the Subscription Credit Facility; (v) funding reserves, escrows, or holdbacks; and (vi) satisfying any other obligations of the Partnership.
2003: 
2004: **[Section 4.3 --- Funding Mechanics]{.underline}**
2005: 
2006: \(a\) All capital contributions shall be made by each Partner by wire transfer of immediately available funds to such account or accounts at Ridgeway Trust Company (the Partnership\'s custodian), or such other account as the General Partner may designate in the applicable Capital Call, on or before the funding date specified in such Capital Call.
2007: 
2008: \(b\) In lieu of or in advance of issuing a Capital Call, the General Partner may draw upon the Subscription Credit Facility to fund Portfolio Investments, pay expenses, or satisfy other Partnership obligations, as set forth in Section 4.8. Amounts drawn under the Subscription Credit Facility shall be repaid from the proceeds of Capital Calls subsequently issued to the Partners.
2009: 
2010: \(c\) The General Partner shall maintain records of all capital contributions received from each Partner and shall provide each Partner with a confirmation of the amount contributed promptly following each funding date.
2011: 
2012: **[Section 4.4 --- Overcalls]{.underline}**
2013: 
2014: In the event that a Partner fails to fund all or any portion of a Capital Call when due (and thereby becomes a Defaulting Partner under Section 4.9), the General Partner may, at its discretion, offer the non-defaulting Partners the right to fund the unfunded amount of the Defaulting Partner on a pro rata basis (based on the relative Capital Commitments of the non-defaulting Partners who elect to participate), or on such other basis as the General Partner may determine. No non-defaulting Partner shall be obligated to fund any portion of a Defaulting Partner\'s share, and any overcall shall be entirely at the election of each non-defaulting Partner. Amounts contributed by non-defaulting Partners in respect of a defaulted amount shall be treated as additional capital contributions by such non-defaulting Partners for all purposes of this Agreement, including for purposes of the distribution waterfall and the allocation of Net Profits and Net Losses.
2015: 
2016: **[Section 4.5 --- Subsequent Close Equalization]{.underline}**
2017: 
2018: \(a\) Each Limited Partner admitted at a Subsequent Close shall pay to the Partnership, on the date of such Subsequent Close, an equalization contribution equal to such Limited Partner\'s pro rata share (based on its Capital Commitment as a proportion of Aggregate Commitments after giving effect to its admission) of all Capital Calls previously funded by the existing Partners, together with interest thereon at the rate of eight percent (8%) per annum, compounded annually, from the date each prior Capital Call was funded through the date of such Subsequent Close.
