7477: **Economic Treatment of Excused Investments.** If BFO exercises its excuse right with respect to a particular investment, BFO\'s unfunded Capital Commitment should be reduced dollar-for-dollar by the amount of the excused capital call (i.e., BFO would not be required to fund its pro rata share of that investment, and its aggregate unfunded commitment would be reduced accordingly). BFO would not participate in any distributions or profits attributable to the excused investment. This is the standard mechanism for excuse rights and ensures that the excused LP is neither burdened by nor benefits from the excused investment.
7478: 
7479: **Cap on Excused Investments.** We anticipate that the GP will seek to impose a cap on the aggregate amount of investments from which BFO may be excused, expressed as a percentage of BFO\'s Capital Commitment. This is standard market practice, as the GP has a legitimate interest in ensuring that each LP funds a meaningful share of the Fund\'s investment portfolio and cannot use the excuse mechanism to effectively reduce its commitment below a minimum threshold.
7480: 
7481: The typical market range for excuse caps is 10%--25% of an LP\'s Capital Commitment. We recommend that BFO propose a cap of 25%, which would permit BFO to exercise excuse rights with respect to investments aggregating up to \$18,750,000 (\$75,000,000 × 25%). We anticipate that the GP may counter at a lower cap of 15%, which would limit excused investments to \$11,250,000 (\$75,000,000 × 15%). We consider a 15% cap to be acceptable as a fallback position, given the relatively low likelihood that the Fund would make a significant number of investments in the specified categories given its North American commercial real estate focus.
7482: 
7483: We have prepared a separate Excuse Rights Analysis Memorandum providing a detailed legal analysis of the enforceability and structure of excuse provisions under Delaware law and current market practice, which we will deliver to BFO upon completion.
7484: 
7485: **[VIII. Key Person Provisions]{.underline}**
7486: 
7487: **A. LPA Baseline Key Person Clause**
7488: 
7489: The LPA identifies two individuals as \"Key Persons\" for purposes of the Fund\'s key person provisions: (i) Conrad J. Ellsworth, Co-Founder, Managing Partner, and Chief Executive Officer of MPCA; and (ii) Priya Narayan, Co-Founder, Managing Partner, and Chief Investment Officer of MPCA. Messrs. Ellsworth and Narayan are the founders of MPCA and have been the principal decision-makers for all prior MPCA funds (Funds I--III). Their continued involvement is a critical element of BFO\'s investment thesis for Fund IV.
7490: 
7491: A \"Key Person Event\" is triggered under the LPA if either Ellsworth or Narayan ceases to devote \"substantially all\" of his or her business time and attention to the affairs of MPCA and Fund IV. The LPA defines \"substantially all\" as devoting at least 75% of such person\'s business time to Fund IV-related activities, inclusive of MPCA management activities that benefit Fund IV. The 75% threshold is standard and provides reasonable latitude for the Key Persons to engage in limited outside activities (such as industry board memberships, speaking engagements, and charitable activities) without triggering a Key Person Event.
7492: 
7493: We note that the Key Person provision is structured as a disjunctive trigger --- that is, the departure or reduced involvement of *either* Ellsworth *or* Narayan (not both) would trigger a Key Person Event. This is favorable to BFO, as it provides protection against the loss of either founder, rather than requiring the departure of both before the key person protections are activated.
7494: 
7495: **Consequences of a Key Person Event.** Upon the occurrence of a Key Person Event, the following consequences ensue:
7496: 
7497: > \(a\) The Investment Period is automatically suspended for a period of 180 calendar days (the \"Key Person Suspension Period\"). During the Suspension Period, the GP may not make any new investments on behalf of the Fund, though it may continue to fund previously committed investments and Fund Expenses.
7498: >
7499: > \(b\) During the Key Person Suspension Period, the GP may propose one or more replacement key persons for approval by the LPAC. The GP must provide the LPAC with a written proposal identifying the proposed replacement, including a description of the proposed replacement\'s qualifications, experience, and intended role. The LPAC may approve or reject the proposed replacement in its sole discretion.
7500: >
7501: > \(c\) If the LPAC approves a replacement key person within the 180-day Suspension Period, the Investment Period resumes and continues for its remaining duration as if no Key Person Event had occurred.
7502: >
7503: > \(d\) If no replacement key person is approved by the LPAC within the 180-day Suspension Period, the Investment Period terminates permanently, and the GP may not make any further new investments on behalf of the Fund.
7504: 
7505: We note that the LPA does not provide individual Limited Partners with any right to cease capital calls during the Key Person Suspension Period. The suspension operates at the Fund level only --- the GP is prohibited from making new investments, but capital calls for Fund Expenses, follow-on investments, and reserves may continue. Individual LPs cannot unilaterally elect to cease funding capital calls during the suspension.
7506: 
7507: **B. Side-Letter Recommendation**
7508: 
7509: We recommend that BFO negotiate an enhanced key person provision through its side letter. Specifically, we propose the following:
7510: 
7511: > \(a\) Upon the occurrence of a Key Person Event with respect to either Ellsworth or Narayan, the Investment Period would be subject to a suspension of 90 calendar days (rather than the LPA\'s 180-day suspension) during which BFO may evaluate the situation and the GP\'s proposed remediation.
7512: >
7513: > \(b\) During the 90-day suspension period, BFO would have the unilateral right to elect, by written notice to the GP, to cease participating in future capital calls for new investments. If BFO elects to exercise this right, BFO\'s unfunded Capital Commitment would be reduced to zero (or, alternatively, BFO\'s commitment to fund future capital calls would be limited to previously committed investments and Fund Expenses only).
7514: >
7515: > \(c\) This individualized suspension right would operate independently of the LPAC process described in the base LPA. That is, even if the LPAC approves a replacement key person and the Fund-level Investment Period resumes, BFO would retain the right to have elected not to participate in future new investments.
7516: 
7517: This enhanced key person provision is a stronger right than the LPA baseline, which only provides for a Fund-level suspension and requires LPAC action. The individualized suspension right gives BFO direct control over its commitment in the event of a Key Person Event, without requiring BFO to rely on the LPAC (on which BFO may not have a seat, as discussed in Section XI.A below).
7518: 
7519: We anticipate that the GP may push back on the concept of an individualized suspension right, as it could create disparate treatment among LPs and potentially reduce the Fund\'s available capital during a critical transitional period. We recommend discussing fallback positions with BFO during the strategy call scheduled for February 5, 2024. Potential fallback positions include: (i) accepting the 180-day suspension period (rather than 90 days) but retaining BFO\'s unilateral election right; (ii) limiting BFO\'s election to a right to reduce (rather than eliminate) its future commitment; or (iii) conditioning BFO\'s election on the GP\'s failure to secure LPAC approval of a replacement key person within the 180-day period.
7520: 
7521: **[IX. Default Remedies]{.underline}**
7522: 
7523: **A. LP Default Provisions**
7524: 
7525: The LPA contains a detailed set of provisions governing the consequences of a Limited Partner\'s failure to fund a capital call (an \"LP Default\"). Understanding these provisions is important for BFO\'s operational planning and cash management, as the consequences of a default are severe.
7526: 
7527: **Triggering Event.** An LP Default is triggered if a Limited Partner fails to fund its pro rata share of a capital call within ten (10) business days of the funding date specified in the capital call notice. This is a hard deadline --- the LPA does not provide for any grace period beyond the 10-business-day notice period already built into the capital call mechanics. However, the LPA does provide for a separate cure period after a default has been triggered.
7528: 
7529: **Cure Period.** If an LP fails to fund by the funding date, the GP is required to deliver a written notice of default to the affected LP within five (5) business days following the missed funding date. Upon receipt of the notice of default, the defaulting LP has an additional five (5) business days to cure the default by funding the full amount of the missed capital call, together with any default interest that has accrued from the original funding date through the date of the cure payment.
7530: 
7531: **Consequences of an Uncured Default.** If the LP fails to cure the default within the five-business-day cure period, the GP may, in its sole discretion, impose any or all of the following remedies:
7532: 
7533: > \(a\) **Capital Account Forfeiture.** The defaulting LP\'s interest in the Fund is subject to forfeiture of up to 50% of its capital account balance. This is a punitive measure designed to deter defaults and compensate non-defaulting LPs and the Fund for the disruption caused by the default. The 50% forfeiture rate is at the high end of the market range, which typically falls between 25% and 50%. We note that a 50% forfeiture on BFO\'s \$75,000,000 commitment could represent a forfeiture of up to \$37,500,000 of capital account value (assuming BFO\'s full commitment has been called and funded at the time of the default), which would constitute a catastrophic loss.
7534: >
7535: > \(b\) **Default Interest.** The GP may charge interest on the unfunded capital call amount at a rate equal to the lesser of (i) 18% per annum, or (ii) the maximum rate permitted by applicable law. Default interest accrues from the original funding date specified in the capital call notice through the date on which the defaulting LP cures the default or the GP exercises its other remedies. The 18% per annum default interest rate is within the market range (typically 12%--18%) but represents a meaningful cost of a default.
7536: >
7537: > \(c\) **Legal Remedies.** The GP may pursue any and all legal remedies available to it under the LPA, the defaulting LP\'s Subscription Agreement, and applicable law, including an action for specific performance or damages. The LPA provides that the prevailing party in any such proceeding shall be entitled to recover its reasonable attorneys\' fees and costs from the non-prevailing party.
7538: >
7539: > \(d\) **Overcall of Non-Defaulting LPs.** As discussed in Section IV.B above, the GP may call upon non-defaulting Limited Partners to fund the defaulting LP\'s shortfall, subject to the 125% overcall limitation.
7540: 
7541: We note that the LPA does not include a \"pay-to-play\" or interest downgrade mechanism as an alternative to outright forfeiture. In some fund LPAs, a defaulting LP\'s interest is converted from a full participating interest to a non-voting, non-participating interest (sometimes referred to as a \"penalty box\" or \"zombie\" interest), which reduces the defaulting LP\'s economic rights but does not result in outright forfeiture of capital. The absence of such an intermediate remedy in Fund IV\'s LPA means that the consequences of a default are binary --- either the LP cures the default within the cure period, or it faces the full suite of punitive consequences described above.
7542: 
7543: **B. Recommendation.** While the default remedies in the LPA are aggressive, they are within the range of market practice for institutional PE funds and serve the legitimate purpose of deterring defaults and protecting the Fund and non-defaulting LPs from the consequences of an LP\'s failure to fund. We advise BFO to ensure that it maintains adequate liquidity and operational procedures to timely fund all capital calls issued by the GP throughout the life of the Fund.
7544: 
7545: We do not recommend side-letter negotiation on the default remedies provisions. In our experience, the GP is unlikely to agree to modifications to the default provisions for a single LP, as the uniformity of default remedies across all LPs is important for the structural integrity of the Fund and the GP\'s ability to manage LP defaults consistently. BFO should instead focus its attention on establishing robust internal processes for monitoring and responding to capital call notices within the required funding periods.
7546: 
7547: **[X. Transfer Restrictions]{.underline}**
7548: 
7549: **A. LPA Baseline**
7550: 
7551: The LPA imposes significant restrictions on the transferability of LP interests. The key transfer provisions are as follows:
7552: 
7553: **General Prohibition.** LP interests in the Fund are not transferable without the prior written consent of the General Partner. The GP may grant or withhold such consent in its sole and absolute discretion, and the GP is not required to provide any reason or basis for withholding consent. This is a broad restriction that effectively gives the GP a veto right over any proposed transfer.
7554: 
7555: **Affiliate Transfer Exception.** The LPA provides a limited exception for transfers to affiliates of the transferring LP. An LP may transfer all or a portion of its interest to an \"affiliate\" (as defined in the LPA) without GP consent, provided that: (i) the transferring LP provides the GP with at least 30 days\' prior written notice of the proposed transfer, (ii) the GP\'s consent to the transfer is obtained (which consent may not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed), and (iii) the transferee affiliate executes a joinder agreement and becomes bound by all provisions of the LPA. We note that, while the LPA states that GP consent for affiliate transfers may not be \"unreasonably withheld,\" this standard still provides the GP with meaningful discretion to block a proposed transfer on reasonable grounds.
7556: 
7557: **Transfers by Operation of Law.** The LPA recognizes transfers by operation of law (e.g., in connection with a merger, estate administration, or court order) as an exception to the general transfer restriction, provided that the transferee complies with applicable securities laws and the other requirements of the LPA.
7558: 
7559: **General Conditions.** Any transfer of an LP interest, whether pursuant to the general consent requirement, the affiliate exception, or by operation of law, must satisfy the following conditions: (i) the transfer must comply with all applicable federal and state securities laws, including the Securities Act of 1933, as amended, and applicable state blue sky laws; (ii) the transfer must not cause the Fund to be treated as a \"publicly traded partnership\" within the meaning of Section 7704 of the Internal Revenue Code; and (iii) the transfer must not cause any material adverse tax consequence to the Fund or any other Limited Partner, as determined by the GP in consultation with the Fund\'s tax advisors.
7560: 
7561: The LPA does not include a right of first refusal in favor of other Limited Partners --- that is, existing LPs do not have the right to purchase a transferring LP\'s interest before it is transferred to a third party. Additionally, the LPA does not include drag-along or tag-along rights, which would be unusual for a limited partnership fund of this type.
7562: 
7563: **B. Side-Letter Recommendation**
7564: 
7565: We recommend that BFO negotiate a side-letter provision permitting BFO to transfer its LP interest to any \"Hargrove Family Entity\" without the consent of the General Partner, subject only to compliance with applicable securities laws and the requirement that the transfer not cause adverse tax consequences to the Fund or other Limited Partners.
7566: 
7567: For purposes of the side letter, \"Hargrove Family Entity\" should be defined broadly to include: (i) any trust or estate established for the benefit of one or more members of the Hargrove family (defined to include Julian Hargrove, his spouse, his lineal descendants, and any trust or estate for the primary benefit of any such person); (ii) any limited partnership, limited liability company, or other entity wholly owned or controlled (directly or indirectly) by one or more members of the Hargrove family; and (iii) any charitable foundation or donor-advised fund established by one or more members of the Hargrove family. The definition should be drafted with sufficient breadth to accommodate BFO\'s current estate planning structure as well as any future changes to the Hargrove family\'s wealth planning arrangements.
7568: 
7569: This provision addresses BFO\'s estate planning and family wealth structuring needs, which may require the transfer of BFO\'s LP interest to one or more family trusts, holding companies, or other entities during the life of the Fund. Without this provision, any such transfer would require GP consent, introducing delay and uncertainty into BFO\'s estate planning process.
7570: 
7571: We anticipate that the GP will be willing to agree to this provision subject to reasonable conditions, including (i) execution of a joinder agreement by the transferee Hargrove Family Entity, (ii) compliance with applicable securities laws, (iii) delivery of a tax opinion confirming no adverse tax consequences, and (iv) advance written notice to the GP (typically 15--30 days). These conditions are reasonable and should be acceptable to BFO.
7572: 
7573: **[XI. Governance and Reporting]{.underline}**
7574: 
7575: **A. Limited Partner Advisory Committee (LPAC)**
7576: 
7577: The LPA provides for the formation of a Limited Partner Advisory Committee (\"LPAC\") composed of representatives of five to seven (5--7) Limited Partners. LPAC members are selected by the General Partner from among the Fund\'s largest investors. The LPA does not specify a minimum commitment threshold for LPAC membership but states that the GP will \"endeavor to select LPAC members from among the Fund\'s most significant investors.\"
7578: 
7579: The LPAC\'s responsibilities under the LPA are limited to the following matters:
7580: 
7581: > \(a\) Review and approval of conflicts of interest between the GP (or its affiliates) and the Fund, including co-investment transactions between the Fund and other MPCA-managed funds;
7582: >
7583: > \(b\) Resolution of valuation disputes with respect to the Fund\'s portfolio investments;
7584: >
7585: > \(c\) Approval of replacement key persons following a Key Person Event (as discussed in Section VIII above); and
7586: >
7587: > \(d\) Review and approval of transactions between the Fund and GP affiliates, including any fee-sharing arrangements or allocation of investment opportunities among MPCA-managed funds.
7588: 
7589: The LPA expressly provides that LPAC members owe no fiduciary duty to any other Limited Partner or to the Fund in their capacity as LPAC members. This is standard practice and is intended to protect LPAC members from liability for actions taken in good faith in their advisory capacity.
7590: 
7591: We note that, at a \$75,000,000 commitment level, BFO may not be entitled to an LPAC seat. LPAC seats are typically allocated to the Fund\'s largest investors, and for a fund of this size (with a target of \$1,500,000,000), we would expect the GP to allocate LPAC seats to investors committing \$100,000,000 or more. BFO\'s \$75,000,000 commitment, while meaningful, may fall below the threshold at which the GP offers LPAC representation. We recommend that BFO raise the question of LPAC representation during the subscription process and, if a seat is not offered, consider negotiating a side-letter right to designate an observer to the LPAC (i.e., the right to attend LPAC meetings in a non-voting, observer capacity). An LPAC observer right is increasingly common for investors at BFO\'s commitment level and would provide BFO with valuable insight into the Fund\'s governance activities.
7592: 
7593: **B. Reporting. LPA Standard Reporting.** The LPA establishes the following minimum reporting obligations for the GP:
7594: 
7595: > \(a\) **Quarterly Financial Statements.** Unaudited financial statements (including a balance sheet, income statement, and statement of cash flows) within sixty (60) days after the end of each fiscal quarter.
7596: >
7597: > \(b\) **Annual Audited Financial Statements.** Audited financial statements, prepared in accordance with U.S. GAAP by Brockton Marsh & Associates LLP, within one hundred twenty (120) days after the end of each fiscal year.
7598: >
7599: > \(c\) **Capital Account Statements.** A capital account statement for each Limited Partner, reflecting the LP\'s capital contributions, distributions, and capital account balance, accompanying each distribution.
7600: >
7601: > \(d\) **Schedule K-1s.** An IRS Schedule K-1 (Form 1065) for each Limited Partner within one hundred twenty (120) days after the end of each fiscal year.
7602: 
7603: **Side-Letter Enhanced Reporting Recommendations.** The LPA\'s standard reporting obligations, while adequate, fall below what we consider to be best-in-class reporting for an institutional LP of BFO\'s sophistication and commitment size. We recommend that BFO negotiate the following enhanced reporting provisions through its side letter:
7604: 
7605: > \(a\) **Quarterly Portfolio-Level Reports.** In addition to the standard quarterly financial statements, the GP should provide BFO with detailed portfolio-level reports on a quarterly basis, including investment-level detail for each portfolio asset (property name, location, acquisition date, acquisition cost, current appraised value, debt outstanding, occupancy rate, net operating income, and capital expenditure activity). These portfolio-level reports should be delivered within forty-five (45) days after the end of each fiscal quarter (compared to the 60-day standard in the LPA for general quarterly financials).
7606: >
7607: > \(b\) **Accelerated Annual Financial Statements.** Audited annual financial statements within ninety (90) days after the end of each fiscal year (compared to the 120-day standard in the LPA). The 120-day timeline is generous by institutional standards, and a 90-day timeline is achievable with adequate planning by the GP and fund administrator.
7608: >
7609: > \(c\) **ESG Reporting.** An annual environmental, social, and governance (\"ESG\") report for the Fund, covering topics such as energy consumption, carbon emissions, water usage, waste management, diversity and inclusion metrics, and governance practices across the Fund\'s portfolio. ESG reporting is increasingly expected by institutional investors and is consistent with BFO\'s stated commitment to responsible investing principles.
7610: >
7611: > \(d\) **Accelerated Schedule K-1s.** Delivery of Schedule K-1s within seventy-five (75) days after the end of each fiscal year (compared to the 120-day standard in the LPA). We note that this is an aggressive ask --- the 120-day K-1 delivery timeline reflects the complexity of preparing partnership tax returns for a multi-asset real estate fund with investments across multiple state and local tax jurisdictions. The 75-day timeline may be resisted by the GP and the fund administrator (Granite Ledger Fund Services LLC), and BFO should be prepared to accept a compromise at 90 days if the GP and administrator indicate that 75 days is not operationally feasible.
7612: 
7613: **C. LP Voting Rights and GP Removal**
7614: 
7615: The LPA establishes the following voting thresholds for significant Fund governance actions:
7616: 
7617: **GP Removal for Cause.** The GP may be removed by the affirmative vote of Limited Partners holding at least 75% of the aggregate Capital Commitments (a \"super-majority vote\"). Removal \"for cause\" is limited to the following grounds: (i) fraud by the GP or its principals; (ii) willful misconduct by the GP or its principals; (iii) gross negligence by the GP or its principals in the management of the Fund; or (iv) a material and uncured breach of the LPA by the GP. We note that the \"for cause\" standard is defined narrowly and sets a high bar for GP removal --- ordinary negligence, poor investment performance, or disagreements over investment strategy would not constitute grounds for removal under this standard.
7618: 
7619: **No \"Without Cause\" GP Removal.** The LPA does not provide for removal of the GP \"without cause\" (i.e., at the election of the LP super-majority for any or no reason). This is less favorable to LPs than some institutional fund LPAs, which include a \"no fault\" removal right exercisable by a super-majority of LPs (typically 75%--80% in interest). The absence of a \"without cause\" removal right means that, absent fraud, willful misconduct, gross negligence, or material breach, the LPs cannot remove the GP even if the Fund\'s investment performance is materially below expectations.
7620: 
7621: **Fund Dissolution.** The Fund may be dissolved by the affirmative vote of Limited Partners holding more than 50% of the aggregate Capital Commitments (a \"majority vote\"). This is a standard dissolution threshold.
7622: 
7623: **Amendments to the LPA.** Amendments to the LPA that would adversely affect the economic rights of any Limited Partner require the consent of each affected LP. This provides important protection against unilateral modifications to BFO\'s economic terms.
7624: 
7625: **BFO\'s Voting Power.** At the target fund size of \$1,500,000,000, BFO\'s \$75,000,000 commitment would represent 5.0% of the total Capital Commitments. This means that BFO alone would not have blocking power on any vote requiring a majority or super-majority of LPs. BFO would need to coordinate with other LPs to achieve the requisite voting thresholds for GP removal (75%) or fund dissolution (50%). However, BFO\'s consent would be required for any amendment that adversely affects BFO\'s individual economic rights, regardless of the votes of other LPs.
7626: 
7627: **[XII. Most Favored Nation (MFN) Rights]{.underline}**
7628: 
7629: **A. LPA Baseline**
7630: 
7631: The base LPA does not contain a most favored nation (\"MFN\") provision. The LPA acknowledges that the General Partner may enter into side letters with individual Limited Partners granting \"additional or modified terms\" without the consent of other Limited Partners. This is a standard side-letter authorization provision, but it does not include any mechanism for disclosure of side-letter terms to other LPs or any right for other LPs to elect the benefit of more favorable terms granted to another LP.
7632: 
7633: The absence of an MFN provision in the base LPA means that, without a side-letter MFN right, BFO would have no visibility into the terms granted to other LPs and no ability to \"level up\" to more favorable terms granted to a comparably-sized or smaller investor. Given the importance of MFN rights in ensuring equitable treatment among investors, this is a significant gap that must be addressed through BFO\'s side letter.
7634: 
7635: **B. Side-Letter Recommendation**
7636: 
7637: We recommend that BFO negotiate a most favored nation clause in its side letter. The MFN clause should entitle BFO to elect the benefit of any economic or governance term that the GP grants to any other Limited Partner committing \$50,000,000 or more to the Fund. The \$50,000,000 MFN threshold is designed to capture all investors at or above BFO\'s general commitment tier while excluding smaller investors who may receive standard terms without negotiation.
7638: 
7639: **Proposed MFN Mechanics:**
7640: 
7641: > \(a\) Within fifteen (15) business days following the close at which BFO is admitted to the Fund, the GP shall deliver to BFO a redacted summary (the \"Side Letter Summary\") of all material economic and governance terms contained in side letters entered into with Limited Partners committing \$50,000,000 or more to the Fund. The redacted summary need not identify the relevant LPs by name but must describe the substance of each material term with sufficient specificity to permit BFO to make an informed election.
7642: >
7643: > \(b\) BFO shall have a period of twenty (20) business days following receipt of the Side Letter Summary (the \"MFN Election Period\") to notify the GP in writing of any terms that BFO elects to incorporate into its own side letter.
7644: >
7645: > \(c\) Any terms elected by BFO during the MFN Election Period shall be deemed incorporated into BFO\'s side letter and shall be effective retroactively to the date of BFO\'s admission to the Fund.
7646: >
7647: > \(d\) If the GP enters into any additional side letters after the close at which BFO is admitted (e.g., at subsequent closings), the GP shall deliver a supplemental Side Letter Summary to BFO within fifteen (15) business days following each subsequent close, and BFO shall have an additional twenty (20) business day election period with respect to any new terms.
7648: 
7649: **Proposed MFN Carve-Outs.** The MFN clause should include carve-outs for the following categories of terms, which BFO would not be entitled to elect:
7650: 
7651: > \(i\) **Anchor Investor Terms.** Terms granted to Limited Partners committing \$200,000,000 or more to the Fund (\"Anchor Investors\"). At the target fund size of \$1,500,000,000, a \$200,000,000 commitment would represent approximately 13.33% of the target fund size. Anchor Investors typically receive more favorable economics (e.g., deeper management fee reductions, enhanced co-investment rights, advisory committee seats) that reflect the scale and strategic importance of their commitment. It is standard practice to exclude Anchor Investor terms from MFN elections, and BFO should expect the GP to insist on this carve-out.
7652: >
7653: > \(ii\) **Regulatory Accommodations.** Terms granted to Limited Partners that are ERISA plan investors, tax-exempt investors (including state pension funds, endowments, and foundations), or governmental plan investors, where such terms are granted solely for the purpose of addressing the regulatory or legal requirements applicable to such investors. These regulatory accommodations are investor-specific and are not relevant to BFO as a non-tax-exempt family office.
7654: >
7655: > \(iii\) **GP Affiliate Terms.** Terms granted to entities that are affiliates of the GP or MPCA, including any co-investment vehicles or parallel funds managed by MPCA. GP affiliate terms are structural rather than negotiated and are appropriately excluded from MFN elections.
7656: 
7657: The MFN clause is critical given BFO\'s position as a meaningful but not anchor-level investor. At 5.0% of the target fund size, BFO has sufficient commitment size to warrant favorable terms, but is not so large as to command the most preferential treatment available to the Fund\'s largest investors. The MFN clause ensures that BFO is not disadvantaged relative to similarly-sized LPs that may negotiate more aggressively or more effectively on particular points.
7658: 
7659: We have prepared an internal MFN Provision Comparison Matrix benchmarking Fund IV\'s proposed MFN framework against comparable provisions in recent fund formation engagements, which we will make available to BFO upon request.
7660: 
7661: **[XIII. Co-Investment Rights]{.underline}**
7662: 
7663: **A. LPA Baseline**
7664: 
7665: The base LPA provides the General Partner with discretion to offer co-investment opportunities to Limited Partners on a deal-by-deal basis. Section 6.4 of the LPA states that the GP \"may, in its sole discretion, offer co-investment opportunities to one or more Limited Partners in connection with specific Investments.\" However, the LPA does not create any entitlement or right for any Limited Partner to receive co-investment opportunities. The allocation of co-investment opportunities is entirely within the GP\'s discretion, and the GP is not required to offer co-investments to any particular LP or to allocate co-investments on a pro rata or other formulaic basis.
7666: 
7667: The LPA does not specify the fee or carry structure applicable to co-investments. This means that, absent a side-letter provision, the GP could offer co-investment opportunities on terms that include management fees and/or carried interest, which would reduce the economic benefit of the co-investment to the participating LP. In the current market environment, co-investments offered at full fees and carry provide limited incremental value to LPs relative to their primary fund commitment.
7668: 
7669: **B. Side-Letter Recommendation**
7670: 
7671: We recommend that BFO negotiate a pro rata co-investment right through its side letter. Specifically, we propose the following terms:
7672: 
7673: > \(a\) **Pro Rata Co-Investment Right.** The GP shall offer BFO a co-investment opportunity on each Fund IV investment with aggregate equity capitalization exceeding \$100,000,000. BFO\'s maximum co-investment allocation shall be equal to BFO\'s percentage share of the Fund\'s total Capital Commitments (approximately 5.0% at target fund size) applied to the available co-investment amount (i.e., the amount of the investment in excess of Fund IV\'s allocation).
7674: >
7675: > \(b\) **No Fee / No Carry.** Co-investments made by BFO shall be free of management fees and carried interest. This is increasingly the market standard for LP co-investments and is a significant economic benefit to BFO, as it effectively allows BFO to deploy additional capital alongside the Fund at zero incremental cost. Over the life of the Fund, the elimination of fees and carry on co-investments could represent hundreds of thousands of dollars (or more) in economic benefit, depending on the volume and profitability of co-investment opportunities.
7676: >
7677: > \(c\) **Election Period.** BFO shall have ten (10) business days from receipt of a co-investment offer to elect to participate (in whole or in part) or to decline the opportunity. If BFO declines or fails to respond within the election period, the GP may offer the co-investment to other LPs or third parties without further obligation to BFO.
7678: >

7680: 
7681: Co-investment rights at no fee/no carry are increasingly standard for commitments of BFO\'s size and serve as a meaningful value-add to BFO\'s overall relationship with the Fund. The ability to deploy additional capital at zero incremental cost improves BFO\'s blended fee load across its total exposure to Fund IV investments and can meaningfully enhance net returns. We anticipate that the GP will be willing to agree to the concept of co-investment rights, though it may seek to condition the right on (i) minimum co-investment amounts, (ii) the GP\'s right to allocate co-investments among multiple requesting LPs, and (iii) BFO\'s ability to execute co-investments within the required timeframe. 7685: **A. Tax Structure**
7686: 
7687: Fund IV is organized as a Delaware limited partnership and is treated as a partnership for U.S. federal income tax purposes. As a partnership, Fund IV is not subject to entity-level federal income tax; instead, each partner (including each LP) is taxed on its allocable share of the Fund\'s income, gain, loss, deduction, and credit items, as reported on the annual Schedule K-1. This pass-through tax structure is the standard structure for institutional PE funds and is appropriate for BFO.

7691: **UBTI Considerations.** The LPA contains standard provisions addressing unrelated business taxable income (\"UBTI\") for tax-exempt investors. The LPA contains standard tax distribution provisions that are designed to provide partners with cash distributions sufficient to cover their estimated tax liabilities attributable to the Fund\'s income, including state and local taxes. These tax distributions are made on a quarterly estimated basis and are credited against the partner\'s share of subsequent profit distributions.
