lines.text: **Economic Treatment of Excused Investments.** If BFO exercises its excuse right with respect to a particular investment, BFO\'s unfunded Capital Commitment should be reduced dollar-for-dollar by the amount of the excused capital call (i.e., BFO would not be required to fund its pro rata share of that investment, and its aggregate unfunded commitment would be reduced accordingly). BFO would not participate in any distributions or profits attributable to the excused investment. This is the standard mechanism for excuse rights and ensures that the excused LP is neither burdened by nor benefits from the excused investment.

**Cap on Excused Investments.** We anticipate that the GP will seek to impose a cap on the aggregate amount of investments from which BFO may be excused, expressed as a percentage of BFO\'s Capital Commitment. This is standard market practice, as the GP has a legitimate interest in ensuring that each LP funds a meaningful share of the Fund\'s investment portfolio and cannot use the excuse mechanism to effectively reduce its commitment below a minimum threshold.

The typical market range for excuse caps is 10%--25% of an LP\'s Capital Commitment. We recommend that BFO propose a cap of 25%, which would permit BFO to exercise excuse rights with respect to investments aggregating up to \$18,750,000 (\$75,000,000 × 25%). We anticipate that the GP may counter at a lower cap of 15%, which would limit excused investments to \$11,250,000 (\$75,000,000 × 15%). We consider a 15% cap to be acceptable as a fallback position, given the relatively low likelihood that the Fund would make a significant number of investments in the specified categories given its North American commercial real estate focus.

We have prepared a separate Excuse Rights Analysis Memorandum providing a detailed legal analysis of the enforceability and structure of excuse provisions under Delaware law and current market practice, which we will deliver to BFO upon completion.
**[VIII. Key Person Provisions]{.underline}**
**A. LPA Baseline Key Person Clause**

The LPA identifies two individuals as \"Key Persons\" for purposes of the Fund\'s key person provisions: (i) Conrad J. Ellsworth, Co-Founder, Managing Partner, and Chief Executive Officer of MPCA; and (ii) Priya Narayan, Co-Founder, Managing Partner, and Chief Investment Officer of MPCA. Messrs. Ellsworth and Narayan are the founders of MPCA and have been the principal decision-makers for all prior MPCA funds (Funds I--III). Their continued involvement is a critical element of BFO\'s investment thesis for Fund IV.

A \"Key Person Event\" is triggered under the LPA if either Ellsworth or Narayan ceases to devote \"substantially all\" of his or her business time and attention to the affairs of MPCA and Fund IV. The LPA defines \"substantially all\" as devoting at least 75% of such person\'s business time to Fund IV-related activities, inclusive of MPCA management activities that benefit Fund IV. The 75% threshold is standard and provides reasonable latitude for the Key Persons to engage in limited outside activities (such as industry board memberships, speaking engagements, and charitable activities) without triggering a Key Person Event.

We note that the Key Person provision is structured as a disjunctive trigger --- that is, the departure or reduced involvement of *either* Ellsworth *or* Narayan (not both) would trigger a Key Person Event. This is favorable to BFO, as it provides protection against the loss of either founder, rather than requiring the departure of both before the key person protections are activated.
**Consequences of a Key Person Event.** Upon the occurrence of a Key Person Event, the following consequences ensue:

> \(a\) The Investment Period is automatically suspended for a period of 180 calendar days (the \"Key Person Suspension Period\"). During the Suspension Period, the GP may not make any new investments on behalf of the Fund, though it may continue to fund previously committed investments and Fund Expenses.

> \(b\) During the Key Person Suspension Period, the GP may propose one or more replacement key persons for approval by the LPAC. The GP must provide the LPAC with a written proposal identifying the proposed replacement, including a description of the proposed replacement\'s qualifications, experience, and intended role. The LPAC may approve or reject the proposed replacement in its sole discretion.

> \(c\) If the LPAC approves a replacement key person within the 180-day Suspension Period, the Investment Period resumes and continues for its remaining duration as if no Key Person Event had occurred.

> \(d\) If no replacement key person is approved by the LPAC within the 180-day Suspension Period, the Investment Period terminates permanently, and the GP may not make any further new investments on behalf of the Fund.

We note that the LPA does not provide individual Limited Partners with any right to cease capital calls during the Key Person Suspension Period. The suspension operates at the Fund level only --- the GP is prohibited from making new investments, but capital calls for Fund Expenses, follow-on investments, and reserves may continue. Individual LPs cannot unilaterally elect to cease funding capital calls during the suspension.
**B. Side-Letter Recommendation**
We recommend that BFO negotiate an enhanced key person provision through its side letter. Specifically, we propose the following:

> \(a\) Upon the occurrence of a Key Person Event with respect to either Ellsworth or Narayan, the Investment Period would be subject to a suspension of 90 calendar days (rather than the LPA\'s 180-day suspension) during which BFO may evaluate the situation and the GP\'s proposed remediation.

> \(b\) During the 90-day suspension period, BFO would have the unilateral right to elect, by written notice to the GP, to cease participating in future capital calls for new investments. If BFO elects to exercise this right, BFO\'s unfunded Capital Commitment would be reduced to zero (or, alternatively, BFO\'s commitment to fund future capital calls would be limited to previously committed investments and Fund Expenses only).

> \(c\) This individualized suspension right would operate independently of the LPAC process described in the base LPA. That is, even if the LPAC approves a replacement key person and the Fund-level Investment Period resumes, BFO would retain the right to have elected not to participate in future new investments.

This enhanced key person provision is a stronger right than the LPA baseline, which only provides for a Fund-level suspension and requires LPAC action. The individualized suspension right gives BFO direct control over its commitment in the event of a Key Person Event, without requiring BFO to rely on the LPAC (on which BFO may not have a seat, as discussed in Section XI.A below).

We anticipate that the GP may push back on the concept of an individualized suspension right, as it could create disparate treatment among LPs and potentially reduce the Fund\'s available capital during a critical transitional period. We recommend discussing fallback positions with BFO during the strategy call scheduled for February 5, 2024. Potential fallback positions include: (i) accepting the 180-day suspension period (rather than 90 days) but retaining BFO\'s unilateral election right; (ii) limiting BFO\'s election to a right to reduce (rather than eliminate) its future commitment; or (iii) conditioning BFO\'s election on the GP\'s failure to secure LPAC approval of a replacement key person within the 180-day period.
**[IX. Default Remedies]{.underline}**
**A. LP Default Provisions**

The LPA contains a detailed set of provisions governing the consequences of a Limited Partner\'s failure to fund a capital call (an \"LP Default\"). Understanding these provisions is important for BFO\'s operational planning and cash management, as the consequences of a default are severe.

**Triggering Event.** An LP Default is triggered if a Limited Partner fails to fund its pro rata share of a capital call within ten (10) business days of the funding date specified in the capital call notice. This is a hard deadline --- the LPA does not provide for any grace period beyond the 10-business-day notice period already built into the capital call mechanics. However, the LPA does provide for a separate cure period after a default has been triggered.

**Cure Period.** If an LP fails to fund by the funding date, the GP is required to deliver a written notice of default to the affected LP within five (5) business days following the missed funding date. Upon receipt of the notice of default, the defaulting LP has an additional five (5) business days to cure the default by funding the full amount of the missed capital call, together with any default interest that has accrued from the original funding date through the date of the cure payment.
**Consequences of an Uncured Default.** If the LP fails to cure the default within the five-business-day cure period, the GP may, in its sole discretion, impose any or all of the following remedies:

> \(a\) **Capital Account Forfeiture.** The defaulting LP\'s interest in the Fund is subject to forfeiture of up to 50% of its capital account balance. This is a punitive measure designed to deter defaults and compensate non-defaulting LPs and the Fund for the disruption caused by the default. The 50% forfeiture rate is at the high end of the market range, which typically falls between 25% and 50%. We note that a 50% forfeiture on BFO\'s \$75,000,000 commitment could represent a forfeiture of up to \$37,500,000 of capital account value (assuming BFO\'s full commitment has been called and funded at the time of the default), which would constitute a catastrophic loss.

> \(b\) **Default Interest.** The GP may charge interest on the unfunded capital call amount at a rate equal to the lesser of (i) 18% per annum, or (ii) the maximum rate permitted by applicable law. Default interest accrues from the original funding date specified in the capital call notice through the date on which the defaulting LP cures the default or the GP exercises its other remedies. The 18% per annum default interest rate is within the market range (typically 12%--18%) but represents a meaningful cost of a default.

> \(c\) **Legal Remedies.** The GP may pursue any and all legal remedies available to it under the LPA, the defaulting LP\'s Subscription Agreement, and applicable law, including an action for specific performance or damages. The LPA provides that the prevailing party in any such proceeding shall be entitled to recover its reasonable attorneys\' fees and costs from the non-prevailing party.

> \(d\) **Overcall of Non-Defaulting LPs.** As discussed in Section IV.B above, the GP may call upon non-defaulting Limited Partners to fund the defaulting LP\'s shortfall, subject to the 125% overcall limitation.

We note that the LPA does not include a \"pay-to-play\" or interest downgrade mechanism as an alternative to outright forfeiture. In some fund LPAs, a defaulting LP\'s interest is converted from a full participating interest to a non-voting, non-participating interest (sometimes referred to as a \"penalty box\" or \"zombie\" interest), which reduces the defaulting LP\'s economic rights but does not result in outright forfeiture of capital. The absence of such an intermediate remedy in Fund IV\'s LPA means that the consequences of a default are binary --- either the LP cures the default within the cure period, or it faces the full suite of punitive consequences described above.

**B. Recommendation.** While the default remedies in the LPA are aggressive, they are within the range of market practice for institutional PE funds and serve the legitimate purpose of deterring defaults and protecting the Fund and non-defaulting LPs from the consequences of an LP\'s failure to fund. We advise BFO to ensure that it maintains adequate liquidity and operational procedures to timely fund all capital calls issued by the GP throughout the life of the Fund.

We do not recommend side-letter negotiation on the default remedies provisions. In our experience, the GP is unlikely to agree to modifications to the default provisions for a single LP, as the uniformity of default remedies across all LPs is important for the structural integrity of the Fund and the GP\'s ability to manage LP defaults consistently. BFO should instead focus its attention on establishing robust internal processes for monitoring and responding to capital call notices within the required funding periods.
**[X. Transfer Restrictions]{.underline}**
**A. LPA Baseline**
The LPA imposes significant restrictions on the transferability of LP interests. The key transfer provisions are as follows:

**General Prohibition.** LP interests in the Fund are not transferable without the prior written consent of the General Partner. The GP may grant or withhold such consent in its sole and absolute discretion, and the GP is not required to provide any reason or basis for withholding consent. This is a broad restriction that effectively gives the GP a veto right over any proposed transfer.

**Affiliate Transfer Exception.** The LPA provides a limited exception for transfers to affiliates of the transferring LP. An LP may transfer all or a portion of its interest to an \"affiliate\" (as defined in the LPA) without GP consent, provided that: (i) the transferring LP provides the GP with at least 30 days\' prior written notice of the proposed transfer, (ii) the GP\'s consent to the transfer is obtained (which consent may not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed), and (iii) the transferee affiliate executes a joinder agreement and becomes bound by all provisions of the LPA. We note that, while the LPA states that GP consent for affiliate transfers may not be \"unreasonably withheld,\" this standard still provides the GP with meaningful discretion to block a proposed transfer on reasonable grounds.

**Transfers by Operation of Law.** The LPA recognizes transfers by operation of law (e.g., in connection with a merger, estate administration, or court order) as an exception to the general transfer restriction, provided that the transferee complies with applicable securities laws and the other requirements of the LPA.

**General Conditions.** Any transfer of an LP interest, whether pursuant to the general consent requirement, the affiliate exception, or by operation of law, must satisfy the following conditions: (i) the transfer must comply with all applicable federal and state securities laws, including the Securities Act of 1933, as amended, and applicable state blue sky laws; (ii) the transfer must not cause the Fund to be treated as a \"publicly traded partnership\" within the meaning of Section 7704 of the Internal Revenue Code; and (iii) the transfer must not cause any material adverse tax consequence to the Fund or any other Limited Partner, as determined by the GP in consultation with the Fund\'s tax advisors.

The LPA does not include a right of first refusal in favor of other Limited Partners --- that is, existing LPs do not have the right to purchase a transferring LP\'s interest before it is transferred to a third party. Additionally, the LPA does not include drag-along or tag-along rights, which would be unusual for a limited partnership fund of this type.
**B. Side-Letter Recommendation**

We recommend that BFO negotiate a side-letter provision permitting BFO to transfer its LP interest to any \"Hargrove Family Entity\" without the consent of the General Partner, subject only to compliance with applicable securities laws and the requirement that the transfer not cause adverse tax consequences to the Fund or other Limited Partners.

For purposes of the side letter, \"Hargrove Family Entity\" should be defined broadly to include: (i) any trust or estate established for the benefit of one or more members of the Hargrove family (defined to include Julian Hargrove, his spouse, his lineal descendants, and any trust or estate for the primary benefit of any such person); (ii) any limited partnership, limited liability company, or other entity wholly owned or controlled (directly or indirectly) by one or more members of the Hargrove family; and (iii) any charitable foundation or donor-advised fund established by one or more members of the Hargrove family. The definition should be drafted with sufficient breadth to accommodate BFO\'s current estate planning structure as well as any future changes to the Hargrove family\'s wealth planning arrangements.

This provision addresses BFO\'s estate planning and family wealth structuring needs, which may require the transfer of BFO\'s LP interest to one or more family trusts, holding companies, or other entities during the life of the Fund. Without this provision, any such transfer would require GP consent, introducing delay and uncertainty into BFO\'s estate planning process.

We anticipate that the GP will be willing to agree to this provision subject to reasonable conditions, including (i) execution of a joinder agreement by the transferee Hargrove Family Entity, (ii) compliance with applicable securities laws, (iii) delivery of a tax opinion confirming no adverse tax consequences, and (iv) advance written notice to the GP (typically 15--30 days). These conditions are reasonable and should be acceptable to BFO.
**[XI. Governance and Reporting]{.underline}**
**A. Limited Partner Advisory Committee (LPAC)**

The LPA provides for the formation of a Limited Partner Advisory Committee (\"LPAC\") composed of representatives of five to seven (5--7) Limited Partners. LPAC members are selected by the General Partner from among the Fund\'s largest investors. The LPA does not specify a minimum commitment threshold for LPAC membership but states that the GP will \"endeavor to select LPAC members from among the Fund\'s most significant investors.\"
The LPAC\'s responsibilities under the LPA are limited to the following matters:
> \(a\) Review and approval of conflicts of interest between the GP (or its affiliates) and the Fund, including co-investment transactions between the Fund and other MPCA-managed funds;
> \(b\) Resolution of valuation disputes with respect to the Fund\'s portfolio investments;
> \(c\) Approval of replacement key persons following a Key Person Event (as discussed in Section VIII above); and
> \(d\) Review and approval of transactions between the Fund and GP affiliates, including any fee-sharing arrangements or allocation of investment opportunities among MPCA-managed funds.

The LPA expressly provides that LPAC members owe no fiduciary duty to any other Limited Partner or to the Fund in their capacity as LPAC members. This is standard practice and is intended to protect LPAC members from liability for actions taken in good faith in their advisory capacity.

We note that, at a \$75,000,000 commitment level, BFO may not be entitled to an LPAC seat. LPAC seats are typically allocated to the Fund\'s largest investors, and for a fund of this size (with a target of \$1,500,000,000), we would expect the GP to allocate LPAC seats to investors committing \$100,000,000 or more. BFO\'s \$75,000,000 commitment, while meaningful, may fall below the threshold at which the GP offers LPAC representation. We recommend that BFO raise the question of LPAC representation during the subscription process and, if a seat is not offered, consider negotiating a side-letter right to designate an observer to the LPAC (i.e., the right to attend LPAC meetings in a non-voting, observer capacity). An LPAC observer right is increasingly common for investors at BFO\'s commitment level and would provide BFO with valuable insight into the Fund\'s governance activities.
**B. Reporting. LPA Standard Reporting.** The LPA establishes the following minimum reporting obligations for the GP:

> \(a\) **Quarterly Financial Statements.** Unaudited financial statements (including a balance sheet, income statement, and statement of cash flows) within sixty (60) days after the end of each fiscal quarter.

> \(b\) **Annual Audited Financial Statements.** Audited financial statements, prepared in accordance with U.S. GAAP by Brockton Marsh & Associates LLP, within one hundred twenty (120) days after the end of each fiscal year.

> \(c\) **Capital Account Statements.** A capital account statement for each Limited Partner, reflecting the LP\'s capital contributions, distributions, and capital account balance, accompanying each distribution.
> \(d\) **Schedule K-1s.** An IRS Schedule K-1 (Form 1065) for each Limited Partner within one hundred twenty (120) days after the end of each fiscal year.

**Side-Letter Enhanced Reporting Recommendations.** The LPA\'s standard reporting obligations, while adequate, fall below what we consider to be best-in-class reporting for an institutional LP of BFO\'s sophistication and commitment size. We recommend that BFO negotiate the following enhanced reporting provisions through its side letter:

> \(a\) **Quarterly Portfolio-Level Reports.** In addition to the standard quarterly financial statements, the GP should provide BFO with detailed portfolio-level reports on a quarterly basis, including investment-level detail for each portfolio asset (property name, location, acquisition date, acquisition cost, current appraised value, debt outstanding, occupancy rate, net operating income, and capital expenditure activity). These portfolio-level reports should be delivered within forty-five (45) days after the end of each fiscal quarter (compared to the 60-day standard in the LPA for general quarterly financials).

> \(b\) **Accelerated Annual Financial Statements.** Audited annual financial statements within ninety (90) days after the end of each fiscal year (compared to the 120-day standard in the LPA). The 120-day timeline is generous by institutional standards, and a 90-day timeline is achievable with adequate planning by the GP and fund administrator.

> \(c\) **ESG Reporting.** An annual environmental, social, and governance (\"ESG\") report for the Fund, covering topics such as energy consumption, carbon emissions, water usage, waste management, diversity and inclusion metrics, and governance practices across the Fund\'s portfolio. ESG reporting is increasingly expected by institutional investors and is consistent with BFO\'s stated commitment to responsible investing principles.

> \(d\) **Accelerated Schedule K-1s.** Delivery of Schedule K-1s within seventy-five (75) days after the end of each fiscal year (compared to the 120-day standard in the LPA). We note that this is an aggressive ask --- the 120-day K-1 delivery timeline reflects the complexity of preparing partnership tax returns for a multi-asset real estate fund with investments across multiple state and local tax jurisdictions. The 75-day timeline may be resisted by the GP and the fund administrator (Granite Ledger Fund Services LLC), and BFO should be prepared to accept a compromise at 90 days if the GP and administrator indicate that 75 days is not operationally feasible.
**C. LP Voting Rights and GP Removal**
The LPA establishes the following voting thresholds for significant Fund governance actions:

**GP Removal for Cause.** The GP may be removed by the affirmative vote of Limited Partners holding at least 75% of the aggregate Capital Commitments (a \"super-majority vote\"). Removal \"for cause\" is limited to the following grounds: (i) fraud by the GP or its principals; (ii) willful misconduct by the GP or its principals; (iii) gross negligence by the GP or its principals in the management of the Fund; or (iv) a material and uncured breach of the LPA by the GP. We note that the \"for cause\" standard is defined narrowly and sets a high bar for GP removal --- ordinary negligence, poor investment performance, or disagreements over investment strategy would not constitute grounds for removal under this standard.

**No \"Without Cause\" GP Removal.** The LPA does not provide for removal of the GP \"without cause\" (i.e., at the election of the LP super-majority for any or no reason). This is less favorable to LPs than some institutional fund LPAs, which include a \"no fault\" removal right exercisable by a super-majority of LPs (typically 75%--80% in interest). The absence of a \"without cause\" removal right means that, absent fraud, willful misconduct, gross negligence, or material breach, the LPs cannot remove the GP even if the Fund\'s investment performance is materially below expectations.

**Fund Dissolution.** The Fund may be dissolved by the affirmative vote of Limited Partners holding more than 50% of the aggregate Capital Commitments (a \"majority vote\"). This is a standard dissolution threshold.

**Amendments to the LPA.** Amendments to the LPA that would adversely affect the economic rights of any Limited Partner require the consent of each affected LP. This provides important protection against unilateral modifications to BFO\'s economic terms.

**BFO\'s Voting Power.** At the target fund size of \$1,500,000,000, BFO\'s \$75,000,000 commitment would represent 5.0% of the total Capital Commitments. This means that BFO alone would not have blocking power on any vote requiring a majority or super-majority of LPs. BFO would need to coordinate with other LPs to achieve the requisite voting thresholds for GP removal (75%) or fund dissolution (50%). However, BFO\'s consent would be required for any amendment that adversely affects BFO\'s individual economic rights, regardless of the votes of other LPs.
**[XII. Most Favored Nation (MFN) Rights]{.underline}**
**A. LPA Baseline**

The base LPA does not contain a most favored nation (\"MFN\") provision. The LPA acknowledges that the General Partner may enter into side letters with individual Limited Partners granting \"additional or modified terms\" without the consent of other Limited Partners. This is a standard side-letter authorization provision, but it does not include any mechanism for disclosure of side-letter terms to other LPs or any right for other LPs to elect the benefit of more favorable terms granted to another LP.

The absence of an MFN provision in the base LPA means that, without a side-letter MFN right, BFO would have no visibility into the terms granted to other LPs and no ability to \"level up\" to more favorable terms granted to a comparably-sized or smaller investor. Given the importance of MFN rights in ensuring equitable treatment among investors, this is a significant gap that must be addressed through BFO\'s side letter.
**B. Side-Letter Recommendation**

We recommend that BFO negotiate a most favored nation clause in its side letter. The MFN clause should entitle BFO to elect the benefit of any economic or governance term that the GP grants to any other Limited Partner committing \$50,000,000 or more to the Fund. The \$50,000,000 MFN threshold is designed to capture all investors at or above BFO\'s general commitment tier while excluding smaller investors who may receive standard terms without negotiation.
**Proposed MFN Mechanics:**

> \(a\) Within fifteen (15) business days following the close at which BFO is admitted to the Fund, the GP shall deliver to BFO a redacted summary (the \"Side Letter Summary\") of all material economic and governance terms contained in side letters entered into with Limited Partners committing \$50,000,000 or more to the Fund. The redacted summary need not identify the relevant LPs by name but must describe the substance of each material term with sufficient specificity to permit BFO to make an informed election.

> \(b\) BFO shall have a period of twenty (20) business days following receipt of the Side Letter Summary (the \"MFN Election Period\") to notify the GP in writing of any terms that BFO elects to incorporate into its own side letter.
> \(c\) Any terms elected by BFO during the MFN Election Period shall be deemed incorporated into BFO\'s side letter and shall be effective retroactively to the date of BFO\'s admission to the Fund.

> \(d\) If the GP enters into any additional side letters after the close at which BFO is admitted (e.g., at subsequent closings), the GP shall deliver a supplemental Side Letter Summary to BFO within fifteen (15) business days following each subsequent close, and BFO shall have an additional twenty (20) business day election period with respect to any new terms.
**Proposed MFN Carve-Outs.** The MFN clause should include carve-outs for the following categories of terms, which BFO would not be entitled to elect:

> \(i\) **Anchor Investor Terms.** Terms granted to Limited Partners committing \$200,000,000 or more to the Fund (\"Anchor Investors\"). At the target fund size of \$1,500,000,000, a \$200,000,000 commitment would represent approximately 13.33% of the target fund size. Anchor Investors typically receive more favorable economics (e.g., deeper management fee reductions, enhanced co-investment rights, advisory committee seats) that reflect the scale and strategic importance of their commitment. It is standard practice to exclude Anchor Investor terms from MFN elections, and BFO should expect the GP to insist on this carve-out.

> \(ii\) **Regulatory Accommodations.** Terms granted to Limited Partners that are ERISA plan investors, tax-exempt investors (including state pension funds, endowments, and foundations), or governmental plan investors, where such terms are granted solely for the purpose of addressing the regulatory or legal requirements applicable to such investors. These regulatory accommodations are investor-specific and are not relevant to BFO as a non-tax-exempt family office.

> \(iii\) **GP Affiliate Terms.** Terms granted to entities that are affiliates of the GP or MPCA, including any co-investment vehicles or parallel funds managed by MPCA. GP affiliate terms are structural rather than negotiated and are appropriately excluded from MFN elections.

The MFN clause is critical given BFO\'s position as a meaningful but not anchor-level investor. At 5.0% of the target fund size, BFO has sufficient commitment size to warrant favorable terms, but is not so large as to command the most preferential treatment available to the Fund\'s largest investors. The MFN clause ensures that BFO is not disadvantaged relative to similarly-sized LPs that may negotiate more aggressively or more effectively on particular points.

We have prepared an internal MFN Provision Comparison Matrix benchmarking Fund IV\'s proposed MFN framework against comparable provisions in recent fund formation engagements, which we will make available to BFO upon request.
**[XIII. Co-Investment Rights]{.underline}**
**A. LPA Baseline**

The base LPA provides the General Partner with discretion to offer co-investment opportunities to Limited Partners on a deal-by-deal basis. Section 6.4 of the LPA states that the GP \"may, in its sole discretion, offer co-investment opportunities to one or more Limited Partners in connection with specific Investments.\" However, the LPA does not create any entitlement or right for any Limited Partner to receive co-investment opportunities. The allocation of co-investment opportunities is entirely within the GP\'s discretion, and the GP is not required to offer co-investments to any particular LP or to allocate co-investments on a pro rata or other formulaic basis.

The LPA does not specify the fee or carry structure applicable to co-investments. This means that, absent a side-letter provision, the GP could offer co-investment opportunities on terms that include management fees and/or carried interest, which would reduce the economic benefit of the co-investment to the participating LP. In the current market environment, co-investments offered at full fees and carry provide limited incremental value to LPs relative to their primary fund commitment.
**B. Side-Letter Recommendation**
We recommend that BFO negotiate a pro rata co-investment right through its side letter. Specifically, we propose the following terms:

> \(a\) **Pro Rata Co-Investment Right.** The GP shall offer BFO a co-investment opportunity on each Fund IV investment with aggregate equity capitalization exceeding \$100,000,000. BFO\'s maximum co-investment allocation shall be equal to BFO\'s percentage share of the Fund\'s total Capital Commitments (approximately 5.0% at target fund size) applied to the available co-investment amount (i.e., the amount of the investment in excess of Fund IV\'s allocation).

> \(b\) **No Fee / No Carry.** Co-investments made by BFO shall be free of management fees and carried interest. This is increasingly the market standard for LP co-investments and is a significant economic benefit to BFO, as it effectively allows BFO to deploy additional capital alongside the Fund at zero incremental cost. Over the life of the Fund, the elimination of fees and carry on co-investments could represent hundreds of thousands of dollars (or more) in economic benefit, depending on the volume and profitability of co-investment opportunities.

> \(c\) **Election Period.** BFO shall have ten (10) business days from receipt of a co-investment offer to elect to participate (in whole or in part) or to decline the opportunity. If BFO declines or fails to respond within the election period, the GP may offer the co-investment to other LPs or third parties without further obligation to BFO.

> \(d\) **No Obligation to Invest.** BFO\'s co-investment right is an option, not an obligation. BFO may decline any co-investment opportunity without prejudice to its right to participate in future co-investment opportunities.

Co-investment rights at no fee/no carry are increasingly standard for commitments of BFO\'s size and serve as a meaningful value-add to BFO\'s overall relationship with the Fund. The ability to deploy additional capital at zero incremental cost improves BFO\'s blended fee load across its total exposure to Fund IV investments and can meaningfully enhance net returns. We anticipate that the GP will be willing to agree to the concept of co-investment rights, though it may seek to condition the right on (i) minimum co-investment amounts, (ii) the GP\'s right to allocate co-investments among multiple requesting LPs, and (iii) BFO\'s ability to execute co-investments within the required timeframe. These conditions are reasonable and should be acceptable to BFO.
**[XIV. Tax and Regulatory Considerations]{.underline}**
**A. Tax Structure**

Fund IV is organized as a Delaware limited partnership and is treated as a partnership for U.S. federal income tax purposes. As a partnership, Fund IV is not subject to entity-level federal income tax; instead, each partner (including each LP) is taxed on its allocable share of the Fund\'s income, gain, loss, deduction, and credit items, as reported on the annual Schedule K-1. This pass-through tax structure is the standard structure for institutional PE funds and is appropriate for BFO.

**K-1 Reporting.** As noted in Section XI.B above, the LPA provides for delivery of Schedule K-1s within 120 days after the end of each fiscal year. We have recommended that BFO negotiate accelerated K-1 delivery to 75 days (or, as a fallback, 90 days) through its side letter. Timely receipt of K-1s is important for BFO\'s tax planning and filing obligations.

**UBTI Considerations.** The LPA contains standard provisions addressing unrelated business taxable income (\"UBTI\") for tax-exempt investors. Specifically, the LPA permits the GP to establish one or more \"Blocker\" entities through which tax-exempt investors may invest in order to shield themselves from UBTI generated by the Fund\'s use of debt-financed real estate and operating company investments. While these UBTI provisions are not directly applicable to BFO (which is not a tax-exempt entity), they are relevant to the overall Fund structure because the presence of blocker entities can affect the allocation of income and loss among the Fund\'s partners. BFO should not be adversely affected by the UBTI blocker structure, but we will confirm this with MPCA\'s tax advisors during the diligence process.

**State and Local Tax.** BFO may be subject to state and local income tax in jurisdictions where Fund IV\'s investments are located. Real estate PE funds with investments across multiple states often generate filing obligations for their partners in each state where portfolio properties are situated. The LPA contains standard tax distribution provisions that are designed to provide partners with cash distributions sufficient to cover their estimated tax liabilities attributable to the Fund\'s income, including state and local taxes. These tax distributions are made on a quarterly estimated basis and are credited against the partner\'s share of subsequent profit distributions. BFO should consult with its own tax advisors regarding the state and local tax implications of the Fund IV commitment, including estimated tax payment obligations and filing requirements.

**B. ERISA.** Fund IV is structured to avoid holding \"plan assets\" within the meaning of Section 3(42) of the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974, as amended (\"ERISA\"), and the Department of Labor\'s plan asset regulations at 29 C.F.R. § 2510.3-101, as modified by Section 3(42) of ERISA. To achieve this result, the LPA limits the aggregate participation of \"benefit plan investors\" (as defined in the plan asset regulations) to less than 25% of each class of equity interests in the Fund. The GP is required to monitor compliance with this 25% threshold on an ongoing basis and may reject or limit subscriptions from benefit plan investors to ensure continued compliance.

BFO is not itself a benefit plan investor, as it is a private family office vehicle and is not subject to the fiduciary responsibility provisions of Title I of ERISA or the prohibited transaction provisions of Section 4975 of the Internal Revenue Code. However, as discussed in Section VII above, we have recommended that BFO negotiate an excuse right for any Fund investment that would cause BFO to be treated as holding \"plan assets\" under ERISA. While this is a belt-and-suspenders approach given the Fund-level ERISA protections, it provides an additional layer of protection for BFO against the unlikely scenario in which the Fund\'s ERISA compliance monitoring fails or in which a change in law or regulation alters the plan asset analysis.

**C. Confidentiality.** The LPA contains standard confidentiality provisions in Section 12.1, which prohibit each Limited Partner from disclosing any non-public information regarding the Fund, its investments, its performance, or the terms of the LPA to any third party, subject to certain enumerated exceptions. The standard carve-outs in the LPA permit disclosure:
> \(a\) To the extent required by applicable law, regulation, or governmental order (including state public records laws that may apply to governmental plan investors);
> \(b\) To the LP\'s legal, tax, and accounting advisors who have agreed to be bound by confidentiality obligations;
> \(c\) To regulatory authorities having jurisdiction over the LP; and
> \(d\) With the prior written consent of the GP.
**Recommendation.** We recommend that BFO negotiate broader confidentiality carve-outs through its side letter. Specifically, BFO\'s side letter should include the following additional carve-outs:

> \(a\) Disclosure to BFO\'s investment advisors, consultants, and other professional advisors engaged by BFO in connection with its oversight and monitoring of the Fund IV investment, without requiring such advisors to execute separate confidentiality agreements (though they may be required to acknowledge the confidential nature of the information);
> \(b\) Disclosure to members of the Hargrove family and their respective personal advisors, in connection with family wealth planning, estate planning, and philanthropic activities;
> \(c\) Disclosure to any Hargrove Family Entity (as defined in the transfer provisions discussed in Section X above) in connection with any proposed transfer of BFO\'s LP interest; and

> \(d\) Disclosure to any regulatory authority, self-regulatory organization, or judicial body in connection with any examination, investigation, or proceeding involving BFO or any member of the Hargrove family.

These expanded carve-outs are necessary to accommodate BFO\'s operational needs as a family office, which include regular communication with family members, personal advisors, and estate planning professionals regarding the family\'s investment portfolio. We anticipate low resistance from the GP on these points, as they are consistent with standard family office side-letter provisions.
**[XV. Summary of Recommended Side-Letter Negotiation Points]{.underline}**

Based on our review of the LPA, we have identified nine (9) categories of provisions that we recommend BFO negotiate through a side letter to the LPA. The following table summarizes each recommended provision, BFO\'s proposed position, the anticipated GP response, the priority ranking (with 1 being highest priority), and relevant notes:

**Priority**   **Provision**                       **BFO Position**                                                                                                                         **Anticipated GP Position**                                                                                    **Notes**

1              Most Favored Nation Rights          MFN for LPs committing ≥ \$50M; Anchor Investor carve-out at \$200M; 20 business day election period                                     Likely to accept concept; may negotiate scope of carve-outs or MFN threshold                                   Critical protection for BFO given 5.0% commitment size; ensures BFO is not disadvantaged relative to similarly-sized LPs

2              Excuse/Exclusion Rights             Cannabis, gaming/casino, OFAC sanctions, ERISA plan assets; 25% cap on excused investments (\$18.75M); 15 business day election period   Will accept concept but likely push for 15% cap (\$11.25M)                                                     Not in base LPA --- must be negotiated; critical for legal/regulatory/reputational risk management

3              Management Fee Reduction            1.50% / 1.25% (25 bps reduction in each tier)                                                                                            May resist or counter at 1.60% / 1.35% (15 bps reduction)                                                      Potential savings of \$187,500/yr during Investment Period (\$750,000 cumulative over 4 years)

4              Co-Investment Rights                Pro rata on deals exceeding \$100M equity; no management fee / no carried interest                                                       Likely to accept with conditions (allocation discretion, minimum amounts, execution timeline)                  Increasingly market standard at BFO\'s commitment level; significant value-add

5              Enhanced Reporting                  Quarterly portfolio reports in 45 days; annual audited financials in 90 days; annual ESG report; K-1s in 75 days                         May resist K-1 acceleration (administrator capacity); likely to accept portfolio reports and ESG               K-1 acceleration is most aggressive ask; 90 days is reasonable fallback

6              Key Person Enhancement              90-day BFO-specific suspension; unilateral right to cease future capital calls upon Key Person Event                                     Will likely resist individualized suspension/cessation right; may accept observer-level notice rights          Stronger than LPA baseline; discuss fallback positions with BFO

7              Transfer Rights                     Transfer to Hargrove Family Entities without GP consent; broadly defined family entity concept                                           Likely to accept with conditions (joinder agreement, securities law compliance, tax opinion, advance notice)   Necessary for estate planning and family wealth structuring

8              Confidentiality Carve-Outs          Disclosure to advisors, Hargrove family members, family entities, and regulators                                                         Standard; likely accepted with minimal negotiation                                                             Low resistance expected

9              Placement Fee Offset Confirmation   100% offset of \$750,000 placement fee against management fees; front-loaded application                                                 Already in base LPA; GP should confirm mechanics in side letter                                                Confirm timing and application mechanics

In addition to the items listed above, BFO should consider requesting an LPAC observer seat and a side-letter provision requiring LPAC consent or LP super-majority vote for the second one-year Fund term extension, as discussed in Sections XI.A and III.B, respectively. These items are lower priority than the nine items listed above but would provide meaningful governance protections.
**[XVI. Next Steps]{.underline}**
Based on the analysis set forth in this memorandum, we recommend the following next steps:

**1. Strategy Call with BFO.** We recommend scheduling a strategy call with Julian Hargrove (Principal, Briarwood Family Office LLC), Sandra M. Whitfield (General Counsel), and Derek T. Calloway (Director of External Investments) to review the findings of this memorandum, align on negotiation priorities, and discuss the recommended side-letter positions in detail. We are targeting this call for **February 5, 2024**. Please confirm the availability of the BFO team at your earliest convenience.

**2. Preparation and Transmission of Side-Letter Term Sheet.** Upon alignment on negotiation priorities during the strategy call, Calderwood & Harkness will prepare an initial side-letter term sheet reflecting BFO\'s proposed positions on each of the items identified in Section XV. We will transmit the term sheet to Ashford Crane & Hewitt LLP (Harrison K. Drummond and Elaine C. Woodbury, counsel to the GP) to initiate the side-letter negotiation process. We are targeting transmission of the initial term sheet during the **week of February 5, 2024**, subject to BFO\'s approval.

**3. Subscription Agreement and Investor Questionnaire Review.** In parallel with the side-letter negotiation, Calderwood & Harkness will undertake a review of the Fund IV subscription agreement and investor questionnaire, which BFO will be required to execute in connection with its commitment to the Fund. We will provide a separate memorandum addressing any notable provisions or areas of concern in the subscription documents.

**4. BFO Investment Committee Approval.** We understand that BFO\'s commitment to Fund IV requires the approval of BFO\'s investment committee, which consists of four (4) members. Approval requires the affirmative vote of at least three (3) of the four committee members, and Julian Hargrove, as the founding principal of BFO, holds veto authority over any proposed commitment. We recommend that the investment committee presentation incorporate the findings of this memorandum and the separate PPM Summary & Risk Assessment Memorandum. We are available to attend the investment committee meeting (in person or by videoconference) to present our findings and respond to questions from the committee members.

**5. Ongoing Communication.** Please direct any questions regarding this memorandum or the Fund IV commitment process to Theresa Kim (Lead Associate) or Pamela Cross (Responsible Partner) at Calderwood & Harkness LLP. Contact information is as follows:
> Theresa Kim, Lead Associate Calderwood & Harkness LLP 425 Lexington Avenue New York, NY 10017 Direct: (212) 555-4287
> Email: tkim@calderwoodharkness.com
> Pamela Cross, Partner Funds & Asset Management Calderwood & Harkness LLP 425 Lexington Avenue New York, NY 10017 Direct: (212) 555-4190
> Email: pcross@calderwoodharkness.com
**[XVII. Limitations and Disclaimers]{.underline}**

This memorandum is prepared solely for the use of Briarwood Family Office LLC and its authorized representatives in connection with BFO\'s evaluation of a proposed commitment to Meridian Peak Capital Partners Fund IV, L.P. The contents of this memorandum are protected by the attorney-client privilege and the work product doctrine. This memorandum may not be disclosed to, or relied upon by, any third party without the prior written consent of Calderwood & Harkness LLP.

The legal analysis contained in this memorandum is based on our review of the Amended and Restated Agreement of Limited Partnership of Meridian Peak Capital Partners Fund IV, L.P., dated December 20, 2023, as provided to Calderwood & Harkness LLP by Ashford Crane & Hewitt LLP (counsel to the General Partner) on January 26, 2024. We have assumed the authenticity and completeness of the LPA as provided and have not independently verified the representations or factual statements contained therein. If the LPA is amended, supplemented, or restated after the date of this memorandum, the analysis contained herein may need to be updated accordingly.

The balance of this letter sets forth the relevant background, the basis and scope of BFO\'s withdrawal, and the parties\' respective obligations going forward.
**[Background and Summary of Negotiations]{.underline}**

By way of background, BFO received the Fund IV Confidential Private Placement Memorandum, dated December 15, 2023 (the \"PPM\"), and the Amended and Restated Agreement of Limited Partnership of Fund IV, dated December 20, 2023 (the \"LPA\"), on or about January 8, 2024. These materials were transmitted electronically via Meridian Peak\'s secure data room, together with related subscription documents, investor questionnaire forms, and ancillary fund documentation.

Following an initial internal review of the PPM, the LPA, and related materials by BFO\'s investment professionals and in-house legal team, BFO engaged Calderwood & Harkness LLP on January 24, 2024 to advise BFO in connection with the proposed commitment and, specifically, to negotiate a side letter to the LPA (the \"Side Letter\") on BFO\'s behalf with respect to certain economic, governance, reporting, and regulatory terms.

> • On February 21, 2024, Calderwood & Harkness delivered a revised term sheet incorporating certain of the General Partner\'s counterproposals and providing further detail on BFO\'s remaining requests.

> • On February 28, 2024, Calderwood & Harkness circulated the first full draft of the Side Letter, reflecting the substantially agreed term-sheet provisions and presenting the remaining open points in long-form contractual language.

> • On March 4, 2024, Ashford Crane & Hewitt LLP returned a markup of the first draft Side Letter on behalf of the General Partner, which included revisions to a number of substantive provisions and counter-drafting on several material terms.

> • On March 7, 2024, Calderwood & Harkness circulated a second draft of the Side Letter, which responded to the General Partner\'s March 4 markup and proposed compromise language on certain of the disputed provisions.

> • On March 11, 2024, a four-party conference call was held among representatives of Calderwood & Harkness, BFO, Ashford Crane & Hewitt LLP, and Meridian Peak to discuss the remaining open negotiation points. That call addressed, among other things, the scope of excuse and exclusion rights, the structure of the most favored nation election mechanism, and certain aspects of the proposed management fee reduction.
> • On March 14, 2024, Calderwood & Harkness circulated a third draft of the Side Letter, reflecting the discussion points from the March 11 call and proposing revised language on the open items.
> • On March 18, 2024, Ashford Crane & Hewitt LLP returned a markup of the third draft Side Letter on behalf of the General Partner.

At the time negotiations were paused on March 28, 2024, certain material terms remained in brackets in the most recent draft of the Side Letter, including, without limitation, the excuse and exclusion cap percentage, the precise scope of the co-investment allocation methodology, and other items that had not been resolved to both parties\' mutual satisfaction. No final, execution-ready version of the Side Letter was produced.
**[Notification of Withdrawal]{.underline}**

We write to inform you that BFO\'s investment committee convened on April 2, 2024 and, following deliberation and consideration of the matter, voted to decline the proposed Seventy-Five Million Dollar (\$75,000,000) capital commitment to Fund IV. This decision was reached after a thorough review of BFO\'s current portfolio allocation, liquidity requirements, and broader investment strategy, and reflects BFO\'s internal investment considerations at this time. BFO wishes to emphasize that this decision is not a reflection on the merits of Fund IV, its investment strategy, the quality of its management team, or the capabilities of Meridian Peak as an investment adviser. Rather, BFO has concluded that a commitment to Fund IV does not align with BFO\'s current investment priorities and allocation targets.

Accordingly, BFO will not be subscribing for a limited partnership interest in Fund IV and will not be participating in Fund IV\'s anticipated initial closing, which we understand is expected to occur on or about April 30, 2024, or in any subsequent closing of Fund IV.
**[Lapse of Negotiated Provisions]{.underline}**

As a direct result of BFO\'s decision not to proceed with the proposed commitment, all draft Side Letter provisions negotiated between the parties are of no further force or effect and have lapsed in their entirety, effective as of the date of this letter. For clarity and completeness, the lapsed provisions include, without limitation, the following:

> \(a\) **Most Favored Nation Rights.** All provisions relating to most favored nation (\"MFN\") protections for BFO, including the MFN election mechanism, the Fifty Million Dollar (\$50,000,000) limited partner commitment threshold for MFN eligibility, the Two Hundred Million Dollar (\$200,000,000) anchor investor carve-out from MFN disclosure, and the twenty (20) business day election period following delivery of MFN disclosure materials.

> \(b\) **Excuse and Exclusion Rights.** All provisions granting BFO the right to be excused or excluded from participation in, or the obligation to fund capital contributions with respect to, certain categories of investments, including investments in cannabis-related assets, gaming and casino properties, investments in jurisdictions subject to U.S. sanctions administered by the Office of Foreign Assets Control (\"OFAC\"), and investments that would cause Fund IV assets to constitute \"plan assets\" within the meaning of Section 3(42) of the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974, as amended (\"ERISA\"), or the regulations promulgated thereunder.

> \(c\) **Management Fee Reductions.** All provisions providing for reduced management fees payable by BFO, including a management fee of one and one-half percent (1.50%) per annum on committed capital during the investment period and a management fee of one and one-quarter percent (1.25%) per annum on invested capital (net of write-downs and write-offs) following the expiration or termination of the investment period.

> \(d\) **Co-Investment Rights.** All provisions granting BFO pro rata co-investment participation rights with respect to equity investments by Fund IV exceeding One Hundred Million Dollars (\$100,000,000) in aggregate transaction value, including the terms providing that such co-investment interests would be offered at no management fee and no carried interest to the General Partner or the Adviser.

> \(e\) **Enhanced Reporting Obligations.** All provisions imposing enhanced quarterly and annual reporting obligations on the General Partner or the Adviser with respect to BFO, including the delivery of supplemental portfolio and valuation reports on a quarterly basis and annual audited financial statements in enhanced form, as well as periodic environmental, social, and governance (\"ESG\") reporting in a format reasonably satisfactory to BFO.

> \(f\) **Key Person Event Enhancements.** All provisions modifying the key person provisions set forth in the LPA with respect to BFO, including the provision requiring a ninety (90) day automatic suspension of the investment period upon the departure, death, disability, or material reduction in involvement of either Conrad J. Ellsworth or Priya Narayan from Fund IV investment activities, and the related cure and notice mechanisms negotiated in connection therewith.

> \(g\) **Transfer Rights.** All provisions granting BFO the right to transfer all or a portion of its limited partnership interest in Fund IV to Hargrove family entities (as defined in the draft Side Letter) without the prior consent of the General Partner, subject to compliance with applicable securities laws and the delivery of customary transfer documentation.

> \(h\) **Confidentiality Carve-Outs.** All provisions expanding or modifying the confidentiality obligations set forth in the LPA as applied to BFO, including carve-outs permitting disclosure to BFO\'s affiliates, advisors, auditors, and regulatory authorities in the ordinary course.

> \(i\) **Accelerated Schedule K-1 Delivery.** All provisions requiring the General Partner to deliver, or cause to be delivered, Schedule K-1 (IRS Form 1065) and related tax information to BFO within seventy-five (75) days following the end of each fiscal year of Fund IV, in advance of the delivery timeline set forth in the LPA.

> \(j\) **Placement Agent Fee Offset.** All provisions requiring a one hundred percent (100%) offset of any placement agent fees, commissions, or other compensation paid or payable by Fund IV, the General Partner, the Adviser, or any of their affiliates to Pinnacle Capital Markets LLC (the \"Placement Agent\") in connection with BFO\'s commitment, against management fees otherwise payable by BFO.

All of the foregoing provisions, whether reflected in the initial term sheet dated February 7, 2024, the revised term sheet dated February 21, 2024, any of the three successive drafts of the Side Letter dated February 28, March 7, and March 14, 2024, any of the General Partner\'s markups received on February 14, March 4, and March 18, 2024, or discussed orally during the March 11, 2024 conference call or in any other communication between the parties, have lapsed in their entirety and are of no further force or effect as of the date hereof.
**[No Executed Agreements; No Binding Obligations]{.underline}**
For the avoidance of doubt, we confirm the following:
> \(i\) No subscription agreement or subscription booklet was executed by or on behalf of BFO in connection with Fund IV at any time during the course of negotiations.

> \(ii\) No capital commitment --- whether binding, conditional, or otherwise --- has been made by BFO to Fund IV, the General Partner, or the Adviser, whether pursuant to the LPA, any Side Letter, or any other agreement or instrument.

> \(iii\) No investor questionnaire, investor certification, or similar document was submitted by or on behalf of BFO to Fund IV, the General Partner, the Adviser, or any placement agent or other intermediary in connection with the proposed commitment.

> \(iv\) No binding obligations of any kind exist between BFO, on the one hand, and Fund IV, Meridian Peak Capital Partners GP IV LLC, Meridian Peak Capital Advisors LLC, or any of their respective affiliates, on the other hand, in connection with the proposed commitment to Fund IV, and no party has any claim against BFO arising out of or related to the negotiations described herein.
**[Confidentiality]{.underline}**

BFO acknowledges and expects that the terms of the parties\' negotiations, including all draft Side Letter provisions, term sheets, markups, and related communications (whether written or oral), will be treated as confidential by Ashford Crane & Hewitt LLP, Meridian Peak, the General Partner, and Fund IV in accordance with customary practice applicable to fund subscription negotiations. BFO similarly will maintain the confidentiality of all Fund IV materials received by BFO and its advisors in connection with this process, including the PPM, the LPA, subscription documents, data room materials, and all related fund documentation, and will not disclose the terms thereof to any third party except as may be required by applicable law, regulation, or legal process, or to BFO\'s professional advisors on a need-to-know basis subject to customary confidentiality undertakings.
**[Return and Retention of Materials]{.underline}**

We note that BFO and Calderwood & Harkness LLP will retain copies of Fund IV documents received during the course of this process --- including the PPM, the LPA, subscription documents, and related materials --- in their respective files, as required by applicable law, professional responsibility obligations, and firm and institutional document-retention policies. Neither BFO nor Calderwood & Harkness LLP will use or disclose such materials for any purpose other than as may be required by applicable law, regulation, or legal process, or in connection with BFO\'s internal recordkeeping. Should Meridian Peak or its counsel wish to discuss further arrangements regarding the retention or return of specific materials, we are happy to accommodate any reasonable request.
**[Professional Courtesy]{.underline}**

In closing, on behalf of BFO and this firm, we wish to express our sincere appreciation for the professionalism, responsiveness, and constructive engagement demonstrated by Ashford Crane & Hewitt LLP and the Meridian Peak team throughout the negotiation process. The negotiations were conducted in good faith and in a manner reflecting well on all parties involved. We reiterate that BFO\'s decision to decline the proposed commitment should not be taken as a negative assessment of Fund IV, its investment thesis, or the capabilities of Meridian Peak and its principals. BFO values the relationship it has developed with Meridian Peak during this process and does not foreclose the possibility of future engagement on matters of mutual interest.
Please do not hesitate to contact me if you have any questions regarding the foregoing or if there is anything further we can address in connection with this matter.
Very truly yours,

**CALDERWOOD & HARKNESS LLP** 425 Lexington Avenue New York, NY 10017
**INTERNAL MEMORANDUM --- PRIVILEGED & CONFIDENTIAL**

This memorandum constitutes attorney work product and is protected by the attorney-client privilege and the work product doctrine. It is intended solely for internal use by the attorneys and professional staff of Calderwood & Harkness LLP involved in this matter. This memorandum should not be disclosed to any third party without the prior written consent of the Responsible Partner.
**Date:** April 5, 2024
**To:** File --- Matter No. 1026-00001
**From:** Pamela Cross, Responsible Partner, Funds & Asset Management
**Re:** Matter Closing Memorandum --- Briarwood Family Office LLC / Meridian Peak Capital Partners Fund IV, L.P. --- Side-Letter Negotiation
**Matter Number:** 1026-00001
**Status:** CLOSED --- TERMINATED
**[1. Purpose]{.underline}**

This memorandum documents the formal closing and termination of Matter No. 1026-00001 and is prepared in accordance with Calderwood & Harkness LLP\'s matter closing policies and procedures. The purpose of this memorandum is to create a comprehensive record of the work performed, the status of all documents and deliverables, the financial summary of the engagement, and the circumstances surrounding the termination of the matter, so that the firm\'s files may be properly closed and archived.

The matter involved the representation of Briarwood Family Office LLC (\"BFO\") in the negotiation of a side letter in connection with a proposed Seventy-Five Million Dollar (\$75,000,000) limited partnership commitment to Meridian Peak Capital Partners Fund IV, L.P. (\"Fund IV\" or the \"Fund\"), a Delaware limited partnership managed by Meridian Peak Capital Advisors LLC (\"MPCA\" or the \"Sponsor\"). Calderwood & Harkness LLP (\"C&H\" or the \"Firm\") was retained to review the Fund\'s offering and governing documents, advise BFO on the terms thereof, negotiate a side letter containing customized economic, governance, and reporting provisions on BFO\'s behalf, and review and mark up the subscription documents in anticipation of the commitment.

On April 2, 2024, BFO\'s investment committee reconvened and voted to decline the proposed commitment to Fund IV. On April 3, 2024, Sandra M. Whitfield, General Counsel of BFO, notified the undersigned of BFO\'s decision and instructed C&H to transmit a formal withdrawal letter to counsel for the Fund\'s general partner and to the Sponsor. On April 4, 2024, the undersigned transmitted such withdrawal letter, confirming that all draft side-letter provisions had lapsed without execution, that no subscription agreement had been executed, and that no capital commitment had been made by BFO to Fund IV.

As a consequence of BFO\'s decision, all draft side-letter provisions --- including, without limitation, the most favored nation rights, excuse and exclusion rights, management fee concessions, co-investment rights, enhanced reporting obligations, key person enhancements, transfer rights, confidentiality carve-outs, tax reporting commitments, and placement fee offset provisions that had been the subject of negotiation over the preceding approximately ten weeks --- lapsed and are of no further force or effect. No subscription agreement was executed, and no capital commitment of any kind was made by BFO to Fund IV or to any affiliated vehicle.
This matter is hereby closed effective as of the date hereof.

**Client:** Briarwood Family Office LLC
**Entity Type:** Delaware limited liability company
**Principal Business Address:** 780 Park Avenue, Suite 3200, New York, NY 10021
**Registered Agent:** Capitol Registered Agents Inc., 1209 Orange Street, Wilmington, Delaware 19801

**Primary Contacts:**

> • **Julian R. Hargrove** --- Managing Director & Chief Investment Officer. Mr. Hargrove serves as the principal decision-maker for BFO\'s investment activities and holds a veto right over all investment committee determinations. He was the ultimate authority on the proposed commitment to Fund IV and participated in strategic discussions regarding the scope and priority of side-letter negotiations.

> • **Sandra M. Whitfield** --- General Counsel. Ms. Whitfield served as BFO\'s primary point of contact with C&H throughout the engagement. She executed the engagement letter on behalf of BFO on January 24, 2024, and communicated BFO\'s instructions, feedback, and ultimate decision to decline the commitment. All formal communications between C&H and BFO were directed through Ms. Whitfield.

> • **Derek T. Calloway** --- Director of External Investments. Mr. Calloway was responsible for BFO\'s evaluation of the Fund IV opportunity from an investment and due diligence perspective. He participated in the four-party conference call on March 11, 2024 and provided input on the commercial terms of the side letter, including fee economics and co-investment structuring.
> • **Renata Vasquez** --- Investment Analyst. Ms. Vasquez supported Mr. Calloway in the due diligence process and served as a secondary contact for document production and information requests.

**Client Background:** BFO is a single-family office established in 2007 for the purpose of managing the wealth of the Hargrove family. The Hargrove family\'s wealth was principally derived from commercial real estate development activities in the northeastern United States, including the development and management of office, mixed-use, and multifamily properties across the greater New York metropolitan area and New England. BFO\'s investment strategy encompasses four primary verticals: (i) direct real estate investments, (ii) real estate credit strategies, (iii) private equity, and (iv) liquid alternatives. BFO typically allocates between fifteen percent (15%) and twenty percent (20%) of its total assets under management to third-party managed funds, with a preference for commingled vehicles managed by established sponsors with demonstrated track records. The proposed commitment to Fund IV fell within this allocation strategy and was consistent with BFO\'s historical appetite for institutional-quality real estate private equity vehicles.

8831: **Section 4.2 --- Capital Calls**
8832: 
8833: **(a) Capital Call Notice.** The General Partner shall issue a written notice to each Limited Partner (each, a \"**Capital Call Notice**\") specifying (i) the aggregate amount of the Capital Contribution being called, (ii) each Limited Partner\'s proportionate share of the Capital Contribution (based on its Partnership Percentage), (iii) the purpose of the capital call, (iv) the payment date (which shall not be less than ten (10) Business Days following the date of delivery of such Capital Call Notice), and (v) wire transfer instructions for payment. 8834: 
8835: **(b) Initial Capital Call.** One hundred percent (100%) of each Limited Partner\'s Capital Commitment shall be called at the Closing. The Initial Capital Contribution of each Limited Partner is due and payable on or before January 30, 2026 (the Closing Date). Without limitation, the Initial Capital Contribution of Pellegrino Capital Group LLC shall be Twenty-Five Million Dollars (\$25,000,000), due on or before January 30, 2026. All Initial Capital Contributions shall be funded in immediately available United States dollars by wire transfer to the account designated by the General Partner in the applicable Capital Call Notice. Time shall be of the essence with respect to the payment of Initial Capital Contributions.
8836: 
8837: **(c) Subsequent Capital Calls.** The Partnership is a single-investment co-invest vehicle, and no follow-on investments or additional capital commitments are contemplated. Accordingly, Capital Contributions shall be limited to the Initial Capital Contribution, except that the General Partner may call additional Capital Contributions from the Limited Partners solely for the purpose of funding Partnership expenses (including Organizational Expenses, administrative expenses, and any other expenses properly chargeable to the Partnership under Section 7.5), provided that (i) any such additional Capital Contributions for Organizational Expenses shall not exceed the Organizational Expenses Cap, (ii) any such additional Capital Contributions shall be funded from available Partnership reserves prior to requiring additional contributions from Limited Partners, and (iii) any additional Capital Contributions required hereunder shall be called pro rata from all Limited Partners based on their respective Partnership Percentages.
8838: 
8839: **Section 4.3 --- Return of Capital Contributions**
8840: 
8841: No Limited Partner shall have the right to demand or receive the return of any Capital Contribution or any part thereof at any time. Capital Contributions shall be returned to Limited Partners only through Distributions made in accordance with Article VI. No Limited Partner shall have priority over any other Limited Partner with respect to the return of Capital Contributions, except as expressly set forth in Article VI or in the case of a Defaulting Limited Partner as provided in Section 4.4.
8842: 
8843: **Section 4.4 --- Default**
8844: 
8845: **(a) Definition of Default.** A \"**Default**\" shall occur if any Limited Partner fails to fund all or any portion of a Capital Contribution within five (5) Business Days following the payment date specified in the applicable Capital Call Notice (after giving effect to the minimum ten (10) Business Day notice period set forth in Section 4.2(a)).
8846: 
8847: **(b) Remedies Upon Default.** Upon the occurrence of a Default by any Limited Partner (such Limited Partner, a \"**Defaulting Limited Partner**\"), the General Partner shall have the right, in addition to any other rights and remedies available at law or in equity, to impose any or all of the following penalties and remedies:
8848: 
8849: > \(i\) **Forfeiture of Partnership Interest.** Fifty percent (50%) of the Defaulting Limited Partner\'s Partnership Interest (including fifty percent (50%) of all Capital Contributions previously made by such Defaulting Limited Partner and all rights attributable thereto) shall be forfeited and shall be allocated among the non-defaulting Limited Partners pro rata based on their respective Partnership Percentages (calculated without regard to the Defaulting Limited Partner\'s Partnership Percentage).
8850: >
8851: > \(ii\) **Subordination of Remaining Interest.** The remaining fifty percent (50%) of the Defaulting Limited Partner\'s Partnership Interest shall be subordinated to all other Partnership Interests for purposes of Distributions under Article VI. The Defaulting Limited Partner shall receive Distributions only after all non-defaulting Partners have received a return of their Capital Contributions and their respective Preferred Return Amounts in full.
8852: >
8853: > \(iii\) **Loss of Governance Rights.** The Defaulting Limited Partner shall immediately forfeit any seat on the LPAC and all governance, consent, and voting rights under this Agreement.
8854: >
8855: > \(iv\) **Default Interest.** Interest shall accrue on the unpaid Capital Contribution amount at the lesser of (A) eighteen percent (18%) per annum, compounded monthly, or (B) the maximum rate permitted by applicable law, from the date such Capital Contribution was due until paid in full.
8856: 
8857: **(c) Cure Period.** Notwithstanding the foregoing, a Defaulting Limited Partner may cure a Default by funding the full amount of its unpaid Capital Contribution, together with all accrued and unpaid interest thereon pursuant to Section 4.4(b)(iv), within ten (10) Business Days of receiving written notice from the General Partner of the occurrence of the Default (a \"**Default Notice**\"); provided, however, that the General Partner may waive such cure right in its sole discretion if the failure to fund has materially prejudiced the Partnership, including without limitation if the failure to fund has impaired the Partnership\'s ability to consummate the Acquisition or satisfy its obligations to AcquisitionCo. If a Default is cured within the applicable cure period, the remedies set forth in Section 4.4(b) shall not be imposed.
8858: 
8859: **(d) GP Right to Fund.** If a Default is not cured within the applicable cure period, the General Partner may, but shall not be obligated to, take one or more of the following actions: (i) fund the unpaid Capital Contribution from Partnership reserves, if any, (ii) admit a replacement Limited Partner to fund the unpaid Capital Contribution on terms determined by the General Partner, or (iii) permit the non-defaulting Limited Partners to fund the unpaid Capital Contribution on a pro rata basis (based on their respective Partnership Percentages, calculated without regard to the Defaulting Limited Partner). The General Partner shall have sole discretion in determining which remedies to pursue and in what order.
8860: 
8861: **Section 4.5 --- No Interest on Capital Contributions**
8862: 
8863: Except as expressly provided in Section 4.4(b)(iv) with respect to defaulted Capital Contributions, no Partner shall be entitled to receive any interest on its Capital Contributions. The Preferred Return provided in Article VI is not interest on Capital Contributions but rather a priority return on invested capital.
