**Section 7.3 --- Actions Requiring LPAC Approval**

Notwithstanding the broad authority granted to the General Partner under Sections 7.1 and 7.2, the following actions shall require the prior written approval of a majority of the members of the LPAC (i.e., at least two (2) of three (3) LPAC members):

\(a\) Any borrowing by the Partnership in an aggregate principal amount in excess of One Million Dollars (\$1,000,000), other than short-term borrowings to bridge the funding of Capital Contributions pending receipt thereof from the Limited Partners;

\(b\) Any amendment to this Agreement that adversely affects the economic or governance rights of the Limited Partners, including any amendment to the Distribution waterfall, the Preferred Return, the Carried Interest Percentage, or the LPAC provisions;

\(c\) Any transaction or arrangement between the Partnership, on the one hand, and the General Partner, Ridgeline Management, or any Affiliate thereof, on the other hand (each, a \"conflict transaction\"), including any fee, compensation, or reimbursement arrangement not expressly contemplated by this Agreement;
\(d\) Any Distribution in kind (as set forth in Section 6.7);
\(e\) Any extension of the Term of the Partnership pursuant to Section 11.1;
\(f\) The methodology and inputs used for valuation of the Investment for purposes of Carried Interest calculations, including any year-end or interim valuations; and
\(g\) Any waiver of a Default by a Defaulting Limited Partner or modification of the Default remedies set forth in Section 4.4.
**Section 7.4 --- Parallel Investment with Fund IV**

\(a\) The Partnership shall invest in AcquisitionCo on terms and conditions no less favorable in all material respects than those applicable to Fund IV\'s investment in AcquisitionCo. The Investment shall be made on a pari passu basis with Fund IV, and the Partnership shall be entitled to the same class and type of AcquisitionCo Equity as Fund IV, with the same rights, preferences, privileges, and restrictions.

\(b\) Based on the equity contributions of the Partnership and Fund IV, the Partnership\'s ownership of AcquisitionCo shall be thirty percent (30%) (representing Seventy-Five Million Dollars (\$75,000,000) of Two Hundred Fifty Million Dollars (\$250,000,000) of total equity invested) and Fund IV\'s ownership shall be seventy percent (70%) (representing One Hundred Seventy-Five Million Dollars (\$175,000,000) of Two Hundred Fifty Million Dollars (\$250,000,000) of total equity invested).

\(c\) Following the Closing, the management rollover equity of approximately Thirty Million Dollars (\$30,000,000) contributed by Theodore \"Ted\" J. Barrington and Lisa M. Kwon (each, members of Clarion\'s management team) shall dilute all existing equity holders of AcquisitionCo, including the Partnership and Fund IV, on a proportional basis.
\(d\) The Partnership shall participate in any disposition of all or any portion of the Investment on a pro rata basis with Fund IV, at the same price per unit and on the same terms and conditions.
**Section 7.5 --- Expenses**

**(a) Organizational Expenses.** The Partnership shall bear Organizational Expenses (including legal fees for the preparation and negotiation of this Agreement, formation costs, filing fees, and other expenses directly attributable to the organization of the Partnership) up to the Organizational Expenses Cap of One Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars (\$150,000). Organizational Expenses shall be borne pro rata by the Limited Partners based on their respective Partnership Percentages. Any Organizational Expenses incurred in excess of the Organizational Expenses Cap shall be borne by the General Partner or Ridgeline Management and shall not be charged to the Partnership or any Limited Partner.

**(b) Operating Expenses.** The Partnership shall bear its pro rata share (based on relative equity contributions to AcquisitionCo) of any operating expenses of AcquisitionCo or the Investment that are allocable to the Partnership, as determined by the General Partner in its reasonable discretion. In addition, the Partnership shall bear its own ongoing administrative expenses, including accounting, audit, legal, tax preparation, tax filing, custodial, and other administrative fees and expenses incurred in the ordinary course of the Partnership\'s business.
**(c) Broken Deal Expenses.** Not applicable. The Investment has closed as of the date hereof, and no broken deal expenses have been incurred.

**(d) Management Fee.** For the avoidance of doubt, no management fee, advisory fee, monitoring fee, transaction fee, or similar fee shall be payable by the Partnership or any Limited Partner to the General Partner, Ridgeline Management, or any of their respective Affiliates.
**Section 7.6 --- Other Activities; No Exclusivity**

The General Partner, Ridgeline Management, and their respective Affiliates, partners, members, managers, officers, directors, and employees may engage in and possess interests in other business ventures and investment activities of any kind and description, including the management and operation of Fund IV and other investment funds, separately or jointly with others, whether or not competitive with the Partnership. Such activities shall not constitute a breach of any duty or obligation owed by any such Person to the Partnership or any Partner. No Limited Partner shall have any right to participate in, or receive any benefit from, any other investment opportunity of the General Partner, Ridgeline Management, or their Affiliates, except as may be expressly provided in a Side Letter.
**Section 7.7 --- Delegation**

The General Partner may delegate any of its powers, duties, and responsibilities hereunder to any officer, employee, agent, or Affiliate of the General Partner or Ridgeline Management; provided, however, that no such delegation shall relieve the General Partner of its obligations and liabilities under this Agreement or under the Act, and the General Partner shall remain fully responsible and liable for any act or omission of any delegate to the same extent as if such act or omission were the act or omission of the General Partner.
**Section 7.8 --- Standard of Care; Exculpation**

The General Partner shall manage the business and affairs of the Partnership in good faith and in a manner it reasonably believes to be in the best interests of the Partnership. No Covered Person shall be liable to the Partnership or to any Partner for any act or omission taken or suffered by such Covered Person in good faith and reasonably believed by such Covered Person to be in, or not opposed to, the best interests of the Partnership, provided that such act or omission does not constitute fraud, willful misconduct, gross negligence, or a material breach of this Agreement. The General Partner shall not be liable for any error of judgment or for any mistake of fact or law. No Covered Person shall be obligated to guarantee the return of any Partner\'s Capital Contributions or a profit for any Partner from the operations of the Partnership.
**Section 7.9 --- Indemnification**

**(a) Scope of Indemnification.** To the fullest extent permitted by law, the Partnership shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless each Covered Person from and against any and all losses, damages, liabilities, claims, demands, actions, suits, proceedings, judgments, penalties, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys\' fees and expenses, court costs, and costs of investigation and settlement) (collectively, \"**Losses**\") incurred by such Covered Person and arising out of, resulting from, or in connection with (i) the business, operations, or affairs of the Partnership, (ii) such Covered Person\'s service to or on behalf of the Partnership, or (iii) such Covered Person\'s status as a Covered Person; provided, however, that the Partnership shall not indemnify any Covered Person for any Losses to the extent that such Losses arise from or are attributable to fraud, willful misconduct, gross negligence, or a material breach of this Agreement by such Covered Person.

**(b) Advancement of Expenses.** The Partnership shall advance to any Covered Person reasonable expenses (including attorneys\' fees) incurred by such Covered Person in connection with any proceeding for which indemnification may be sought under this Section 7.9, upon receipt of a written undertaking by such Covered Person to repay such amounts to the Partnership if it is ultimately determined by a court of competent jurisdiction or by final arbitration award that such Covered Person is not entitled to indemnification under this Section 7.9.

**(c) Insurance.** The General Partner may, in its discretion, cause the Partnership to obtain and maintain directors\' and officers\' liability insurance, errors and omissions insurance, or such other insurance coverage as the General Partner deems appropriate to cover the Covered Persons with respect to their activities on behalf of the Partnership. The cost of any such insurance shall be an expense of the Partnership.
**[ARTICLE VIII --- TRANSFERS OF PARTNERSHIP INTERESTS]{.underline}**
**Section 8.1 --- Restrictions on Transfer**

No Limited Partner may Transfer all or any portion of its Partnership Interest without the prior written consent of the General Partner, which consent may be granted or withheld in the General Partner\'s sole and absolute discretion. As used herein, \"**Transfer**\" means any direct or indirect sale, assignment, transfer, conveyance, exchange, gift, pledge, hypothecation, encumbrance, or other disposition of all or any portion of a Partnership Interest or any economic or governance rights therein, whether voluntary or involuntary, by operation of law or otherwise, including by merger, consolidation, liquidation, dissolution, or similar transaction. Any attempted Transfer of a Partnership Interest in violation of this Article VIII shall be null and void and of no force or effect, and the Partnership shall not recognize any such Transfer or accord any rights hereunder to any purported transferee.
**Section 8.2 --- Conditions to Permitted Transfers**
Any Transfer of a Partnership Interest that is permitted by the General Partner pursuant to Section 8.1 shall be subject to and conditioned upon satisfaction of each of the following conditions:
\(a\) Compliance with the Right of First Refusal provisions set forth in Section 8.3;

\(b\) Receipt by the General Partner of a written opinion of counsel, satisfactory to the General Partner in form and substance and from counsel satisfactory to the General Partner, to the effect that such Transfer is exempt from registration under the Securities Act and under all applicable state securities laws;

\(c\) The proposed transferee shall execute and deliver to the General Partner a joinder agreement substantially in the form attached hereto as Exhibit A, pursuant to which such transferee agrees to be bound by all of the terms, conditions, and obligations of this Agreement applicable to the transferring Limited Partner;

\(d\) Such Transfer shall not cause the Partnership to be treated as a \"publicly traded partnership\" within the meaning of Section 7704 of the Code or otherwise to be taxable as a corporation for federal income tax purposes;

\(e\) The transferring Limited Partner shall pay, or cause to be paid, all reasonable out-of-pocket legal, accounting, and administrative costs and expenses incurred by the Partnership and the General Partner in connection with such Transfer; and
\(f\) Such other conditions as the General Partner may reasonably impose.
**Section 8.3 --- Right of First Refusal (ROFR)**

\(a\) Prior to any proposed Transfer of all or any portion of a Partnership Interest to any third party (other than a Permitted Transferee), the transferring Limited Partner shall deliver to the General Partner a written notice (a \"**Transfer Notice**\") setting forth (i) the identity of the proposed transferee, (ii) the proposed purchase price or other consideration for the Partnership Interest to be transferred, (iii) the material terms and conditions of the proposed Transfer, and (iv) a representation that the proposed Transfer complies with all applicable securities laws. A form of Transfer Notice is attached hereto as Exhibit C.

\(b\) The General Partner shall have a period of thirty (30) days following receipt of the Transfer Notice (the \"**GP ROFR Period**\") to elect, by written notice to the transferring Limited Partner, to purchase (or to cause any other Partner, Fund IV, or any other designee of the General Partner to purchase) all (but not less than all) of the Partnership Interest offered for Transfer, at the same price and on the same material terms and conditions set forth in the Transfer Notice.

\(c\) If the General Partner does not exercise the ROFR within the GP ROFR Period, the General Partner shall promptly notify the other Limited Partners, and the other Limited Partners shall have a further period of fifteen (15) days following receipt of such notice (the \"**LP ROFR Period**\") to elect, by written notice to the General Partner and the transferring Limited Partner, to purchase the offered Partnership Interest (or such portion thereof as is offered), pro rata based on their respective Partnership Percentages (calculated without regard to the transferring Limited Partner\'s Partnership Percentage). If more than one non-transferring Limited Partner elects to purchase and the aggregate elections exceed the offered Partnership Interest, such elections shall be satisfied pro rata based on the electing Limited Partners\' respective Partnership Percentages.

\(d\) If neither the General Partner nor the other Limited Partners exercise the ROFR within the applicable periods, the transferring Limited Partner may, subject to satisfaction of all other conditions in Section 8.2, consummate the Transfer to the proposed transferee identified in the Transfer Notice, at the same price and on terms no more favorable to the transferee than those set forth in the Transfer Notice, within sixty (60) days following the expiration of the LP ROFR Period. If the Transfer is not consummated within such sixty (60)-day period, the ROFR process set forth in this Section 8.3 must be repeated before any Transfer may occur.
**Section 8.4 --- Transfers by the General Partner**

The General Partner shall not Transfer its general partner interest in the Partnership without the prior written consent of Limited Partners holding a majority-in-interest of the aggregate Capital Commitments of all Limited Partners; provided, however, that the General Partner may, without the consent of the Limited Partners, Transfer its general partner interest to an Affiliate of the General Partner or Ridgeline Management, provided that (i) such Affiliate assumes all obligations of the General Partner hereunder, (ii) such Affiliate is wholly owned, directly or indirectly, by Ridgeline Management, and (iii) the General Partner provides at least ten (10) Business Days\' prior written notice to the Limited Partners of such Transfer.
**Section 8.5 --- Tag-Along Rights**

\(a\) If Fund IV proposes to Transfer all or any portion of its interest in AcquisitionCo to a third party that is not an Affiliate of Fund IV or Fund IV GP (a \"**Tag-Along Sale**\"), each Limited Partner shall have the right (a \"**Tag-Along Right**\") to participate in such Transfer on a pro rata basis, at the same price per unit of AcquisitionCo Equity and on the same terms and conditions as Fund IV.

\(b\) The General Partner shall provide at least twenty (20) Business Days\' prior written notice to each Limited Partner of any proposed Tag-Along Sale (a \"**Tag-Along Notice**\"), which notice shall set forth the identity of the proposed purchaser, the proposed price, and the material terms and conditions of the proposed sale.

\(c\) Each Limited Partner may elect to exercise its Tag-Along Right by delivering written notice to the General Partner within fifteen (15) Business Days of receipt of the Tag-Along Notice. Any Limited Partner that does not deliver a timely election notice shall be deemed to have waived its Tag-Along Right with respect to such Tag-Along Sale.

\(d\) Each Limited Partner exercising its Tag-Along Right may include in such Tag-Along Sale up to one hundred percent (100%) of its proportionate interest in the AcquisitionCo Equity (determined based on the Partnership\'s proportionate ownership of AcquisitionCo and such Limited Partner\'s Partnership Percentage).
\(e\) The closing of any Tag-Along Sale shall be conditioned upon the participation of all Limited Partners that have timely exercised their Tag-Along Rights.
**Section 8.6 --- Drag-Along Rights**

\(a\) If the General Partner determines, in its sole discretion, to sell one hundred percent (100%) of the AcquisitionCo Equity held by the Partnership and Fund IV to a third party (a \"**Drag-Along Sale**\"), the General Partner may require all Limited Partners to sell their proportionate interests in the AcquisitionCo Equity (indirectly, through the Partnership) on the same terms and conditions as Fund IV (the \"**Drag-Along Right**\").

\(b\) The General Partner shall provide at least twenty (20) Business Days\' prior written notice to each Limited Partner of any proposed Drag-Along Sale (a \"**Drag-Along Notice**\"), which notice shall set forth the identity of the proposed purchaser, the proposed price, and the material terms and conditions of the proposed sale.
\(c\) In any Drag-Along Sale, each Limited Partner shall receive its proportionate share of the sale proceeds in accordance with the Distribution waterfall set forth in Section 6.2.

\(d\) In connection with any Drag-Along Sale, the representations and warranties required of the dragged Limited Partners shall be limited to (i) title to and ownership of their Partnership Interests, (ii) authority and power to enter into and perform the sale transaction, and (iii) the absence of encumbrances on their Partnership Interests. No Limited Partner shall be required to make any representations or warranties with respect to the business, assets, liabilities, operations, or financial condition of AcquisitionCo, Clarion, or any of their respective subsidiaries.

\(e\) Each Limited Partner hereby agrees to take all actions and execute all documents reasonably requested by the General Partner to consummate a Drag-Along Sale, including execution of purchase agreements, closing certificates, and related instruments.
**Section 8.7 --- Substitute Limited Partners**

A permitted transferee of a Partnership Interest shall be admitted to the Partnership as a substitute Limited Partner only upon satisfaction of all conditions set forth in Section 8.2 and execution and delivery of such documentation as the General Partner may reasonably require, including a joinder agreement substantially in the form of Exhibit A. Upon admission as a substitute Limited Partner, the transferee shall succeed to all of the rights and obligations of the transferring Limited Partner with respect to the transferred Partnership Interest, and the transferring Limited Partner shall be released from all obligations hereunder with respect to the transferred Partnership Interest (other than obligations that accrued prior to the effective date of such Transfer). The General Partner shall promptly update Schedule A to reflect any such substitution.
**[ARTICLE IX --- LIMITED PARTNER ADVISORY COMMITTEE (LPAC)]{.underline}**
**Section 9.1 --- Establishment and Composition**

The Partnership shall establish a Limited Partner Advisory Committee (the \"**LPAC**\") consisting of three (3) members. The members of the LPAC shall be appointed by the General Partner from among the Limited Partners or their designated representatives; provided, however, that Pellegrino Capital Group LLC shall be entitled to appoint one (1) member of the LPAC for so long as Pellegrino Capital Group LLC holds a Partnership Interest in the Partnership. LPAC members shall serve in a non-fiduciary, advisory capacity, except where specific approval or consent rights are expressly conferred upon the LPAC by this Agreement. For the avoidance of doubt, LPAC members shall not owe any fiduciary duties to the Partnership or to any other Partner by virtue of their service on the LPAC.
**Section 9.2 --- LPAC Functions**
The LPAC shall have the following functions and responsibilities:
\(a\) Review and approve (or disapprove) conflict transactions between the Partnership and the General Partner or any of its Affiliates as contemplated by Section 7.3(c);
\(b\) Review and approve (or disapprove) all other matters requiring LPAC consent as set forth in Section 7.3;
\(c\) Consult with the General Partner regarding valuations of the Investment, including the methodology and inputs used for such valuations;
\(d\) Review and approve (or disapprove) any proposed Distributions in kind pursuant to Section 6.7;
\(e\) Consult with the General Partner regarding the management transition plan in connection with a Key Person Event pursuant to Section 10.1; and

\(f\) Perform such other advisory functions as the General Partner may request from time to time, including review of the Partnership\'s annual financial statements and consultation on material strategic matters relating to the Investment.
**Section 9.3 --- LPAC Meetings**

\(a\) The LPAC shall meet at least once per calendar year, or more frequently as the General Partner or any two (2) LPAC members may request. Meetings may be held in person at the offices of the General Partner, by video conference, or by telephonic conference, as determined by the General Partner in consultation with the LPAC members.

\(b\) The General Partner shall provide at least ten (10) Business Days\' prior written notice of each meeting to all LPAC members, together with a written agenda and copies of any relevant materials to be discussed at such meeting.

\(c\) A quorum for any meeting of the LPAC shall consist of a majority of the LPAC members (i.e., two (2) of three (3) members). Actions of the LPAC shall be taken by the affirmative vote or written consent of a majority of the LPAC members (i.e., two (2) of three (3) members).
\(d\) Actions may be taken by the LPAC without a meeting by written consent signed by a majority of the LPAC members, which consent shall be effective as of the date of the last signature.
\(e\) The General Partner shall prepare and distribute to all LPAC members written minutes of each meeting within fifteen (15) Business Days following such meeting.
**Section 9.4 --- Indemnification of LPAC Members**

Each member of the LPAC shall be indemnified by the Partnership on the same basis as Covered Persons under Section 7.9 with respect to any Losses incurred by such member arising out of or in connection with such member\'s service on the LPAC. LPAC members acting in good faith in the performance of their duties as LPAC members shall have no personal liability to the Partnership, the General Partner, or any Limited Partner for any actions taken or omitted to be taken in their advisory capacity as LPAC members.
**Section 9.5 --- Removal and Replacement**
\(a\) The General Partner may remove any LPAC member for Cause upon written notice to such LPAC member and the Limited Partner that appointed or designated such member.

\(b\) Any Limited Partner that appointed or designated an LPAC member may, at any time, designate a replacement for such LPAC member by written notice to the General Partner, and such replacement shall become effective upon receipt of such notice by the General Partner.

\(c\) In the event of a vacancy on the LPAC (whether by removal, resignation, or otherwise), the General Partner shall appoint a replacement LPAC member from among the Limited Partners or their designated representatives within thirty (30) days of such vacancy; provided, however, that any vacancy in the LPAC seat held by a designee of Pellegrino Capital Group LLC shall be filled by a designee of Pellegrino Capital Group LLC.
**[ARTICLE X --- KEY PERSON; EXCUSE RIGHTS]{.underline}**
**Section 10.1 --- Key Person Provisions**

**(a) Key Persons.** The Key Persons are Julian T. Whitmore (Co-Founder & Managing Partner, Ridgeline Equity Management LLC) and Connor M. Rafferty (Partner, Head of Hospitality, Ridgeline Equity Management LLC). The Limited Partners have entered into this Agreement in reliance upon the active involvement of the Key Persons in the management and oversight of the Investment.

**(b) Key Person Event.** A \"**Key Person Event**\" shall occur if both Key Persons cease to be actively involved in the management and oversight of the Investment and the business of Fund IV as it relates to the hospitality sector. For purposes of this Section 10.1, \"active involvement\" requires that each Key Person devotes a minimum of fifty percent (50%) of such individual\'s professional time and attention to Fund IV, the Partnership, and related investment activities. A Key Person Event shall not be triggered by the departure of only one Key Person, provided that the remaining Key Person continues to satisfy the active involvement requirement.
**(c) Consequences of a Key Person Event.** Upon the occurrence of a Key Person Event:

> \(i\) The General Partner shall promptly (and in any event within five (5) Business Days) notify all Limited Partners in writing of the occurrence of the Key Person Event, including the circumstances giving rise thereto.

> \(ii\) The General Partner shall suspend any follow-on investments (though for a single-asset co-invest vehicle, the General Partner acknowledges that this provision is not expected to be applicable given the nature of the Partnership\'s Investment).

> \(iii\) Limited Partners holding a majority-in-interest of the Aggregate Capital Commitments shall have the right, exercisable within ninety (90) days following receipt of notice of the Key Person Event, to (A) approve a replacement key person proposed by the General Partner (such approval not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed), or (B) direct the General Partner to commence an orderly liquidation of the Investment (which direction shall be binding on the General Partner), taking into account market conditions and the interests of the Limited Partners as a whole.

> \(iv\) During the ninety (90)-day period referred to in clause (iii) above, the General Partner shall consult with the LPAC regarding a management transition plan, including the identification and evaluation of potential replacement key persons and the impact of the Key Person Event on the Investment.
**Section 10.2 --- Excuse Rights**

**(a) Limited Partner Excuse Rights.** A Limited Partner may request to be excused from the Investment only if participation in the Investment would result in a legal or regulatory conflict for such Limited Partner, including conflicts arising under applicable law, regulation, governmental order, or binding contractual restriction to which such Limited Partner is subject. Any request to be excused must be submitted in writing to the General Partner, together with a reasonably detailed description of the applicable legal or regulatory conflict and supporting documentation as the General Partner may reasonably request.

**(b) GP Approval.** The General Partner shall have the right to approve or deny any excuse request submitted pursuant to Section 10.2(a); provided, however, that such approval shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed. The General Partner shall notify the requesting Limited Partner of its determination within thirty (30) days of receipt of the excuse request. If a Limited Partner is excused from the Investment, such Limited Partner\'s Capital Commitment shall be reallocated among the remaining Limited Partners on a pro rata basis (based on their respective Partnership Percentages, calculated without regard to the excused Limited Partner\'s Partnership Percentage) or to a new Limited Partner, in each case at the General Partner\'s discretion and subject to the consent of the accepting Limited Partners or new Limited Partner.

**(c) No GP-Initiated Excuse or Exclusion.** The General Partner may not excuse or exclude any Limited Partner from the Investment without such Limited Partner\'s prior written consent, except as otherwise expressly agreed in a Side Letter between the General Partner and such Limited Partner.
**[ARTICLE XI --- TERM; DISSOLUTION; WINDING UP]{.underline}**
**Section 11.1 --- Term**

The \"**Term**\" of the Partnership shall commence on the date of the filing of the Certificate of Limited Partnership with the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware and shall continue until the tenth (10th) anniversary of the Closing Date (i.e., January 30, 2036), unless earlier dissolved pursuant to Section 11.2. The General Partner may extend the Term for up to two (2) additional one (1)-year periods (each, a \"**GP Extension**\"), subject to the prior written approval of a majority of the members of the LPAC pursuant to Section 7.3(e). If both GP Extensions are exercised, the maximum Term of the Partnership shall expire on January 30, 2038. The Term of the Partnership is intended to be co-terminous with the term of Fund IV as it relates to the Investment.
**Section 11.2 --- Events of Dissolution**
The Partnership shall be dissolved upon the earliest to occur of any of the following events:
\(a\) The expiration of the Term (including any GP Extensions);

\(b\) The sale, disposition, or other realization of the entire Investment (including, for the avoidance of doubt, a sale of one hundred percent (100%) of the AcquisitionCo Equity held by the Partnership);
\(c\) A determination by the General Partner, with the prior written approval of Limited Partners holding a majority-in-interest of the Aggregate Capital Commitments, to dissolve the Partnership;
\(d\) The entry of a decree of judicial dissolution of the Partnership under Section 17-802 of the Act; or
\(e\) The occurrence of any event that makes it unlawful for the business of the Partnership to continue, unless such illegality is cured within ninety (90) days.
**Section 11.3 --- Winding Up and Liquidation**

Upon dissolution of the Partnership, the General Partner (or, if no General Partner exists at the time of dissolution, a liquidating trustee appointed by Limited Partners holding a majority-in-interest of the Aggregate Capital Commitments) shall proceed to wind up the affairs of the Partnership in an orderly manner. The winding up of the Partnership shall include:
\(a\) The collection of all outstanding receivables and the liquidation of all remaining Partnership assets;

\(b\) The payment and discharge of all debts, liabilities, and obligations of the Partnership, including all amounts owed to the Partners in their capacities as creditors of the Partnership (to the extent otherwise permitted by law);

\(c\) The establishment and setting aside of reasonable reserves for any contingent, conditional, or unmatured liabilities of the Partnership, as determined by the General Partner (or liquidating trustee) in its reasonable discretion, which reserves shall be held for such period as the General Partner (or liquidating trustee) deems advisable and, upon expiration of such period, shall be distributed in accordance with this Section 11.3; and

\(d\) The distribution of remaining assets to the Partners in accordance with the Distribution waterfall set forth in Section 6.2, after satisfaction of all obligations described in clauses (a), (b), and (c) above.
**Section 11.4 --- Final Accounting**

Within one hundred twenty (120) days following the dissolution of the Partnership, the General Partner (or liquidating trustee) shall prepare and deliver to each Partner a final accounting of the Partnership, which shall include a statement of the Partnership\'s assets and liabilities, a summary of all Distributions made during the winding up period, and a final schedule of each Partner\'s Capital Account balance. Such final accounting shall be prepared in accordance with GAAP and reviewed by the Partnership\'s independent accounting firm.
**Section 11.5 --- Certificate of Cancellation**

Upon the completion of the winding up and liquidation of the Partnership, the General Partner (or liquidating trustee) shall file a Certificate of Cancellation with the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware in accordance with the Act, and shall take all other actions necessary to terminate the Partnership\'s existence in Delaware and in any other jurisdiction in which the Partnership is qualified to do business.
**Section 11.6 --- Survival of Certain Provisions**

The following provisions of this Agreement shall survive the dissolution, winding up, and termination of the Partnership and shall remain in full force and effect until all obligations thereunder have been satisfied: Section 6.5 (GP Clawback), Section 7.8 (Standard of Care; Exculpation), Section 7.9 (Indemnification), Section 12.3 (Confidentiality), and Section 14.10 (Governing Law). In addition, the provisions of this Agreement necessary to give effect to, or to interpret, the foregoing surviving provisions shall also survive.
**[ARTICLE XII --- REPORTING AND INFORMATION RIGHTS; CONFIDENTIALITY]{.underline}**
**Section 12.1 --- Financial Reporting**

**(a) Annual Audited Financial Statements.** The General Partner shall cause to be prepared and delivered to each Limited Partner annual audited financial statements of the Partnership within one hundred twenty (120) days following the end of each Fiscal Year. Such financial statements shall include a balance sheet, a statement of operations, a statement of changes in partners\' capital, and a statement of cash flows, each prepared in accordance with GAAP and audited by an independent accounting firm of recognized national standing selected by the General Partner.

**(b) Quarterly Unaudited Financial Statements.** The General Partner shall cause to be prepared and delivered to each Limited Partner unaudited financial statements of the Partnership within sixty (60) days following the end of each fiscal quarter (March 31, June 30, September 30, and December 31). Such quarterly financial statements shall include, at a minimum, a balance sheet and a statement of operations, and shall be accompanied by a brief narrative report on the status of the Investment and any material developments since the prior reporting period.

**(c) Additional Reporting.** The General Partner shall provide such other information as may be reasonably requested by any Limited Partner to satisfy such Limited Partner\'s regulatory, tax, legal, or reporting requirements (including without limitation information required for ERISA compliance, FATCA reporting, Solvency II reporting, and state or municipal pension fund reporting obligations), subject to (i) the General Partner\'s reasonable ability to provide such information, (ii) the requesting Limited Partner\'s execution of any confidentiality or non-disclosure agreement that the General Partner deems reasonably appropriate, and (iii) reimbursement by the requesting Limited Partner of any incremental out-of-pocket costs incurred by the Partnership in connection with providing such information.
**Section 12.2 --- Tax Reporting**

**(a) Schedule K-1.** The General Partner shall deliver, or cause to be delivered, to each Limited Partner an IRS Schedule K-1 (Form 1065) (or any successor form or equivalent thereof) on or before March 15 of each year for the immediately preceding Fiscal Year. If the General Partner is unable to deliver final Schedules K-1 by March 15, the General Partner shall deliver estimated Schedules K-1 by such date, followed by final Schedules K-1 as soon as practicable.

**(b) Tax Estimates.** The General Partner shall use commercially reasonable efforts to provide estimated tax information (including estimated allocable shares of taxable income, gain, loss, deduction, and credit) to each Limited Partner by February 15 of each year for the immediately preceding Fiscal Year, to enable the Limited Partners to prepare their estimated tax returns and payments.

**(c) Partnership Representative.** The General Partner shall serve as the Partnership Representative under Section 6223 of the Code for all taxable years of the Partnership. The General Partner shall not settle, compromise, or take any position with respect to any tax audit, examination, or proceeding that would disproportionately adversely affect any Limited Partner without prior consultation with the LPAC. In the event the Partnership is subject to any tax audit adjustment, the General Partner shall, to the extent permitted by applicable law, elect to push out any imputed underpayment to the Partners under Section 6226 of the Code rather than paying the imputed underpayment at the Partnership level.
**Section 12.3 --- Confidentiality**

**(a) Confidential Information.** Each Partner shall maintain the confidentiality of all non-public information regarding the Partnership, the Investment, AcquisitionCo, Clarion, and the terms and conditions of this Agreement (collectively, \"**Confidential Information**\"), and shall not disclose any Confidential Information to any Person except as permitted by this Section 12.3.
**(b) Permitted Disclosures.** Notwithstanding Section 12.3(a), Confidential Information may be disclosed by a Partner:

> \(i\) To such Partner\'s professional advisors (including legal counsel, tax advisors, and accountants) who are bound by professional obligations of confidentiality or who have entered into confidentiality agreements with such Partner;

> \(ii\) As required by applicable law, regulation, governmental order, subpoena, or legal process; provided, however, that the disclosing Partner shall, to the extent permitted by applicable law, provide prior written notice to the General Partner of any such required disclosure and shall cooperate with the General Partner in seeking a protective order or other appropriate remedy;

> \(iii\) To such Partner\'s Affiliates, limited partners, direct and indirect investors, members, managers, officers, directors, and employees who have a bona fide need to know such information and who are bound by confidentiality obligations that are no less restrictive than those set forth in this Section 12.3;
> \(iv\) With the prior written consent of the General Partner; and
> \(v\) In connection with any bona fide dispute or proceeding relating to this Agreement or the Partnership.

**(c) Survival.** The confidentiality obligations set forth in this Section 12.3 shall survive the withdrawal, removal, or transfer of any Partner\'s Partnership Interest and shall remain in full force and effect for a period of two (2) years following the termination of the Partnership.

Notwithstanding the foregoing, the General Partner may amend Schedule A without the consent of the Limited Partners to reflect (i) the admission of additional or substitute Limited Partners, (ii) the withdrawal or removal of Limited Partners, (iii) permitted Transfers of Partnership Interests, and (iv) adjustments to Capital Commitments and Partnership Percentages resulting from any of the foregoing.
**Section 14.3 --- Waiver**

No waiver of any term, condition, or provision of this Agreement shall be effective unless made in writing and signed by the party against whom enforcement of such waiver is sought. No failure or delay by any party in exercising any right, power, or privilege under this Agreement shall operate as a waiver thereof, nor shall any single or partial exercise of any such right, power, or privilege preclude any other or further exercise thereof or the exercise of any other right, power, or privilege. The rights and remedies provided herein are cumulative and not exclusive of any rights or remedies provided by law or in equity.
**Section 14.4 --- Entire Agreement**

This Agreement (together with any Side Letters, Schedules, and Exhibits attached hereto) constitutes the entire agreement among the Partners with respect to the subject matter hereof and supersedes all prior and contemporaneous agreements, understandings, negotiations, representations, and warranties, whether oral or written, relating to such subject matter. No party has relied on any statement, representation, or warranty of any other party in entering into this Agreement, except as expressly set forth herein.
**Section 14.5 --- Severability**

If any term, provision, covenant, or restriction of this Agreement is held by a court of competent jurisdiction or by an arbitrator to be invalid, illegal, void, or unenforceable, the remainder of the terms, provisions, covenants, and restrictions of this Agreement shall remain in full force and effect and shall in no way be affected, impaired, or invalidated. In the event of any such holding, the parties shall negotiate in good faith to substitute for such invalid, illegal, void, or unenforceable provision a valid, legal, and enforceable provision that most closely approximates the economic effect and intent of the invalid, illegal, void, or unenforceable provision.
**Section 14.6 --- Successors and Assigns**

This Agreement shall be binding upon, and shall inure to the benefit of, the Partners and their respective permitted successors, assigns, heirs, executors, administrators, and legal representatives. Nothing in this Agreement shall confer upon any Partner the right to Transfer its Partnership Interest except in compliance with Article VIII.
**Section 14.7 --- Counterparts**

This Agreement may be executed in any number of counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original, and all of which together shall constitute one and the same instrument. Execution and delivery of this Agreement by electronic transmission (including by .pdf, DocuSign, or other electronic signature technology) shall constitute valid and effective execution and delivery for all purposes, and electronic signatures shall be deemed original signatures for all purposes under this Agreement.
**Section 14.8 --- No Third-Party Beneficiaries**

Except as expressly provided herein with respect to the indemnification of Covered Persons (including LPAC members) under Sections 7.9 and 9.4, nothing in this Agreement, express or implied, is intended to or shall confer upon any Person other than the parties hereto and their permitted successors and assigns any legal or equitable right, benefit, claim, or remedy of any nature whatsoever under or by reason of this Agreement.
**Section 14.9 --- Further Assurances**

Each Partner shall, upon reasonable request of the General Partner, execute and deliver such further instruments, agreements, and documents, and take such further actions, as may be reasonably necessary or desirable to carry out the purposes and intent of this Agreement, to consummate the transactions contemplated hereby, and to evidence the rights of the parties hereunder.
**Section 14.10 --- Governing Law**

This Agreement shall be governed by, and construed and enforced in accordance with, the laws of the State of Delaware, without regard to any principles of conflicts of law that would result in the application of the laws of any other jurisdiction. To the extent not preempted by the Act or other applicable Delaware law, the internal laws of the State of Delaware shall govern all aspects of this Agreement and the Partnership.
**Section 14.11 --- Dispute Resolution**

\(a\) Any dispute, controversy, or claim arising out of or relating to this Agreement, or the breach, termination, or validity thereof, shall be resolved by binding arbitration in New York, New York, administered by the American Arbitration Association in accordance with its Commercial Arbitration Rules then in effect. The arbitral tribunal shall consist of three (3) arbitrators, one selected by each disputing party and the third selected by the two party-appointed arbitrators. The language of the arbitration shall be English. The award rendered by the arbitral tribunal shall be final and binding upon the parties and may be entered and enforced in any court of competent jurisdiction.

\(b\) Notwithstanding Section 14.11(a), any party may seek temporary, preliminary, or permanent injunctive relief, specific performance, or other equitable relief from any court of competent jurisdiction, without the requirement of posting a bond or other security, where such relief is necessary to prevent irreparable harm.

\(c\) Each Partner irrevocably consents to the jurisdiction and venue of the federal and state courts located in the Borough of Manhattan, City of New York, State of New York, and in the Court of Chancery of the State of Delaware, for purposes of any action or proceeding permitted under this Section 14.11.

**\"Capital Contribution\"** means, with respect to each Partner, the aggregate amount of cash actually contributed by such Partner to the Partnership pursuant to this Agreement.

**\"Partnership Interest\"** means a Partner\'s interest in the Partnership, including such Partner\'s right to allocations of Net Profits and Net Losses, the right to receive distributions, and any other rights, benefits, and obligations of such Partner under this Agreement and applicable law.

Each Capital Call Notice shall be substantially in the form attached hereto as Exhibit A and shall be delivered in accordance with Section 12.03. The General Partner shall concurrently fund its pro rata share of each Capital Call on the applicable Funding Date.

(as set forth on Schedule C attached hereto, or as otherwise updated by the General Partner from time to time).

\(a\) If any Partner fails to make all or any portion of a required Capital Contribution within five (5) Business Days after the applicable Funding Date (such failure, a \"Default,\" and such Partner, a \"Defaulting Partner\"), the General Partner (or, if the General Partner is the Defaulting Partner, the Limited Partner) shall deliver written notice to the Defaulting Partner specifying the amount of the deficiency and demanding immediate payment thereof.

> \(i\) **Interest.** The Defaulting Partner shall pay interest on the unpaid amount of its Capital Contribution at the rate of twelve percent (12%) per annum (or, if less, the maximum rate permitted by applicable law), calculated from the applicable Funding Date until the date of payment in full;

> \(v\) **Shortfall Funding.** The non-defaulting Partner shall have the right (but not the obligation) to fund the shortfall amount, in which case the non-defaulting Partner shall receive additional Capital Account credit equal to the amount funded plus an additional amount equal to interest at twelve percent (12%) per annum from the applicable Funding Date to the date of such funding by the non-defaulting Partner.

Pursuant to Section 3.01 of the LP Agreement, the General Partner has exclusive authority to manage and control the business and affairs of the Partnership. This broad grant of authority is consistent with the default rules under DRULPA and with customary market practice for sponsor-led co-investment vehicles. Specifically, the General Partner\'s authority includes, without limitation, the following:
> \(b\) issuing capital calls to the partners and managing capital contributions in accordance with the terms of the LP Agreement;
> \(c\) making distributions to the partners in accordance with the distribution waterfall set forth in Section 6.01 of the LP Agreement;

> \(d\) executing transaction documents on behalf of the Partnership, including the Equity Purchase Agreement, ancillary acquisition agreements, financing agreements, and all other instruments and documents necessary or desirable in connection with the Cascadia acquisition;

> \(g\) taking all actions necessary or desirable in connection with the Cascadia acquisition, including the negotiation and execution of the Equity Purchase Agreement, the stockholders\' agreement, the management services agreement, and all related transaction documents; and

Notwithstanding the broad grant of authority to the General Partner described above, the LP Agreement imposes certain limitations on the General Partner\'s authority. Specifically, the General Partner may not take any of the following actions without the prior written consent of the Limited Partner (Ironside):
> \(a\) amend, modify, or waive any provision of the LP Agreement or the Side Letter;

> \(f\) enter into any related-party transaction (including any transaction with the General Partner, its affiliates, Fund IV, or their respective principals, officers, or employees) that is not expressly contemplated by the LP Agreement or the Co-Investment Allocation Agreement; and
> \(g\) extend the investment period or term of the Partnership beyond the limits set forth in the LP Agreement.

These consent requirements are designed to protect Ironside\'s interests as the sole limited partner and to ensure that the General Partner does not take any material action that could adversely affect Ironside\'s investment without Ironside\'s knowledge and approval. The consent requirements are consistent with market practice for single-LP co-investment vehicles and reflect the negotiated balance of authority between the General Partner and the Limited Partner.

No formal Limited Partner Advisory Committee (\"LPAC\") is established under the LP Agreement. The absence of a formal LPAC is appropriate given the single-LP structure of the Vehicle --- there is no need for a committee to represent the interests of multiple limited partners, as Ironside is the sole limited partner and has direct consent rights on all material matters.

In lieu of a formal LPAC, the Side Letter provides for direct consultation between the General Partner and Ironside on material matters affecting the Partnership and its investment. The GP has agreed to consult with Ironside in good faith on matters that would customarily be brought before an LPAC in a multi-investor fund, including conflict-of-interest matters, related-party transactions, valuation issues, and material deviations from the investment thesis.

The Co-Investment Allocation Agreement governs the parallel investment mechanics between Fund IV and the Vehicle, ensuring that both entities participate in the acquisition and all subsequent investment decisions on a pro rata basis (28.57% Vehicle / 71.43% Fund IV). The Co-Investment Allocation Agreement provides for parallel economic treatment, meaning that Fund IV and the Vehicle receive the same terms with respect to the acquisition, any subsequent investments, and the ultimate disposition of the investment, subject to differences in their respective economic terms (e.g., the Vehicle\'s lower carried interest rate).

Any deviation from the pro rata allocation set forth in the Co-Investment Allocation Agreement requires the prior written consent of the Limited Partner (Ironside). This provision protects Ironside against dilution or adverse reallocation of investment economics as between Fund IV and the Vehicle.

Under the LP Agreement, the General Partner owes fiduciary duties to the Partnership and its partners. These duties are, however, subject to the modifications and limitations permitted under the Delaware Revised Uniform Limited Partnership Act, which provides substantial flexibility to the parties to a limited partnership agreement to define and modify the fiduciary duties owed by the general partner.
The LP Agreement modifies the default fiduciary duties as follows:

**Duty of Loyalty.** The duty of loyalty owed by the General Partner is preserved but is qualified to account for the General Partner\'s role as the sponsor of Fund IV and other investment vehicles. Specifically, the LP Agreement provides that the General Partner and its affiliates (including Meridian and Fund IV) may engage in other business activities, including activities that compete with or are similar to the Partnership\'s business, without any obligation to account to the Partnership for any profits or benefits derived from such activities. This qualification is necessary to accommodate the General Partner\'s role as the general partner of Fund IV and its other investment activities, and the specific allocation as between Fund IV and the Vehicle is governed by the Co-Investment Allocation Agreement.

The LP Agreement includes a customary exculpation provision that limits the personal liability of the General Partner and certain related persons in connection with the Partnership\'s activities. Specifically, the General Partner and its affiliates, managers, members, officers, and employees (collectively, the \"Covered Persons\") are exculpated from liability to the Partnership or the Limited Partner for any act or omission taken or suffered in good faith and reasonably believed by the applicable Covered Person to be within the scope of the authority conferred by the LP Agreement, except to the extent that such act or omission constitutes gross negligence, willful misconduct, fraud, or bad faith.

The LP Agreement provides for indemnification of the Covered Persons by the Partnership against losses, damages, liabilities, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys\' fees and expenses) arising out of or in connection with the Partnership\'s activities. The indemnification obligation is subject to the same carve-outs applicable to the exculpation provision --- indemnification is not available to the extent that the conduct giving rise to the claim constitutes gross negligence, willful misconduct, fraud, or bad faith.

> • The LP Agreement permits advancement of expenses (including attorneys\' fees) to Covered Persons in connection with pending or threatened proceedings, subject to an undertaking by the applicable Covered Person to repay such amounts if it is ultimately determined that indemnification is not available under the terms of the LP Agreement.

The fiduciary duty, exculpation, and indemnification provisions of the LP Agreement have been drafted in accordance with the requirements and limitations of DRULPA. Several provisions of DRULPA are particularly relevant:

**Implied Covenant of Good Faith and Fair Dealing.** In accordance with DRULPA Section 17-1101(d), the LP Agreement expressly preserves the implied contractual covenant of good faith and fair dealing. This covenant provides a baseline level of protection for the Limited Partner against arbitrary or opportunistic conduct by the General Partner, even in areas where the LP Agreement has modified or limited the General Partner\'s fiduciary duties. Delaware courts have consistently held that the implied covenant serves as a gap-filling mechanism to address situations not expressly covered by the partnership agreement, and the preservation of this covenant in the LP Agreement is both appropriate and consistent with best practices.

The modifications to default fiduciary duties set forth in the LP Agreement are within the range of market practice for Delaware limited partnerships in the private equity and infrastructure asset classes and have been reviewed and approved by the Responsible Partner.

The LP Agreement reserves certain matters for the vote or written consent of the Limited Partner (Ironside). Given the single-LP structure of the Vehicle, the Limited Partner\'s vote or consent is, as a practical matter, the sole determinative vote on reserved matters. The matters requiring the Limited Partner\'s consent are as follows:
> \(a\) any amendment, modification, or waiver of any provision of the LP Agreement, including any exhibit or schedule thereto;
> \(f\) any related-party transaction not expressly contemplated by the LP Agreement or the Co-Investment Allocation Agreement; and
> \(g\) any extension of the investment period or the term of the Partnership beyond the limits set forth in the LP Agreement.

These voting rights provide Ironside with meaningful control over the fundamental terms and structure of the Partnership and its investment, while leaving day-to-day management and investment decisions to the General Partner. The scope of the reserved matters is consistent with market practice for single-LP co-investment vehicles and reflects the negotiated allocation of authority between the parties.

The General Partner has sole voting authority on all matters not expressly reserved to the Limited Partner, including all investment decisions, operational decisions, and administrative matters. The General Partner\'s authority in these areas is exercised without the need for Limited Partner consent, except as otherwise specifically provided in the LP Agreement or the Side Letter.

Given the two-party structure of the Vehicle, the LP Agreement adopts streamlined voting and consent mechanics. Votes and consents may be given in writing, which includes delivery by electronic mail, and are effective upon receipt by the General Partner or the Limited Partner, as applicable. No formal meeting procedures, quorum requirements, or record-date mechanics are required or contemplated by the LP Agreement, as such provisions are unnecessary in a two-party partnership.

All notices, requests for consent, and other communications between the partners are to be delivered in accordance with the notice provisions of the LP Agreement (Section 10.01), which provide for delivery by hand, by nationally recognized overnight courier, by registered or certified mail (return receipt requested), or by electronic mail, in each case to the addresses set forth in the LP Agreement or such other addresses as the parties may designate from time to time.

The LP Agreement provides the Limited Partner with the right to remove the General Partner \"for cause\" upon written notice to the General Partner. Removal for cause is effective immediately upon delivery of the written notice or upon such later date as may be specified in the notice. The LP Agreement defines \"Cause\" as any of the following events:
> \(a\) fraud, willful misconduct, or gross negligence by the General Partner in the performance of its duties under the LP Agreement;

> \(b\) a material breach by the General Partner of any provision of the LP Agreement that is not cured by the General Partner within thirty (30) days after written notice of such breach from the Limited Partner;

The LP Agreement does not provide for the removal of the General Partner without cause. The absence of a no-fault removal right is a common feature in co-investment vehicles where the General Partner is the sponsor of the main fund (here, Fund IV). The rationale for this approach is that the General Partner\'s role in managing the co-investment is closely tied to its role in managing the main fund, and removal of the General Partner from the co-investment vehicle without cause could create governance and operational complexities for the broader investment program.

Ironside\'s primary remedy in circumstances falling short of \"Cause\" is the exercise of its wind-down election right under Section 7.04(c) of the LP Agreement (discussed in Section IX.D of this memorandum), which permits Ironside to elect to wind down the Partnership following an extended dormancy period without the need to establish cause for removal.
Upon removal of the General Partner for cause, the following consequences apply under the LP Agreement:

> \(a\) **Appointment of Successor General Partner.** The Limited Partner has the right to appoint a successor general partner in its sole discretion. The successor general partner may be an affiliate of Ironside, a third-party manager, or any other person designated by the Limited Partner. The successor general partner assumes all rights, duties, and obligations of the removed General Partner under the LP Agreement, subject to any modifications agreed to by the parties.

> \(b\) **Conversion of Removed GP\'s Interest.** Upon removal, the removed General Partner\'s partnership interest (0.01%) is automatically converted to a limited partner interest. The converted interest retains economic rights (i.e., the right to receive distributions in respect of capital contributions), but the removed General Partner has no management authority, voting rights, or other governance rights with respect to the Partnership. Importantly, the removed General Partner has no entitlement to carried interest on distributions made after the date of removal. Carried interest accrued prior to the date of removal is subject to the clawback and settlement provisions of the LP Agreement, which require the removed General Partner to return any excess carried interest previously received.

Given the single-purpose, single-LP nature of the Vehicle, removal of the General Partner would likely be exercised only in extreme circumstances involving fraud, willful misconduct, gross negligence, or material breach. In practice, the more typical remedy for disagreements between the General Partner and the Limited Partner --- particularly during periods of dormancy or reduced investment activity --- would be the exercise of the wind-down election right under Section 7.04(c) of the LP Agreement, as discussed in Section IX.D below.

C&H has reviewed the GP removal provisions of the LP Agreement and confirms that they are consistent with market practice for single-LP co-investment vehicles and with the requirements of Delaware law. The removal provisions have been negotiated with Breckenridge Sloane & Pratt LLP (counsel to the General Partner) and reflect a balanced approach that protects Ironside\'s interests while providing appropriate protections for the General Partner against arbitrary or pretextual removal.
**[A. LP Information Rights Under LP Agreement]{.underline}**

The LP Agreement provides the Limited Partner (Ironside) with comprehensive information rights that are designed to ensure that Ironside has timely and complete access to information regarding the Partnership\'s financial condition, investment status, and material developments. The LP\'s information rights under the LP Agreement include the following:

**Ad Hoc Notices.** The General Partner is required to provide prompt written notice to the Limited Partner of any material event affecting the Partnership or the underlying investment, including, without limitation, the occurrence of a Material Impediment Event (as defined in Section 7.04 of the LP Agreement), a Material Adverse Effect with respect to Cascadia, material regulatory developments, material litigation or regulatory proceedings, and any other event that could reasonably be expected to have a material impact on the Partnership\'s investment or operations.

In addition to the information rights provided under the LP Agreement, the Side Letter provides Ironside with enhanced information and reporting rights that go beyond the standard provisions of the LP Agreement. These enhanced rights reflect Ironside\'s position as the sole limited partner and its significant capital commitment to the Vehicle. The enhanced reporting provisions include the following:

> \(a\) **Quarterly Dormancy Reports.** During any period of dormancy (i.e., during the pendency of a Material Impediment Event and the associated suspension of capital calls and investment activity), the General Partner is required to deliver quarterly status reports to the Limited Partner, in addition to the standard quarterly reports required under the LP Agreement. These dormancy reports must include specific detail on the status of the underlying investment, the status of any concession renegotiations, regulatory approvals, financing commitments, and any other material developments relating to the Partnership or the Cascadia acquisition.

> \(d\) **Most-Favored-Nation Provision.** If the General Partner grants any other co-investor (in a parallel or successor co-investment vehicle) more favorable information, reporting, or governance rights than those provided to Ironside under the LP Agreement or the Side Letter, Ironside is entitled to receive the same or equivalent rights. The MFN provision ensures that Ironside is not disadvantaged relative to any other co-investor and provides a mechanism for the automatic enhancement of Ironside\'s rights in the event that more favorable terms are offered to other parties.

The General Partner is required under the LP Agreement to maintain complete and accurate books and records of the Partnership at its principal office, which is currently located at 200 Clarendon Street, Suite 4200, Boston, Massachusetts 02116, or such other location as the General Partner may designate from time to time upon notice to the Limited Partner.

The books and records maintained by the General Partner include, without limitation, the Certificate of Limited Partnership, the LP Agreement and all amendments thereto, the Side Letter, the Co-Investment Allocation Agreement, financial statements, tax returns, capital account records, records of capital contributions and distributions, and all other documents and records reasonably necessary for the proper administration of the Partnership.

All information provided to the Limited Partner pursuant to the LP Agreement or the Side Letter is subject to customary confidentiality restrictions. The Limited Partner is required to maintain the confidentiality of all non-public information received in connection with the Partnership and may not disclose such information to any third party, except as follows:

The confidentiality provisions of the LP Agreement are reciprocal --- the General Partner is also subject to confidentiality obligations with respect to non-public information regarding the Limited Partner.
**[A. Material Impediment Event (§7.04 of LP Agreement)]{.underline}**

The LP Agreement includes provisions addressing the possibility that the Cascadia acquisition may encounter material obstacles or impediments that prevent or delay the closing of the transaction. Pursuant to Section 7.04 of the LP Agreement, the General Partner may declare a \"Material Impediment Event\" and suspend capital calls and investment activity upon its determination that either:

> \(b\) a Material Adverse Effect (as defined in the Equity Purchase Agreement governing the Cascadia acquisition) has occurred or is reasonably expected to occur with respect to Cascadia or its business, properties, or financial condition.

The Material Impediment Event provisions are designed to provide a structured framework for addressing significant obstacles to the Cascadia acquisition, including regulatory delays, financing disruptions, adverse changes in the target\'s business, and other events that could prevent or materially delay the closing of the transaction.

During the pendency of a Material Impediment Event, no further capital calls may be issued by the General Partner. The Limited Partner\'s unfunded capital commitment remains in place during the dormancy period but is not callable by the General Partner until such time as the General Partner determines that the Material Impediment Event has been resolved or the Limited Partner elects to wind down the Partnership in accordance with Section 7.04(c) of the LP Agreement.

These quarterly dormancy reports are in addition to the standard quarterly reports required under the LP Agreement and are intended to provide Ironside with specific, detailed, and timely information regarding the status of the dormancy and the prospects for the Cascadia acquisition.

> \(c\) Remaining assets of the Partnership, including any deposits, reserves, escrow amounts, and insurance interests, are distributed to the partners net of expenses and outstanding obligations, in accordance with the distribution waterfall set forth in Section 6.01 of the LP Agreement (see Section XI of this memorandum).

It is important to note that the wind-down election right is permissive, not mandatory. If the Limited Partner does not elect to wind down the Partnership after the eighteen-month period, the dormancy continues, subject to the General Partner\'s ongoing quarterly reporting obligations and other duties under the LP Agreement. The Limited Partner may exercise the wind-down election right at any time after the expiration of the eighteen-month period.

If the Material Impediment Event is resolved prior to the Limited Partner\'s exercise of the wind-down election right, the General Partner may reactivate the Vehicle by delivering written notice of reactivation to the Limited Partner. Upon reactivation, the General Partner may recommence capital calls in accordance with Section 4.01 of the LP Agreement and proceed with the Cascadia acquisition.

The LP Agreement does not establish a fixed term (e.g., ten years) for the Partnership, which is typical for single-purpose co-investment vehicles. The term is instead tied to the life of the underlying investment, with appropriate dissolution triggers for scenarios in which the investment cannot be completed or is no longer viable.

Upon dissolution of the Partnership, the General Partner (or a liquidating trustee appointed by the Limited Partner if the General Partner has been removed) is responsible for winding up the Partnership\'s affairs. The winding-up process includes the liquidation of the Partnership\'s assets, the satisfaction of the Partnership\'s liabilities and obligations (including any indemnification obligations), and the distribution of remaining proceeds to the partners in accordance with the distribution waterfall set forth in Section 6.01 of the LP Agreement.
Distributions of available cash or other property by the Partnership to its partners are made in the following order of priority, as set forth in Section 6.01 of the LP Agreement:

The LP Agreement imposes customary restrictions on the transfer of partnership interests. Neither the General Partner nor the Limited Partner may transfer, assign, pledge, or otherwise dispose of its interest in the Partnership without the prior written consent of the other partner, except as follows:

> \(a\) **Transfers by the LP.** The Limited Partner may transfer its interest in the Partnership to one or more affiliates of Ironside Capital Management LP without the prior consent of the General Partner, subject to customary conditions, including (i) compliance with applicable federal and state securities laws, (ii) delivery by the transferee of a joinder agreement pursuant to which the transferee agrees to be bound by the terms of the LP Agreement, and (iii) delivery of such opinions of counsel and other documentation as the General Partner may reasonably request.

These transfer restrictions are designed to preserve the integrity of the partnership structure and to ensure that neither party may unilaterally introduce a new partner or alter the governance dynamics of the Vehicle without the consent of the other party.

The following is a summary of the key tax and regulatory considerations applicable to the Partnership. This summary is provided for informational purposes only and does not constitute a comprehensive analysis of the tax or regulatory issues applicable to the Vehicle. Detailed analyses of these matters are set forth in the separate memoranda referenced below.

> 1\. **Execution of Transaction Documents.** The LP Agreement, Side Letter, Co-Investment Allocation Agreement, and Subscription Agreement are anticipated to be executed by all parties on July 29, 2022, at first close.

> 4\. **Ongoing Advisory Role.** Calderwood & Harkness LLP will continue to advise Ironside Capital Management LP on all matters relating to the Vehicle\'s governance, the underlying Cascadia acquisition (including review of the Equity Purchase Agreement and ancillary transaction documents), and ongoing compliance with the LP Agreement, the Side Letter, and applicable law.
> • Placement Agent Agreement Review Memorandum, dated July 18, 2022
Please do not hesitate to contact the undersigned or any member of the Calderwood & Harkness team with questions regarding this memorandum or any aspect of the Vehicle\'s formation and governance.
