===== documents/matters/1023-00001/Engagement/engagement-letter-ironside.docx =====

Calderwood & Harkness LLP (\"C&H\" or the \"Firm\") is pleased to confirm its engagement by Ironside Capital Management LP (\"Ironside\" or the \"Client\"), a Delaware limited partnership, to serve as outside legal counsel in connection with the matters described in Sections 1.1 through 1.4 below (collectively, the \"Engagement\"). The scope of representation is subject to the limitations set forth in Section 1.5. Unless otherwise agreed in writing, the Firm\'s representation shall be limited to the specific matters described herein and shall not extend to other legal matters of the Client or any of its affiliates.

> \(b\) Negotiation, drafting, and review of the Agreement of Limited Partnership of the Co-Investment Vehicle (the \"LPA\"), including provisions relating to capital commitments, capital calls, management and governance, distributions (including the distribution waterfall), carried interest allocations, fees and expenses, transfer restrictions, key-person provisions, default remedies, reporting obligations, term and dissolution, indemnification, and such other terms as may be agreed upon by the parties;

> \(d\) Negotiation and review of the Co-Investment Allocation Agreement between Fund IV and the Co-Investment Vehicle, which is expected to set forth the terms and conditions governing the allocation of the co-investment opportunity, including the relative commitments, co-investment allocation methodology, expense-sharing arrangements, and the rights and obligations of Fund IV and the Co-Investment Vehicle with respect to the Cascadia investment;
> \(h\) Such other matters as may be reasonably necessary or desirable in connection with the formation and organization of the Co-Investment Vehicle.

> \(a\) Legal due diligence review of Cascadia and its direct and indirect subsidiaries (collectively, the \"Tarvex Group\") in connection with the proposed acquisition, including review of corporate organizational documents, material contracts, real property interests, intellectual property, permits and licenses, environmental matters, employment matters, litigation and pending claims, regulatory compliance, tax matters, and such other areas as may be identified during the course of the diligence process. The Firm anticipates coordinating its diligence efforts with the broader diligence workstream being managed by Breckenridge Sloane & Pratt LLP (\"BSP\") on behalf of Meridian Infrastructure Partners LP (\"Meridian\") as lead sponsor of the Transaction;

> \(b\) Review, negotiation, and comment on the Equity Purchase Agreement (the \"Purchase Agreement\") and related transaction documentation (including disclosure schedules, ancillary agreements, officer\'s certificates, and closing deliverables), to the extent that Ironside\'s interests as co-investor require separate or supplemental representation beyond the work being performed by BSP on behalf of Meridian. The Client acknowledges that BSP is serving as lead transaction counsel to the buy-side and that the Firm\'s role with respect to the Purchase Agreement is supplemental in nature, focused on ensuring that Ironside\'s specific interests, rights, and obligations as co-investor are adequately addressed;
> \(e\) Such other transaction-related matters as may arise and as may be reasonably necessary to protect Ironside\'s interests as co-investor in the Transaction.

The Firm will advise and assist the Client in connection with the analysis and assessment of regulatory approvals and filings required for the consummation of the Transaction, as they affect Ironside\'s co-investment position. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, our work in connection with regulatory matters is expected to include the following:
> \(e\) Such other regulatory matters as may arise in connection with the Transaction and as may be reasonably necessary to protect Ironside\'s interests.

> \(a\) Ongoing advice on the governance of the Co-Investment Vehicle, including matters relating to capital calls, distributions, investor communications and reporting, advisory committee proceedings, consent solicitations, and limited partner relations;

> \(b\) Tax structuring analysis and ongoing tax advice relating to the Co-Investment Vehicle, including advice on federal, state, and local tax matters, partnership tax allocations, withholding obligations, UBTI analysis, and any tax elections or filings to be made by or on behalf of the Co-Investment Vehicle. Tax advice will be provided in coordination with the Firm\'s Tax Practice Group, led by Ms. Sylvia Hartwell;
> \(f\) Such other ongoing matters as may arise from time to time in connection with the Co-Investment Vehicle or Ironside\'s participation therein.

The Client acknowledges and agrees that the scope of the Firm\'s representation is limited to the matters described in Sections 1.1 through 1.4 above. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, the Client acknowledges the following:

> \(c\) C&H\'s representation of the Client is limited to the matters expressly described in this engagement letter and does not extend to any general corporate, regulatory, compliance, litigation, employment, intellectual property, or other legal matters of Ironside or any of its affiliated entities, funds, portfolio companies, general partners, officers, directors, employees, or agents, unless separately agreed in a written engagement letter or amendment to this engagement letter.
The following attorneys have been assigned to the Engagement and will have primary responsibility for the delivery of legal services to the Client:

**Responsible Partner:** Pamela Cross, Partner, Funds & Asset Management Practice Group. Ms. Cross will have overall supervisory responsibility for the Engagement and will serve as the primary relationship partner for Ironside. Ms. Cross brings more than twenty years of experience advising institutional investors, fund sponsors, and asset managers on fund formation, co-investment structuring, and complex transactional matters. She will be available to the Client for strategic guidance, senior-level negotiations, and resolution of any significant issues that may arise during the course of the Engagement.

**Billing Partner:** Nicholas Stern, Partner, Funds & Asset Management Practice Group. Mr. Stern will serve as the billing partner and will be responsible for staffing, billing, day-to-day management, and overall work coordination for the Engagement. Mr. Stern has extensive experience in the formation and structuring of private equity, infrastructure, and co-investment vehicles, and in the negotiation of fund documentation and side letters on behalf of institutional investors and sponsors.

**Lead Associate:** Theresa Kim, Associate, Funds & Asset Management Practice Group. Ms. Kim will serve as the lead associate on the matter and will be the primary day-to-day contact for Ironside\'s deal team. Ms. Kim will be responsible for the preparation of initial drafts of fund formation documents, coordination of the diligence process, management of the document production and review workflow, and regular communication with the Client regarding the status of the Engagement.

**Working Associate:** Owen Fischer, Associate, Funds & Asset Management Practice Group. Mr. Fischer will provide additional associate-level support as needed, including assistance with due diligence, regulatory analysis, document review, and drafting of ancillary transaction documents.

**Tax Specialist:** Sylvia Hartwell, Partner, Tax Practice Group. Ms. Hartwell will advise the Client on tax structuring, partnership tax matters, federal and state income tax issues, and state and local tax considerations relating to the Co-Investment Vehicle. Ms. Hartwell has deep expertise in the taxation of private investment funds and co-investment vehicles and will coordinate closely with the Funds & Asset Management team to ensure that the structure of the Co-Investment Vehicle is optimized from a tax perspective.

Fees for legal services rendered in connection with this Engagement will be charged on an hourly basis at the Firm\'s standard rates in effect at the time the services are rendered. The Firm\'s hourly rates are reviewed and adjusted annually, with adjustments typically taking effect on January 1 of each calendar year. The Firm will provide the Client with prior written notice of any rate adjustments. Current standard hourly rate ranges for the categories of professionals assigned to this matter are as follows:
The specific hourly rates applicable to the attorneys currently assigned to this matter are set forth below:

Rates for any additional attorneys, paralegals, or other professionals assigned to the Engagement will be communicated to the Client upon assignment and will be consistent with the Firm\'s standard rate schedule for professionals of comparable seniority and experience. The rates set forth above are subject to annual adjustment as described in this Section 3.1.

The Firm does not provide fee caps, fixed-fee arrangements, or \"not-to-exceed\" budgets for this Engagement. The nature and complexity of fund formation and co-investment structuring matters, and the transactional and regulatory work associated with a transaction of this magnitude, make it impracticable to predict total legal fees with certainty at the outset of the Engagement.

However, the Firm is prepared to provide the Client with periodic, non-binding estimates of anticipated fees for specific phases of the work upon request. Such estimates will be based on the Firm\'s best assessment of the work required at the time of the estimate and will be subject to revision as the scope and complexity of the Engagement evolve. The Client acknowledges and agrees that actual fees will depend on, among other things, the scope and complexity of the matters as they develop, the extent and depth of the legal due diligence required, the pace and complexity of negotiations among the parties, the nature and timing of regulatory filings and approvals, and any dormancy, reactivation, or wind-down proceedings relating to the Co-Investment Vehicle that may arise during the term of the Engagement.

The Client acknowledges that Calderwood & Harkness LLP is a large, diversified law firm with hundreds of attorneys and numerous clients across a wide range of industries and practice areas. The Client understands and agrees that the Firm may currently represent, or may in the future represent, other entities, funds, or individuals whose interests may differ from or be adverse to those of Ironside in matters unrelated to this Engagement. The Firm does not, by reason of this Engagement, undertake any obligation to decline or withdraw from the representation of any other client in any matter not substantially related to this Engagement. The Firm will at all times comply with its ethical obligations and the applicable rules of professional conduct in managing any situations that may arise involving the concurrent representation of clients with differing interests.

The Firm will maintain all files, documents, and records relating to this Engagement (whether in physical or electronic form) in accordance with the Firm\'s standard document retention policies as in effect from time to time. Upon the conclusion of the Engagement, whether by completion of the matters described herein, termination pursuant to Section 7, or otherwise, the Firm will retain files relating to the Engagement for a period of not less than seven (7) years from the date of conclusion of the Engagement. Following the expiration of such seven-year period, the Firm may, in its discretion, destroy or dispose of such files without further notice to the Client, unless the Client has, prior to the expiration of such period, made a written request for the return of the files.

The Client may request the return of original documents, including but not limited to executed agreements, certificates, corporate records, and other original instruments, at any time during or after the Engagement. The Firm will comply with any such request within a reasonable period of time, and the Client will bear any reasonable costs associated with the retrieval, copying, and delivery of such documents.

Upon termination, the Firm will cooperate fully in the orderly transition of the matter to successor counsel designated by the Client, if applicable, including by making available to successor counsel all files, documents, and work product relating to the Engagement (subject to payment of all outstanding fees and expenses) and by providing such reasonable assistance as successor counsel may request to facilitate a seamless transition.

We are delighted to have the opportunity to represent Ironside Capital Management LP in connection with this important co-investment opportunity and look forward to a productive working relationship. If the terms set forth in this engagement letter are acceptable to you, please confirm your agreement by countersigning and returning a copy of this letter to the undersigned at Calderwood & Harkness LLP, 125 Broad Street, 44th Floor, New York, New York 10004, or by email to Pamela Cross (pcross@calderwoodharkness.com) and Nicholas Stern (nstern@calderwoodharkness.com). Your countersignature will constitute your acknowledgment and acceptance of the terms and conditions of this engagement letter.

Line 372: **3.1.1 Formation of Holding Company Structure.** The centerpiece of the restructuring was the formation of a new two-tier holding company structure to replace the prior arrangement under which five individual principals held direct membership interests in both the GP and ManCo. Under the pre-restructuring arrangement, each of the five principals (Aldridge, Narayanan, Kellner, Trask, and Hsiao) held direct ownership percentages in both ManCo and the GP. **[1. Purpose and Engagement]{.underline}**

The engagement encompasses the formation of new holding entities, the negotiation of separation arrangements with departing principals, the realignment of carried interest and management fee economics among continuing and next-generation principals, the solicitation of necessary limited partner consents, compliance with existing side-letter obligations, and related tax structuring. The scope of the representation, the personnel assigned to the engagement, the fee arrangement, and other terms and conditions governing this engagement are set forth in the sections that follow.

\(f\) Preparing Amendment No. 1 to the Amended and Restated Agreement of Limited Partnership of the Fund (the \"LPA\") to reflect the structural changes to the General Partner, including any required modifications to the definitions, representations, and governance provisions of the LPA necessitated by the interposition of GP Intermediate and HoldCo above the General Partner.

\(a\) Preparing materials for notification to, and solicitation of consent from, the Limited Partner Advisory Committee (\"LPAC\") pursuant to Section 9.4 of the LPA, including a detailed memorandum describing the restructuring and its implications for the Fund and its limited partners.

\(b\) Analyzing compliance with the Fund\'s fourteen (14) existing side letters, with particular attention to key-person provisions under Section 5.2 of the LPA and any expanded or supplemental key-person provisions contained in certain side letters, to determine whether the departures of Mr. Kellner and Ms. Trask or the structural changes contemplated by the restructuring trigger key-person events, consent requirements, or notification obligations under any such side letter.

\(c\) Preparing LP notification letters to all forty-seven (47) limited partners of the Fund, describing the restructuring, the changes to the General Partner structure, the departures of Mr. Kellner and Ms. Trask, and any other information required to be disclosed under the LPA or the applicable side letters.

From time to time, additional attorneys or paraprofessionals may be assigned to the engagement as the Firm deems necessary or appropriate to ensure efficient and timely completion of the workstreams described herein. The Client will be notified in advance of any such additions to the engagement team.

This Engagement Letter may be executed in one or more counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original and all of which together shall constitute one and the same instrument. Delivery of an executed counterpart by electronic mail in portable document format (.pdf) or by other electronic transmission shall be effective as delivery of a manually executed counterpart.
The undersigned, on behalf of Ardent Capital Management LLC, hereby acknowledge receipt of the foregoing Engagement Letter and agree to the terms and conditions set forth therein.

Under the pre-restructuring arrangement, each of the five principals (Aldridge, Narayanan, Kellner, Trask, and Hsiao) held direct ownership percentages in both ManCo and the GP. This structure presented several challenges: (i) the departure of any principal required direct amendments to the governing documents of both ManCo and the GP, together with the re-execution of multiple ancillary agreements; (ii) the admission of new principals similarly required direct amendments at both the ManCo and GP levels; (iii) the platform lacked a centralized governance structure capable of facilitating efficient decision-making and succession planning; and (iv) the direct ownership structure created inefficiencies in connection with tax reporting, capital account administration, and allocation mechanics.

This structure permits future changes in principal-level ownership, economics, and governance to be accomplished through amendments to the HoldCo LLC Agreement alone, without the need to amend the governing documents of ManCo, the GP, or the Fund (except in circumstances requiring LP notification or consent under the LPA).

**Re:** Ardent Capital Partners III LP --- Notification of Proposed Management Company Restructuring, Economics Realignment, and Departures of Senior Principals; Solicitation of LPAC Consent Pursuant to Section 9.4 of the Amended and Restated Agreement of Limited Partnership
**[1. Introduction and Purpose]{.underline}**

Ardent Capital GP III LLC (the \"**General Partner**\"), as the sole general partner of Ardent Capital Partners III LP (the \"**Fund**\" or \"**Fund III**\"), is writing to provide notification of, and to solicit the consent of the Limited Partner Advisory Committee (the \"**LPAC**\" or the \"**Committee**\") to, a proposed restructuring of the management company and related realignment of economics among the Fund\'s principals (the \"**Restructuring**\"). This letter sets forth the material terms and circumstances of the Restructuring in detail, together with the background and rationale therefor, and identifies the specific consents being requested of the LPAC in connection therewith.

The consent of the LPAC is being solicited pursuant to **Section 9.4** of the Amended and Restated Agreement of Limited Partnership of the Fund, dated as of April 15, 2019 (as amended, supplemented, or otherwise modified from time to time, the \"**LPA**\"), which requires LPAC consent for certain material structural changes to the General Partner, the management company, or the economic arrangements among the principals, including without limitation any change in the ownership or control of the General Partner, any material amendment to the organizational documents of the General Partner, and any material realignment of the carried interest or management fee economics of the Fund.

The General Partner respectfully requests that each LPAC member review this letter and the enclosed materials carefully and execute and return the enclosed Form of Written Consent (the \"**Consent**\") at or prior to the LPAC meeting scheduled for **February 14, 2024**, which will be held virtually via videoconference. Details regarding the videoconference will be provided under separate cover. LPAC members may deliver their consent either by execution and return of the enclosed Consent in advance of the meeting or by affirmative vote at the meeting itself.

In connection with the Restructuring, the General Partner has engaged **Calderwood & Harkness LLP** (Nicholas Stern, responsible partner, and Owen Fischer, lead associate) as restructuring counsel to advise the General Partner on the structural, governance, and transactional aspects of the Restructuring. **Pemberton Hale LLP** (Victoria Langford, responsible partner) continues to serve as fund counsel for routine Fund operations and has provided guidance on LPA interpretation and side-letter compliance matters. The General Partner wishes to note that Calderwood & Harkness LLP and Pemberton Hale LLP represent the General Partner and the Fund, respectively, and do not represent any individual limited partner or the LPAC. LPAC members are encouraged to consult with their own legal and tax advisors as they deem appropriate.

**Fund Term.** The term of the Fund is scheduled to expire on **December 31, 2029**, subject to two one-year extensions at the discretion of the General Partner in accordance with Section 12.1 of the LPA.

**Carried Interest.** The General Partner is entitled to receive carried interest equal to **20%** of the Fund\'s net profits (calculated on a whole-Fund basis), subject to an **8% per annum preferred return** to the limited partners and a **100% catch-up** to the General Partner thereafter, in each case as more fully described in Section 6.2 of the LPA.

> 3\. **Departing Principal Separation** --- the orderly departure and separation of two senior principals, David Kellner and Joanna Trask, and the negotiation and execution of their respective separation and release agreements; and

> 4\. **LP Consent and Side-Letter Compliance** --- the solicitation of LPAC consent as required under the LPA and compliance with notification and consent provisions contained in individual side letters.

**Current Structure Being Replaced.** Under the current organizational structure, the five individual principals (Aldridge, Narayanan, Kellner, Trask, and Hsiao) hold direct membership interests in both the General Partner and the Management Company. The direct-ownership model was adopted at the time of the Fund\'s formation for simplicity, but as Ardent Capital has grown and matured as an institution, the General Partner has determined that a consolidated holding company structure is more appropriate and consistent with industry best practices for institutional-quality private equity platforms. The holding company structure also facilitates the admission and withdrawal of individual principals without requiring amendments to the organizational documents of the General Partner or the Management Company, thereby reducing administrative burden and the need for LP consents in connection with future personnel changes (to the extent otherwise permitted under the LPA).

> • **Separation Payment:** Ms. Trask will receive a one-time lump-sum separation payment of **\$1,250,000**, payable within 30 days following her departure date, in consideration of her execution of a general release of claims and compliance with her ongoing restrictive covenants.

Both departures are subject to the terms of negotiated separation and release agreements (each, a \"**Separation Agreement**\") that are currently being finalized. Mr. Kellner and Ms. Trask are each independently represented by **Whitford & Chase LLP** (Richard Beaulieu, partner) in connection with the negotiation of their respective Separation Agreements. Copies of the Separation Agreements (in substantially final form) will be made available to LPAC members upon request, subject to applicable confidentiality provisions.

With respect to **accrued carried interest**, as of September 30, 2023, the Fund\'s total accrued (but undistributed) carried interest was approximately **\$87,600,000**. The vested and retained portions of Mr. Kellner\'s and Ms. Trask\'s accrued carried interest will be carved out and preserved in accordance with the terms of their respective Separation Agreements, as described in Section 3.3 above. The redistribution set forth in the table above applies on a **go-forward basis** to carried interest attributable to future appreciation in the Fund\'s portfolio from and after the effective date of the Restructuring. The specific mechanics of the transition and allocation of accrued versus go-forward carry will be set forth in the amended carry allocation provisions of the GP\'s organizational documents and in Amendment No. 1 to the LPA.

The total GP commitment to the Fund is **\$42,000,000**. As a result of the departures of Mr. Kellner and Ms. Trask, their combined unfunded GP commitment of **\$3,402,000** (consisting of \$1,890,000 attributable to Mr. Kellner and \$1,512,000 attributable to Ms. Trask) must be assumed by the remaining principals to ensure that the GP commitment is fully funded through the remainder of the investment period and the balance of the Fund\'s term. The funded portions of Mr. Kellner\'s and Ms. Trask\'s GP commitments will remain in the Fund and will be treated in accordance with their respective Separation Agreements and the LPA.

Section 5.2 of the LPA designates **Marcus Aldridge** and **Priya Narayanan** as \"Key Persons\" of the Fund. Under Section 5.2, a \"Key Person Event\" is triggered if: (a) both Key Persons cease to devote substantially all of their business time and attention to the investment activities of the Fund, or (b) one Key Person ceases to devote substantially all of his or her business time and attention to the investment activities of the Fund and a replacement Key Person is not approved by the LPAC within 120 calendar days of such cessation.

The General Partner confirms that **neither David Kellner nor Joanna Trask is a designated Key Person** under Section 5.2 of the LPA. Accordingly, the departures of Mr. Kellner and Ms. Trask **do not trigger a Key Person Event** under the LPA, and the investment period will continue without suspension or interruption.

Both Marcus Aldridge and Priya Narayanan will continue to serve as Co-Founders and Managing Partners of Ardent Capital and will continue to devote substantially all of their business time and attention to the investment activities of the Fund, consistent with their obligations under the LPA. Neither Mr. Aldridge nor Ms. Narayanan has any present intention to reduce his or her involvement with the Fund or to pursue other business activities that would be inconsistent with the Key Person requirements of Section 5.2.

Additionally, the General Partner has identified that **3 of the 6** side letters containing expanded key-person provisions grant the applicable limited partner a right to request a **90-day suspension** of the investment period pending LPAC review in the event of a Contributing Person\'s departure. The General Partner does not believe that such a suspension is warranted in light of (i) the continued full-time involvement of both designated Key Persons (Aldridge and Narayanan), (ii) the orderly nature of Mr. Kellner\'s planned retirement and transition to a Senior Advisor role, (iii) the depth and continuity of the remaining investment team, and (iv) the ongoing strong performance of the Fund\'s portfolio. The General Partner intends to engage directly and proactively with each of the applicable limited partners to discuss these matters and to address any questions or concerns.

**Co-Investment Priority Rights.** Nine (9) of the 14 side letters contain provisions granting the applicable limited partner co-investment priority rights or preferential co-investment allocation rights. The General Partner intends to update its internal co-investment allocation policy to reflect the revised principal allocations and team responsibilities resulting from the Restructuring. The fundamental co-investment allocation framework --- which is based on commitment size, co-investment track record, and ability to respond to allocation opportunities within the required timeframe --- will remain substantively unchanged. LPAC members with co-investment priority rights will continue to receive advance notice of co-investment opportunities in accordance with their respective side letters.

**Material Change Notification and Consent Provisions.** Four (4) side letters --- those with **Ridgeline Public Employees\' Retirement System**, **Pinnacle Insurance Group**, **Crestwood Endowment Partners**, and **Haverford Capital Partners** --- contain provisions requiring prior written notice and, in certain cases, affirmative consent to any \"material change in the management structure\" of the General Partner, the Management Company, or the Fund\'s investment team. This letter and the LPAC consent process described herein serve as the required notification to the three LPAC members (Ridgeline, Pinnacle, and Crestwood) that hold such provisions. Separate notice will be provided to Haverford Capital Partners in accordance with the specific requirements of its side letter.

A detailed **Side-Letter Compliance and Key-Person Analysis Memorandum** is currently being finalized by Pemberton Hale LLP and Calderwood & Harkness LLP. This memorandum, which will include a provision-by-provision analysis of each side letter and a comprehensive key-person analysis, will be made available to LPAC members upon request. LPAC members who wish to receive a copy of the memorandum should contact Nicholas Stern at Calderwood & Harkness LLP or Victoria Langford at Pemberton Hale LLP.

The General Partner wishes to assure the LPAC that the Restructuring has been designed to ensure continuity and stability in the Fund\'s operations and to minimize any disruption to the Fund\'s investment activities and portfolio management. Specifically, the General Partner confirms that the Restructuring will have **no impact** on the following:

> • **Investment Strategy:** The Fund\'s investment strategy --- control-oriented equity investments in middle-market industrial and business-services companies --- will remain unchanged. The Fund will continue to pursue its stated investment objectives in accordance with the investment guidelines and restrictions set forth in the LPA and the Fund\'s confidential private placement memorandum.

> • **Carried Interest Terms:** The carried interest rate of **20%** of net profits, the **8%** preferred return, the **100%** catch-up, and all other terms of the carried interest waterfall and clawback provisions of the LPA will remain unchanged.
> • **Fund Term:** The term of the Fund will remain as set forth in the LPA, expiring on **December 31, 2029**, subject to two one-year extensions at the discretion of the General Partner.
Pursuant to Section 9.4 of the LPA, the General Partner respectfully requests that each member of the LPAC consent to each of the following actions in connection with the Restructuring:

> 4\. **Amendment No. 1 to the LPA.** The execution and delivery of **Amendment No. 1 to the Amended and Restated Agreement of Limited Partnership** of Ardent Capital Partners III LP, reflecting the structural changes to the General Partner and the Management Company described herein, including updated definitions, representations, and organizational chart references, as necessary to conform the LPA to the post-Restructuring organizational structure.

Consent may be delivered by execution and return of the enclosed **Form of Written Consent** to the attention of Marcus Aldridge or Nicholas Stern at the addresses set forth in Section 11 below, or by affirmative vote at the LPAC meeting scheduled for February 14, 2024. Under Section 9.4(c) of the LPA, the affirmative consent of a majority of the members of the LPAC (i.e., at least three of the four current LPAC members) is required for each of the actions described above.
**[8. LPAC Meeting]{.underline}**

The General Partner proposes to hold a virtual meeting of the LPAC on **February 14, 2024** (the \"**LPAC Meeting**\") to discuss the Restructuring in detail, to respond to questions from LPAC members, and to receive LPAC consent to the actions described in Section 7 above.

Dial-in and videoconference details for the LPAC Meeting will be provided under separate cover no later than February 9, 2024. The General Partner anticipates that the LPAC Meeting will last approximately 90 minutes to two hours.
The following representatives of the General Partner and its counsel will be available to present the enclosed LPAC Presentation Memorandum and to answer questions at the LPAC Meeting:

LPAC members are encouraged to submit any questions or requests for additional information in advance of the LPAC Meeting to facilitate a productive and efficient discussion. Advance questions may be directed to Nicholas Stern or Owen Fischer at the contact information set forth in Section 11 below.
The following materials are enclosed with this letter for the review and consideration of each LPAC member:

> 1\. **LPAC Presentation Memorandum** --- A detailed summary of the Restructuring, including pre- and post-restructuring organizational charts, economics tables, departing principal terms, key-person analysis, and side-letter compliance summary. This memorandum is intended to serve as a comprehensive reference document for LPAC members and will also form the basis of the presentation at the LPAC Meeting.

> 2\. **Form of Written Consent** --- A form of written consent for execution by each LPAC member, consenting to each of the actions described in Section 7 of this letter. LPAC members who wish to deliver their consent in advance of the LPAC Meeting may do so by executing and returning the Form of Written Consent to Marcus Aldridge or Nicholas Stern at the addresses set forth in Section 11 below.

The General Partner reminds each member of the LPAC that the information contained in this letter and the enclosed materials is **confidential and proprietary** to Ardent Capital and its principals. This letter, the enclosed materials, and all information contained herein and therein constitute \"Confidential Information\" within the meaning of Section 11.2 of the LPA and the confidentiality provisions of each LPAC member\'s respective side letter.

The General Partner respectfully requests that each LPAC member treat this letter and all enclosed materials in strict confidence and in accordance with the confidentiality obligations set forth in the LPA and the applicable side letter. This letter and the enclosed materials should not be disclosed, distributed, or made available to any third party (other than the LPAC member\'s own legal, tax, and investment advisors who have a need to know and who are bound by obligations of confidentiality) without the prior written consent of the General Partner.
LPAC members who have questions about the Restructuring or who require additional information are encouraged to contact any of the following individuals:

We appreciate your continued confidence in Ardent Capital and the investment team. The General Partner is committed to managing the Restructuring in a transparent and orderly manner and to ensuring that the interests of the Fund\'s limited partners are fully protected throughout the process. We look forward to discussing the Restructuring with you at the LPAC Meeting on February 14, 2024, and to receiving your consent in connection therewith.

We are pleased to confirm the engagement of Calderwood & Harkness LLP (\"Calderwood & Harkness,\" the \"Firm,\" \"we,\" or \"us\") by Ardent Capital Management LLC (the \"ManCo\" or the \"Client\") to serve as legal counsel in connection with the matters described herein. This letter (the \"Engagement Letter\") sets forth the terms and conditions upon which we will provide legal services to the Client in connection with this engagement.

The engagement encompasses the formation of new holding entities, the negotiation of separation arrangements with departing principals, the realignment of carried interest and management fee economics among continuing and next-generation principals, the solicitation of necessary limited partner consents, compliance with existing side-letter obligations, and related tax structuring. The scope of the representation, the personnel assigned to the engagement, the fee arrangement, and other terms and conditions governing this engagement are set forth in the sections that follow.

The engagement will comprise the following principal workstreams, each of which is described in greater detail below. We understand that the scope of the engagement may evolve as the restructuring progresses; any material expansion of the scope described herein will be discussed with the Client in advance.

\(a\) Advising on the reallocation of carried interest percentages and management fee profit-share allocations among the remaining and next-generation principals, taking into account the departure of the principals described in Section 2.3 below, the contributions of continuing principals, and the Firm\'s understanding of the Client\'s objectives with respect to the incentivization and retention of key personnel.

\(f\) All tax structuring advice under this engagement will be provided by Sylvia Hartwell, Specialist Partner (Tax), who will coordinate as necessary with the Client\'s independent accountants at Heathrow Whitman & Co.

The scope of this engagement is limited to the matters described in Sections 2.1 through 2.5 above. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, the following matters are expressly excluded from the scope of this engagement:

\(b\) Accounting, auditing, and valuation services, which we understand are provided by Heathrow Whitman & Co. (accountants and auditors) and Broadleaf Consulting Group (valuation), respectively. Nothing in this engagement shall be construed as the provision of accounting, auditing, or valuation advice by Calderwood & Harkness.

To the extent matters arise during the course of this engagement that fall outside the scope described herein but that may benefit from our involvement, we will discuss with the Client whether and on what terms such matters should be added to the scope of this engagement or addressed through a separate engagement.
The following attorneys will serve as the primary members of the engagement team:
Nicholas Stern          Responsible Partner        Overall supervision of the engagement, strategic advice, and senior-level involvement in key negotiations and decision points
Graham Sutherland       Billing Partner            Billing, engagement administration, and fee-related communications

Owen Fischer            Lead Associate             Day-to-day management of the engagement, including document drafting and negotiation, coordination with counterparty counsel (Whitford & Chase LLP) and other advisors (Pemberton Hale LLP, Heathrow Whitman & Co., Broadleaf Consulting Group)

From time to time, additional attorneys or paraprofessionals may be assigned to the engagement as the Firm deems necessary or appropriate to ensure efficient and timely completion of the workstreams described herein. The Client will be notified in advance of any such additions to the engagement team.
Fees for services rendered in connection with this engagement will be charged on an hourly basis at the following standard rates:

The foregoing rates are subject to annual adjustment, typically effective January 1 of each year. In the event of any rate adjustment during the term of this engagement, the Firm will communicate such adjustment to the Client in advance. Adjusted rates will apply to services rendered on or after the effective date of the adjustment.

Based on the anticipated scope and complexity of the engagement as described in Section 2 above, and taking into account the number of workstreams, the anticipated volume of document drafting and negotiation, and the extent of LP consent and regulatory compliance work expected to be required, we estimate that total professional fees for this engagement will fall within the range of **\$850,000 to \$1,100,000**.

This estimate is provided solely for budgeting purposes and does not constitute a cap, ceiling, or fixed fee. Actual fees may vary from this estimate based on a number of factors, including (without limitation) the ultimate scope and complexity of the work, the nature and duration of negotiations with Whitford & Chase LLP on behalf of the departing principals, the extent and complexity of LP consent solicitation and side-letter compliance matters, the number and complexity of tax structuring issues that arise, and any expansion of the scope of the engagement beyond the matters described herein. The Firm will endeavor to keep the Client informed on an ongoing basis of any circumstances that are likely to cause total fees to exceed the upper end of the estimated range, and will discuss with the Client any potential modifications to the scope or approach to the engagement that might mitigate such costs.

**4.3 Disbursements.** In addition to professional fees, the Client will be responsible for reimbursement of reasonable out-of-pocket disbursements incurred by the Firm in connection with the engagement. Disbursements may include, without limitation, filing fees (including Delaware Secretary of State filing fees for Certificates of Formation and other filings), messenger and courier charges, travel expenses (including transportation, lodging, and meals incurred in connection with travel reasonably necessary for the engagement), document production and reproduction costs, computerized legal research charges, and similar items. All disbursements will be itemized on the Firm\'s monthly invoices.

Copies of all invoices will also be provided to Marcus Aldridge and Priya Narayanan at the address set forth above, or at such other address or electronic mail address as the Client may designate in writing from time to time. The Client agrees to notify the Firm promptly if there is any question or dispute regarding any invoice, so that any such matter may be addressed in a timely manner.
**[5. Client Identity and Conflicts]{.underline}**

The Client for purposes of this engagement is Ardent Capital Management LLC. Calderwood & Harkness does not represent, and will not be deemed to represent, any individual principal of the Fund (including, without limitation, Marcus Aldridge, Priya Narayanan, or any other continuing principal), any departing principal (including David Kellner and Joanna Trask), any limited partner of the Fund, or any other entity in the Ardent Capital structure (including, without limitation, the Fund, the General Partner, HoldCo, GP Intermediate, or any portfolio company) in their individual or separate capacities. Each such person and entity should consult with its own independent legal counsel with respect to any matter in which its interests may differ from those of the ManCo.

The Firm has conducted a conflict check in accordance with its standard procedures and, as of the date hereof, has identified no conflicts of interest that would preclude this engagement. In the event that a conflict of interest arises during the course of the engagement, the Firm will promptly notify the Client and take appropriate action, which may include seeking an informed written waiver of the conflict from the affected parties or, if a waiver cannot be obtained or is not appropriate under the circumstances, withdrawing from the representation in whole or in part as required by applicable rules of professional conduct.

Calderwood & Harkness will maintain the confidentiality of all information provided by or on behalf of the Client in connection with this engagement, in accordance with the Firm\'s professional obligations and applicable rules of professional conduct. This obligation of confidentiality extends to all non-public information concerning the Fund, the General Partner, the ManCo, HoldCo, GP Intermediate, the principals (whether continuing or departing), the limited partners, the portfolio companies, and any other entities or persons about which information is provided to the Firm in connection with the engagement.

The Firm may disclose confidential information as required by applicable law, regulation, or court order, or with the prior written consent of the Client. In the event the Firm receives a subpoena, court order, or other compulsory process seeking the disclosure of confidential information relating to this engagement, the Firm will, to the extent permitted by law and practicable under the circumstances, provide prompt notice to the Client prior to making any such disclosure, so that the Client may seek protective measures or take other appropriate action.

Calderwood & Harkness will retain engagement files, including correspondence, memoranda, agreements, and other documents generated or received in connection with this engagement, in accordance with the Firm\'s document retention policy, as in effect from time to time. Upon completion or termination of the engagement, the Firm will, at the Client\'s request and expense, return original documents to the Client or make arrangements for the transfer of files. Documents retained by the Firm may be destroyed in accordance with the Firm\'s document retention policy following the expiration of the applicable retention period, unless the Client requests in writing that such documents be returned or otherwise preserved.

Either party may terminate this engagement at any time upon written notice to the other party. In the event of termination by either party, the Client will remain responsible for payment of all professional fees earned and disbursements incurred through the date of termination, in accordance with the billing and payment terms set forth in Section 4 above.

Upon termination, Calderwood & Harkness will take reasonable steps to protect the Client\'s interests, including cooperating in the orderly transition of the matter to successor counsel designated by the Client. The Firm will promptly deliver to the Client or its successor counsel all documents and materials necessary for the continued handling of the matter, subject to the Firm\'s right to retain copies of such documents in accordance with its document retention policy and applicable rules of professional conduct.

We respectfully request that the Client confirm its acceptance of the terms and conditions of this engagement by having each of the undersigned representatives execute and return the enclosed copy of this Engagement Letter to Calderwood & Harkness at the address set forth above, or by transmitting an executed copy by electronic mail to Nicholas Stern at nstern@calderwoodharkness.com or Graham Sutherland at gsutherland@calderwoodharkness.com.

We look forward to working with you and the Ardent Capital team on this important matter. Please do not hesitate to contact either of us if you have any questions regarding the terms of this engagement or if you would like to discuss any aspect of the representation in greater detail.

1396: This AMENDMENT NO. 1 TO THE AMENDED AND RESTATED AGREEMENT OF LIMITED PARTNERSHIP OF ARDENT CAPITAL PARTNERS III LP (this \"Amendment\") is entered into and made effective as of February 28, 2024 (the \"Amendment Effective Date\"), by Ardent Capital GP III LLC, a Delaware limited liability company (the \"General Partner\"), acting in its capacity as the sole general partner of, and on behalf of, Ardent Capital Partners III LP, a Delaware limited partnership (the \"Partnership\" or the \"Fund\").
1397: 
1398: This Amendment amends and supplements that certain Amended and Restated Agreement of Limited Partnership of Ardent Capital Partners III LP, dated as of April 15, 2019 (the date of the Fund\'s final closing) (as in effect immediately prior to this Amendment, the \"Partnership Agreement\" or the \"LPA\").

(the \"DRULPA\"), and this Amendment shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Delaware. Capitalized terms used but not otherwise defined herein shall have the meanings ascribed to such terms in the Partnership Agreement.

1407:

1409: 
1410: **WHEREAS**, Ardent Capital Management LLC, a Delaware limited liability company and registered investment adviser with the United States Securities and Exchange Commission (the \"SEC\") (CRD #298417), serves as the investment adviser and manager of the Fund pursuant to the terms of the Partnership Agreement and a separate Investment Management Agreement dated as of April 15, 2019 (the \"Management Company\");
1411: 
1412: **WHEREAS**, the General Partner has undergone a management company restructuring (the \"Restructuring\"), pursuant to which Ardent Capital Holdings LLC, a newly formed Delaware limited liability company (\"HoldCo\"), has been established as the parent holding company of both (i) the General Partner, through Ardent GP Intermediate LLC, a newly formed Delaware limited liability company (\"GP Intermediate\"), which serves as the sole member of the General Partner, and (ii) the Management Company, which is directly owned by HoldCo;
1413: 
1414: **WHEREAS**, in connection with the Restructuring, David Kellner, a Senior Partner of the General Partner and the Management Company, is retiring from his positions with the General Partner and the Management Company effective March 31, 2024, and Joanna Trask, a Partner of the General Partner and the Management Company, is departing from her positions with the General Partner and the Management Company effective April 15, 2024, and each of David Kellner and Joanna Trask has withdrawn, or has agreed to withdraw, as a member of the General Partner and the Management Company in connection with the Restructuring;
1415: 
1416: **WHEREAS**, in connection with the Restructuring, the ownership structure of the General Partner has been converted from direct ownership by five (5) individual principals --- namely, Marcus Aldridge, Priya Narayanan, David Kellner, Joanna Trask, and Robert Hsiao --- to indirect ownership through the following chain: the HoldCo Members (as defined below) hold membership interests in HoldCo, which is the sole member of GP Intermediate, which in turn is the sole member of the General Partner;
1417: 
1418: **WHEREAS**, the members of HoldCo following the completion of the Restructuring are as follows: Marcus Aldridge (42%), Priya Narayanan (36%), Robert Hsiao (14%), Elena Marchetti (4%), and Samuel Okonkwo (4%) (collectively, the \"HoldCo Members\");
1419: 
1420: **WHEREAS**, Section 9.4 of the Partnership Agreement provides that the consent of the Limited Partner Advisory Committee (the \"LPAC\") shall be required for certain amendments to the Partnership Agreement and for material changes to the management structure of the Fund, including changes in the ownership or control of the General Partner;
1421: 
1422: **WHEREAS**, the LPAC, currently consisting of duly appointed representatives of Ridgeline Public Employees\' Retirement System, Crestwood Endowment Partners, Pinnacle Insurance Group, and Graystone Family Office LLC, has been duly notified of the Restructuring and the proposed amendments to the Partnership Agreement contemplated by this Amendment, and has provided its written consent to this Amendment and the Restructuring at a duly convened meeting of the LPAC held on February 14, 2024, in compliance with the requirements of Section 9.4 of the Partnership Agreement;
1423: 
1424: **WHEREAS**, the General Partner desires to amend the Partnership Agreement to (a) reflect the Restructuring, including the interposition of HoldCo and GP Intermediate in the ownership chain of the General Partner and the Management Company, (b) update certain defined terms to reflect the new organizational structure and the departure of David Kellner and Joanna Trask, (c) amend the GP Commitment provisions to reflect the assumption of departing principals\' unfunded commitments by the remaining and newly admitted principals, and (d) make conforming changes to Section 5.2 (Key Person), Section 8.3 (Transfer of GP Interest), Section 9.4 (LPAC Consent), and related provisions of the Partnership Agreement;
1425: 
1426: **WHEREAS**, the General Partner is authorized to execute this Amendment on behalf of the Partnership pursuant to the terms of Section 9.4 of the Partnership Agreement and has obtained all requisite consents and approvals, including the consent of the LPAC and the written consent of all members of the General Partner prior to the Restructuring;
1427:
